Large outdoor seating area, plus indoor tables. One of the nicer public bathroom in Quy Nhơn (damning with faint praise, but modern clean toilets aren't one of Quy Nhơn's specialties).

listings.name: Marina Cafe
listings.description: Mid-market, modern-style cafe in the southwest corner of the An Phú Thịnh Plaza building.

listings.name: Osaka Cafe
listings.description: Multi-storey cafe in the centre. A two-minute walk east from the airport shuttle bus drop-off. Typical large mid-budget Vietnamese style cafe/restaurant. Nothing to do with Japan other than the name and a painting of Mt. Fuji. Large indoor water-pond display with dozens of small porcelain Buddhas playing under plastic cherry blossoms. Karaoke on upper floors. Big open windows on street. Old but clean toilets.

listings.name: p.u.q. Cafe
listings.description: Hip little cafe in the centre. The decor is a mix between urban industrial and Asian kitsch. Stylish smoothies served in an edible glass made of sweet jelly.

listings.name: Queen Cafe
listings.description: Pleasant two-storey treehouse-cafe a 10-minute walk northwest from the beach.

listings.name: Reform Cafe
listings.price: Espresso 15,000 dong, Irish cafe 20,000, latte 25,000, mocha 28,000, cappuccino 25,000
listings.description: Industrial-style hipster-esque coffee shop. Complete with intricate latte art and baristas wielding tough attitudes, Reform cafe could (almost) be at home in London, Paris or Brooklyn. Small indoor and outdoor space. Smokey. Offers more varieties of coffee drinks than most cafes in Quy Nhơn.

listings.name: Sam Cafe
listings.description: Very large outdoor cafe set rather unusually amidst dozens of bonsai trees which are for sale. At the entrance waits a human-sized statue of a fisher goddess to greet you.

listings.name: Tien Loi Coffee
listings.description: Tiny and sweet cafe a block north of the Long Khánh temple in the northeast of the city centre. Small outdoor seating. Milk tea and coffee served in artsy jars tied off with burlap rope designs. Specialty drink of red and green Thai sweet tea. The upstairs has a no-shoes pillow-seating area surrounded by massive posters illustrating Vietnamese fantasy stories.

listings.name: Violet Cafe
listings.description: Very pleasant, modern cafe. Wood tables and chairs. Has a glass-enclosed non-smoking room with pillow-seating on a sparkling-clean hardwood floor. Drinks only, no food.

listings.name: Style Pub & Bar
listings.description: The biggest nightclub in Quy Nhơn. The only one, as well. Lots of blue and green neon lights. Lots of smoke, both from cigarettes and from smoke machines. Mainly Vietnamese music, loud and with the bass cranked up, but some Western pop mixed in.

listings.name: Anh Khoa Hotel
listings.description: Clean, low-budget hotel in centre of city. The building's four-storey outside features a prominent green and yellow art-deco motif which contrasts with the wood or solid colour patterns more typical of buildings in the area. Only basic English spoken.

listings.name: Anh Vy Hotel
listings.description: Straddling the border between the low- and mid-budget categories, this hotel directly across the street from the beach in the southwest of the city offers rooms which are clean but small and dark. Near Seagull hotel. One of several hotels on the block which cooperate in offering to foreigners semi-scammy tourist services such as plane tickets, car rental, tours, etc. Some English spoken.

listings.name: Au Co Mini 1 Hotel By The Sea Quy Nhon
listings.description: Small low-budget hotel across the road from the city's central waterfront area. Exterior designed like a very narrow German castle. Quirky room decor features lots of floral patterns and garish colours. Rooms not very clean, but adequate for the price. Across the street from Hoàng Yến hotel and a three-minute walk from the up-market Seagull Hotel.

listings.name: Thiên Hải Home
listings.price: Double room: with window 230,000 dong; smaller windowless rooms: 180,000 dong
listings.description: Budget hotel offering reasonable value for price. Old, but well-maintained and clean. Friendly, but almost no English spoken.

listings.name: Phương Mai Hotel
listings.description: Low-budget guesthouse in the southwest of city offering good quality for the price. Quiet nondescript neighbourhood, with a 4-minute walk to beach. 25 minutes by foot to Coopmart. Owner manages several hotels, speaks good English after living five years in San Francisco and very good Japanese after studying medicine in Tokyo for 10 years. Temporarily closed as of Oct 2026.

listings.name: Thiên Các Hotel
listings.description: Most low-budget of three adjacent hotels directly behind (due west) of the Coopmart complex in centre. A 3-minute walk to beach. Reasonably clean. Typical family-operated guesthouse style.

listings.name: Đông Tây Hotel
listings.price: Double room: 300,000 dong at normal times, 500,000 during holidays and high season
listings.description: Mid-budget hotel opened at the end of 2015. Directly opposite the beach and offering many rooms with sea views, it's still close to the city centre. The hotel entrance is flanked by open-air seafood restaurants, and a small night-food market is steps away. The Coopmart is a 5-minute walk to the north. Clean, modern rooms with air conditioning, TV, Wi-Fi. Elevator. Basic English understood.

listings.name: Eden Hotel
listings.price: Double room with breakfast included: 400,000 dong
listings.description: The only mid-budget hotel in the northeast centre of the city. Rooms are small, but comfortable and clean. Six storeys. Elevator. Karaoke in basement, restaurant on top floor. 15-minute walk to Coopmart or the beach. 3-minute walk from the airport shuttle bus drop-off. Street-facing rooms on top floors have impressive panoramic views over the city, sea and mountains. Only basic English spoken.

listings.name: Hoàng Sơn Hotel
listings.description: Standard mid-budget Vietnamese-style family-run hotel. Rooms dark, but clean enough in the southern end of the city centre, a 3-minute walk to the beach and 5 minutes to Coopmart.

listings.name: Sunflowers Hotel
listings.price: Double room: 400,000 without view, 450,000 with view. Management is noteworthy for wanting to fill unoccupied rooms, so when the hotel isn't full, walk-in rates can be much cheaper than online booking
listings.description: Large Vietnamese-style hotel on a small street 20 m (65 ft) off the beach boulevard at the far eastern end of the city. With its 10 storeys towering over the sparsely populated area at the tip of the peninsula, many of the rooms offer unobstructed views in all directions over the bay, the ocean, the city and the mountains. Simple breakfast included. Elevator.

listings.name: Hoàng Yến Hotel
listings.price: Walk-in rates for double room including breakfast buffet: 990,000 dong (city view), 1,150,000 (sea view). Online booking often 20% cheaper than walk-in
listings.description: Large 3-star hotel directly on the beach in the southwest of the city. Outdated decor, Vietnamese upper-mid business-class style. Two intact, African elephant tusks are displayed proudly in the lobby. Nine-storey building with impressive views of the sea, the mountains and the city from top-floor rooms. Outdoor swimming pool, indoor and outdoor restaurants offering both Vietnamese and Western food, large conference rooms, sauna. Elevator. Good English spoken at the reception desk.

listings.name: Khách sạn Sài Gòn – Quy Nhơn
listings.price: Walk-in rates starting at 1,200,000–1,500,000 for a double room. Walk-in rates often slightly cheaper than online bookings
listings.description: Multi-storey four-star hotel across from beach. Soaring lobby. Outdated, impersonal decor. Higher — and more expensive — rooms have wonderful city and beach views. Elevator. Swimming pool, spa, and small gym on top floor. English understood.

listings.name: Seagull Hotel
listings.price: Double room including breakfast: 1,100,000 dong (city view), 1,300,000 (sea view). Online booking price and walk-in rate generally the same
listings.description: Multi-storey hotel on the beach in the southwest of the city. 170 rooms. Dated decor, small rooms, but it's the only four-star hotel in this section of the beach. Many of the rooms offer sea views with balconies. Several restaurants offering both Vietnamese and Western food, rooftop bar, swimming pool, spa, tiny fitness centre, gift shop, travel agency. English spoken. Website offered in Russian, although no staff speak the language.

listings.name: Big Tree Backpackers and Bistro
listings.description: Foreign-run backpackers hostel on the beach in the tiny fishing village of Bãi Xép. Offers three simple but clean dorm rooms: one female-only room with private bathroom and two mixed-gender rooms with shared toilets. Shared shower cubicles are open to the sky. Same management as Haven Guesthouse.

listings.name: Haven Guesthouse
listings.price: Rooms at Haven: 700,000–1,000,000, minimum stay two nights
listings.description: Foreign-run guesthouse on the beach in the tiny fishing village of Bãi Xép. Offers four double rooms and one family room. Restaurant (open to non-guests as well) serves traveller-favourite Western fare and some Vietnamese specialities. Shares the same beach with Life's A Beach Guesthouse, which sits on the opposite side of the one-metre wide alleyway. The luxury Avani Resort lies on the same cove and beach about 100 m (330 ft) to the south, although its end of the beach is private and off-limits to non-guests.

listings.name: Life's a Beach Guesthouse
listings.price: Private house at Life's a Beach for two people: from US$30. Single dorm bed: $7 (budget) and $10 (luxury room with air conditioning)
listings.description: Guesthouse on the beach in the tiny fishing village of Bãi Xép. Run by two Englishmen. Offers bamboo beach houses, beach-view bungalow, treehouse and dorm beds. Shares the same beach with Haven Guesthouse, which is just on the opposite side of the one-metre wide road. Avani Resort is on the same cove and beach about 100 m (330 ft) to the south, although its end of the beach is private and off-limits to non-guests.

listings.name: Avani Quy Nhơn Resort & Spa
listings.price: Standard suite from $180, deluxe suite offering closet and sofa from $230
listings.description: Resort on the private Bai Dai Beach run by the Avani Hotel Group of Thailand. 63 rooms and suites. Restaurants with Western and Vietnamese fare, open-air bar, swimming pool, spa offering massage and facial treatments, yoga pavilion and billiards. Avani shares the same cove and beach as Haven Guesthouse and Life's a Beach Guesthouse 100 m (330 ft) to the north, but the beach is divided and Avani's side is private and off-limits to non-guests.

listings.name: Colonial Palaces
listings.description: The three palaces and summer home of the colonial era, last emperor of Vietnam Bao Dai, which is of great interest once you visit these three heritage sites, named Palace I, II and III, the Dalat Palace Hotel being one of them, with its adjacent Dalat Du Park Hotel, all from the 1920s, together with the Dalat Palace Golf Club, which was built in 1922, to give his majesty the opportunity to practice his golf skills picked up during his years of study in France. The golf course is an awesome site, whether you enjoy the swinging and putting or not, as the coffee shop at the golf course has some…

listings.name: Crazy House
listings.description: A striking, not-quite-finished Gaudi-esque fantasy house designed by the daughter of an independence war hero. Well worth a visit, even if you are not too interested in architecture.

listings.name: Dalat Market
listings.description: Filled with local specialities: strawberry jam, fruit conserves, avocado, artichokes.

listings.name: Flower Garden
listings.description: A set of flower gardens centred around a reconstructed traditional Vietnamese teak wood house. If you go for a stroll around the lake, it can be visited as a stop.

listings.name: Golden Spring Lake
listings.description: Unspoiled scenery.

listings.name: Truc Lam Zen Monastery
listings.price: Bus: 7,000 dong, cable car: 150,000 dong both ways, 120,000 dong one way (Feb 2026)
listings.description: Best to reach it via a cable car ride over the pine forest. Note that both men and women must wear pants and cover their shoulders to enter the monastery.

listings.name: Lake of Sorrow
listings.description: The Lake of Sorrow is a common destination in Dalat. The Lake of Sorrow is so-named because of a tale of two lovers, one who committed suicide after the other was called up to serve in the army.

listings.name: Langbiang Mountain
listings.description: There are 2 peaks: 1915 m and 2167 m. First one is reachable by a steep paved path, you can ride in a Jeep (360,000 dong for 1 Jeep). The second one is 2-3 hours great hike. You don't need to enter the main gate and pay the fee if going to 2167 m peak, trail start on the right of the gate. Also visit the ethnic village at the foot of the mountain.

listings.name: Linh Phuoc Pagoda
listings.description: This kitschy temple is one of a kind in Vietnam. Broken porcelain is used to compose beautiful mosaics that adorn the whole of this 7-level pagoda, and it is still expanding.

listings.name: Nha Tho Domaine de Marie
listings.description: A pink church on top of a hill, with a store selling various dried fruits and snacks from the local orchards run by the nuns of the monastery.

listings.name: Pongour Falls
listings.price: 10,000 dong per person. 5,000 dong per bike
listings.description: It's one of the largest and widest waterfalls in Vietnam and during the wet season is a magnificent sight. A dam built nearby has reduced the water flow. Toilets are pit latrines with no water, soap or tissue, so bring your own.

listings.name: Prenn Falls
listings.description: A very common stop on a typical Dalat tour, Prenn Falls is quite beautiful, but is a lot more fun when you're hiking it than just taking pictures of it.

listings.name: Thien Vien Truc Lam Monastery
listings.price: Free admission. The cable car to the monastery costs 50,000 dong one-way, return 70,000 dong.
listings.description: The monastery has a magnificent view over the dams below and its gardens are full of landscaped shrubs in animal form. Extremely peaceful. A great place to relax and soak in the tranquility. People who do not want to complete the round trip could opt for a 4.1-km walk back to Tran Phu. Be sure to bring a map. On the walk back you can go down to Tuyen Lam Lake, visit nearby Datanla waterfall, and take the bus back to town. A 54-m-tall statue of the goddess of mercy, Guan Yin, was completed in 2019.

listings.name: Tuyen Lam Lake
listings.description: Its clean green waters flow from the beautiful Tia Spring and from the Da Tam River, which flows down from Voi mountain. Its waters stretch over an immense 350 ha and because of its various sources, Tuyen Lam is known as the lake where rivers, springs, and forests meet. The lake was built in the 1980s. It is one of the largest and most beautiful lakes in town. The other side of the lake is Voi Mountain which is a good place for hiking.

listings.name: Valley of Love
listings.description: The Valley of Love is common stop on Dalat tours and is very popular with honeymooners. The Valley of Love is also a great spot for canyoning.

listings.name: Xuan Huong Lake
listings.description: Public lake in the centre. Approximately 5 km in length, this lake was made after two dams on the Camly River were destroyed during a storm in the 1930s. Now, Xuan Huong Lake is one of the main draws of Da Lat, and you can see honeymooners and locals strolling its banks. Many nice hotels have a view of the lake. The lake was drained in 2010, but is now filled again. Boats can be rented on both sides of the lake. The lake is adorned with a blindingly bright advertising sign, aimed directly at the lakeside hotels and coffee shops.

listings.name: Lak Lake
listings.description: Stop on a bike-tour in the central highlands. It's a beautiful ride down to the elephant waterfall through coffee plantations and then up to Lak Lake over a mountain and then through sunny highlands with rice fields. The road is partly very bad, but doable.

listings.name: University of Dalat
listings.description: Students from the Hand-in-Hand Club are eager to serve as free guides.

listings.name: Dalat (Central) Market
listings.description: Dalat's Central Market place is the best place in town to eat fresh fruits and vegetables. Near the entrance, there is a lively and always busy vegetable restaurant that serves excellent soups. A tiny vegetarian food stall is in a corner of the second level.

listings.name: Sữa đậu nành Nguyễn Văn Cừ -Soya Milk Stall
Quán Cơm chay An Lạc Tâm
Vcafe restaurant
listings.description: Popular place for Western travellers. Diverse menu of international dishes and live music every evening.

listings.name: IndiaGate
listings.description: Indian restaurant. Vegan and halal options available.

listings.name: Fungi Chingu Chợ Đêm - Quán nướng Hàn Quốc
listings.description: Korean BBQ

listings.name: Dalat Palace Golf Club
listings.description: Cafe, pro shop and clubhouse, offering Mexican and Western food.

listings.name: Cafe Noi
listings.description: Lovely cafe with relaxed music and great coffee with chocolate flavour. Lots of young locals playing cards and board games here. Not yet spoiled by masses of tourists.

listings.name: Cafe Tung'
listings.description: Really nice cafe. The delicious Vietnamese coffee costs 8,000 dong and is served with tea.

listings.name: Hangout Bar
listings.description: Classic backpacker bar. Free pool table, board games, and darts. Guests can choose their music. Good place to meet other travellers and expats.

listings.name: Larry's Bar
listings.description: Library-style decorations with dark wood paneling, pool table, and darts.

listings.name: Saigon Taste
listings.description: A small cocktail bar

listings.name: The Escape Bar
listings.description: Live music every night, cosy and friendly bar.

listings.name: 100 Roofs Cafe
listings.description: The main attraction here is the building, which is a themed maze of indoor caves, tunnels, staircases, alcoves, ladders, a rooftop garden and everything in between, while built-in bar tables and chairs are plentifully scattered all around. Definitely not the place to get drunk (unless you sit at the 1st or 2nd floor). Definitely a unique, must-see experience in the city.

listings.name: Bon Mua Guesthouse
listings.description: Clean, basic guesthouse.

listings.name: Dalat Hotel
listings.description: Clean rooms, friendly staff and big breakfast. They also have sauna, steam, and hot tub free of charge for guests (16:00-19:00).

listings.name: Hang Nga Guest House
listings.description: Friendly staff, clean rooms, good English spoken.

listings.name: Mooka's Home
listings.price: Dorm beds from 150,000 dong, private rooms from 350,000 dong
listings.description: Small backpacker hostel with capsule-style dorm beds (privacy curtain, reading light, charging port, locker) and private rooms. Breakfast costs extra. The desk can arrange local tours such as canyoning and Easy Rider motorbike trips, and bus tickets.

listings.name: Mr. Peace backpacker's house
listings.description: Friendly, cosy, clean, good atmosphere, centrally located, excellent English speaking, crazy, may have family dinner with you. Good price.

listings.name: Hoa Binh 1 Hotel
listings.description: It is anything but peaceful, and fills to capacity on weekends, but staff are friendly. There is a cafe next door.

listings.name: Mai Tam Guesthouse
listings.description: Clean family-run guesthouse a little outside city centre in a Vietnamese residential area (about 1½-km, 20-min walk). The family rents out scooters for USD5/day. They also have a convenience shop downstairs.

listings.name: Nam Ky Hotel
listings.description: Nice view from the rooms.

listings.name: Ngoc My Hotel
listings.description: Nice location with Xuan Huong Lake view and clean rooms, balconies facing the lake.

listings.name: Peace Hotel
listings.description: Free Wi-Fi, breakfast extra for USD1.

listings.name: Sakura Hotel
listings.description: Cheap hotel near the student centre.

listings.name: Les Sapins 60 Hotel
listings.description: Renovated, clean rooms, free Wi-Fi and Internet in the lobby, breakfast for USD1 available.

listings.name: Thanh Huong Hotel
listings.description: Includes cable TV, Wi-Fi and fridge. Some rooms have balconies.

listings.name: Van Anh Hotel
listings.description: The staff speak good English, rooms are clean with cable TV, free Wi-Fi. Very motorcycle-friendly.

listings.name: Villa Vista Dalat
listings.description: This is a new villa, with breathtaking views from all rooms, food, great coffee, tours, transportation options, live music and personal service.

listings.name: Pine Hill Homestay Dalat
listings.description: Home on top of the hill overlooking the city. 3 min from King's summer palace, 10 min walk from crazy house. With kitchen.

listings.name: N.T hostel
listings.description: In the heart of the city, Super comfortable beds, friendly staff, in the city center.

listings.name: Ana Mandara Villas
listings.description: 65 rooms within 17 refurbished French colonial villas. A bit far from the city centre and only recommended to those who like to walk, what with large distances between the accommodations and the other services of the resort. Charming and for the adventurous. Must like sharing living rooms and other services, as each villa houses several rooms, hence the sharing issue.

listings.name: Dalat Du Parc Heritage Boutique Hotel
listings.description: Hotel built in 1922, part of the original Dalat Palace compound, with 143 rooms and one ambassador suite. Style and glory of yesteryear, a very old fashioned lift and great views from the rooms at the back of the hotel.

listings.name: Dalat Edensee Lake Resort & Spa
listings.description: Mountain and garden view, Eden suite, all equipped with 32-inch LCD TV, king bed and minibar. Free Wi-Fi. Nam Xuan, Eden Lake Café, and Riesling restaurants within the compound.

listings.name: The Dalat Palace Heritage
listings.description: 43 luxury rooms and suites, one presidential suite. Built in the art deco-style of the 1920s with imperial dining rooms and facilities. It has beautiful gardens. It was conceived as the very centre of the city and dominates with great views onto the Xuan Huong Lake. It also has an 18-hole golf course, tennis courts, and spa.

listings.name: Binh An village
listings.description: Good place to sleep, great view, but far from the city

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh Museum
listings.description: Contains photos and information on Ho Chi Minh, and the history of Hue in photographs.

listings.name: Phu Bai Airport
listings.description: A must-see if you are interested in the earlier conflicts, back when the airport was a dirt strip. During the Vietnam War, an American garrison was assigned there and built up the airport with concrete bunkers, a paved airstrip and a few other luxuries. The airport was vital in keeping Hue supplied during the Easter Offensive of 1972 when "Charlie jumped the line". The airport retains the original buildings built by the Americans; however, they have been retrofitted for use by the Vietnamese.

listings.name: Thien Mu Pagoda
listings.description: Perched on a bluff over the river and housing some very fine gold and silver Buddha images. The Thien Mu Pagoda overlooks the Perfume River and is the official symbol of the city of Hue. Thien Mu means "elderly celestial woman", and refers to an old legend about the founding of the pagoda. Brimming with opportunities for great photos. And don't forget the historical Austin (car) of Thích Quảng Đức!

listings.name: Imperial City of Hue
listings.description: The former imperial seat of government and Hue's prime attraction, this is a great sprawling complex of temples, pavilions, moats, walls, gates, shops, museums and galleries, featuring art and costumes from various periods of Vietnamese history. Thanks to its size, it is also delightfully peaceful, a rare commodity in Vietnam. The citadel was badly knocked about during fighting between the French and the Viet Minh in 1947, and again in 1968 during the Tet Offensive, when it was shelled by the Viet Cong and then bombed by the Americans. As a result, some areas are now only empty fields, bits…

listings.name: Huế Museum of Royal Fine Arts
Tomb of Gia Long
listings.description: The most remote of the tombs, quiet and fallen into disrepair as Gia Long, the first Nguyen emperor, was notoriously despotic.

listings.name: Tomb of Minh Mang
listings.description: In this opulent complex, the main buildings are arranged on an east-west axis, including a courtyard surrounded by warrior statues and several temples and pavilions. Several bridges cross two lakes before the axis ends before the vast burial mound (which is circled by a fence). The mausoleum features large gardens and lakes: a pleasant place to sit and relax. If you're dropped off by boat note that there is a stretch of souvenir sellers to navigate during the short walk to the mausoleum entrance.

listings.name: Tomb of Thieu Tri
listings.description: Built in 1848. This emperor and his wife were the most revered and loved throughout the country. Although he only ruled for 7 years, he was the most sorely missed. In a time of strife and economic problems, he was careful with the country's treasury and improved his people's living standard. His last wish was to be placed in a tomb that was not extravagant, parting ways with the tradition of creating lavish final resting places for emperors.

listings.name: Tomb of Tu Duc
listings.description: Built between 1864–1867, the complex served as a second Imperial City where the emperor went for "working vacations". Tu Duc's contemplative nature and poetic spirit is reflected in the landscape and arrangement of the 50 buildings that at one time stood here. A vast, sprawling complex set around a lake, with wooden pavilions and tombs and temples dedicated to wives and favoured courtesans (Tu Duc had 104 to choose from). The courtesans' quarters are in ruins, with only outlines and crumbling walls left amid waves of overgrown grass and silence, but other areas are stunningly well-preserved.…

listings.name: Tomb of Dong Khanh
listings.description: Built in 1917. Beautiful interior murals. The tomb area is a colorful construction of marble and ceramics. The 100 or so stairs may be an issue for people with mobility difficulties.

listings.name: Tomb of Khai Dinh
listings.description: Dating from 1925, this is the best preserved of the lot and, while comparatively compact, quite grand at first sight. While it follows the classic formula of forecourts leading up to the tomb of the emperor, complete with statues in attendance, architecture buffs will spot some European influences. The tomb itself is completely over the top with incredibly detailed and opulent mosaics of cavorting dragons. Try to get to this one early, as it is a favourite stop for Asian tour-bus groups. Also, you may want to leave the tourist path and head up the hill on the right side of the tomb, where a…

listings.name: Blind Massage
listings.price: 40,000 dong/hr for massage and 30,000 dong/hr for steam-bath
listings.description: At the institute for the blind. All of the staff work and live in this facility and speak a little English. Popular with the locals.

listings.name: My An Hot Spring and Spa
listings.price: US$3 for foreigners to use the swimming pool and 2 hot spring pools
listings.description: The water here has a high sulphur content, purported to have health benefits.

listings.name: Thanh Tan Hot Springs
listings.description: Similar to My An, but without the odour of sulphur. This site is surrounded by woods, which are pleasant to explore. Has graduated sections. Start with the cool section and work your way up. The hottest section is closed off, as it is too hot to bathe in. There are also private pools for 2 or 4 people and a swimming pool. There is a tiny restaurant on site. This is also where the local bottled Thanh Tan mineral water comes from.

listings.name: Banh Bao
listings.description: A street vendor who sells wonderful Banh Bao.

listings.name: Quán Chay Thanh Liễu
listings.description: Totally vegan. You eat with the locals. Great food. The hot pot is fantastic and can be had for 50,000 dong (June 2017). The portions are huge. Great atmosphere. The staff is lovely.

listings.name: Cafe on Thu Wheels
listings.description: Traveler restaurant, with many simple, delicious dishes. There is even white and red wine. Very pleasant family business. The landlady runs the restaurant by heart.

listings.name: Family Home Restaurant
listings.description: It is small and looks like grandma's living room. It's cute. The Hue dishes are just tasty, spicy and great. It is not Westernized food. The staff is very friendly and helpful.

listings.name: Nina's Cafe Restaurant
listings.description: Restaurant tucked away in a back alley that apparently caters to foreigners. English menus and the friendly staff speaks English. A nice little simple restaurant. Good music and atmosphere.

listings.name: Lien Hoa
listings.description: Monks and nuns frequent this vegetarian restaurant during lunch.

listings.name: Cơm Chay Diệu Lạc
listings.description: Simple and good vegetarian meals.

listings.name: Banh Khoai Hong Mai
listings.address: 110 Dinh Tien Hoang – Nguyen Bieu corner
listings.description: Pancakes, nem lui (minced pork grilled with lemon grass on coal) and banh beo recommended.

listings.name: Quán Cơm Chay - Nhật Lệ
listings.description: Popular vegetarian restaurant. You only need to let the owner know if you want a rice or noodles dish and she would do the magic for you. The soy milk and lotus seed milk are also very refreshing. Delicious grilled vermicelli.

listings.name: Đường bánh canh Hàn Thuyên
listings.description: The food is good, sold until late at night so everyone can eat comfortably. 15,000-20,000 dong for a bowl (April 2022). Sitting on the roadside is cool.

listings.name: Hông Thùy
listings.description: Honestly one of the best places to eat in all of Vietnam. It's great street sea food, you choose the type of snail that will be served to you with noodles and vegetables, and a side dish of roasted shrimps / shells / langostinos depending on your choice (30.000 - 60.000 dong depending on which one you choose). Chosen by locals and no English spoken, so you'll probably have to use a translation app, but strongly recommended. Try to go early because they can run out of food (happened at 20.15).

listings.name: Hanh Pancake
listings.price: Ban khoai, 20,000-25,000 dong; nem lui, 80,000 dong, bánh bèo 60,000 dong (Jan 2018)
listings.description: This is a family restaurant where locals come to eat Hue specialities. About half of the guests are Western tourists these days, and a set sampler menu is available.

listings.name: La Carambole
listings.description: Serves French food, Vietnamese food and pizza. Quite touristy.

listings.name: Hot Tuna
listings.description: Recommend the chicken breast with mushroom sauce and mashed potatoes well worth it. Duck also quite nice.

listings.name: Ta.ke Japanese Restaurant
listings.description: Excellent food.

listings.name: Ong Tao
listings.description: Excellent traditional Hue food, try the meat rolls (wrapped in mint leaves) or the fried spring rolls. Incredibly crunchy. Not too crowded. On the first floor. All dishes available as small and big portions, so you can order a few.

listings.name: Ancient Hue Royal Cuisine and Gallery
listings.description: One of the biggest restaurants in the city. Prices are good, food is excellent, extremely clean. It is also a complex of ancient houses among a huge garden area. Nice food carvings.

listings.name: B4 Bar-Café
listings.description: A charming Belgian-Vietnamese owned bar, with a welcoming interior and free pool.

listings.name: Brown Eyes Chillout Bar-Club
listings.description: Live DJ, free pool table and a good vibe. Not far from Pham Ngu Lao, but they offer to pay for taxis from hotels for parties of four persons or more. Stays open till the last one passes out.

listings.name: Café on Thu Wheels
listings.description: It's a little bar owned by the charming lady Thu.

listings.name: Sinh To Place
listings.price: Rau má (centella asiatica juice) 6,000 dong, smoothies (sinh to) 8,000 dong
listings.description: Shop for drinking ice tea, coffee, smoothies and juices. Local prices (they are published on a board). Try rau má juice: reputed to be very good for your health.

listings.name: Vy Da Xua
listings.description: Enjoy a delicious cup of Vietnamese coffee, or any beverage, in this beautiful setting. The traditional beam house is surrounded by a garden and small stream where you can hear birds and restful music.

listings.name: Garden river Bar coffee
listings.description: Bar coffee in the center of hue You can enjoy your drink and listen music near to the river inside the amazing garden. A Vietnamese and French team will be here to helping you.

listings.name: La Beaute
listings.description: Lovely cafe on a quiet side street and therefore still unspotted by the LP crowd. Atmosphere with soft music and green bamboo around and half the prices than in the tourist area 200 m around the block. Lots of different coffees and cakes, where especially the very recommendable coffee with cacao flavour is not easy to find in Hue.

listings.name: Sidewalk Coffee
listings.description: Go local and try some delicious early morning coffee with chocolaty overtones, hot or iced, while watching river life on the canal. The woman who brews it up also offers banh mi, French bread with your choice of fillings. Another woman shares the same area of pavement and sells very reasonably priced banh canh, a popular local breakfast soup. Very clean. After your coffee, you walk along Bach Dang to two nearby pagodas.

listings.name: Amigo Hotel
listings.description: Tucked away in the heart of the guesthouse/cheaper district. Friendly staff, good rooms and rates are negotiable. Free Wi-Fi and PCs available for guest use. Air-con. Satellite TV. Laundry service at 20,000 dong per kilo. Restaurant downstairs serves good food and very reasonably priced.

listings.name: Hue Amazing Homestay
listings.description: Nice and helpful staff, free wifi, free breakfast, 24 hr front desk.

listings.name: Bamboo Hotel
listings.description: Good hotel. The staff are friendly, the rooms are clean and neat. Free Internet.

listings.name: Binh Duong I Hotel
listings.price: From US$10. Dorms are US$4 (84,000 dong)
listings.description: Air-con, hot water & satellite TV included. Popular with Japanese tourists. Friendly and helpful staff. Some rooms have bathtubs and/or private balcony.

listings.name: Canary Hotel
listings.description: All rooms are air conditioned, all equipped with 32-inch LCD cable TV, shower with bath and minibar. Bar and restaurant, Internet room, boutique and souvenir shop and laundry service.

listings.name: Halo
listings.description: Spotless rooms, spacious, with large bathrooms and TV. There is a balcony to sit on at night, and it's close to all the nightlife in Hue.

listings.name: Vietnam Backpacker Hostels - Hue Hostel & Sports Bar
listings.description: Same owners as the popular Hanoi Backpacker's Hostel. Hue Backpacker's is the newest addition to Chu Van An (as of May, 2018. Cheap accommodation, very clean, spacious balconies. Free Internet, Free Wi-Fi and friendly & helpful staff. The downstairs area is also a bar and restaurant serving burgers and other Western food. Bike rentals, tours, cooking classes.

listings.name: Lam Bao Long Hotel
listings.description: Has 15 non-smoking rooms, air conditioning, bathrobes, daily newspaper, desk, hair dryer.

listings.name: Mimosa Guesthouse
listings.description: Friendly, quiet location in a backpacker hotel alley off Le Loi.

listings.name: Minh Hieu Hotel
listings.description: Family-run hotel named after the wild urchin who'll make his displeasure known if you spend too long on the Internet-ready computer downstairs, thereby keeping him from online puzzle games. The rooms are spotlessly clean, with satellite TV, hot water and mini-fridges; each floor has a balcony, and it's not too loud outside. Breakfast costs US$1.

listings.name: Phong Lan
listings.description: Very nice, clean hotel on a small, calm side street near Pham Ngu Lao. All rooms have balcony, air-con, private bath. Rooms for 2 to 4 persons. Free Wi-Fi, bicycle and motorbike rental available. Staff are friendly and speaks good English.

listings.name: Sports Hotel
listings.description: Nice cheap hotel located on the main tourist hangout. Clean and big spacious rooms and not far from the river.

listings.name: Homeland Hotel
listings.description: Boutique hotel near Perfume River. All rooms have wooden floors and are equipped with IDD telephone, air conditioning, cable TV, refrigerator, bath, (bath and shower), hair dryer, coffee and tea making facilities, private computer with ADSL.

listings.name: Carnosa Hotel Hue
listings.description: Replaced Tigon Hostel, has wifi, a/c, breakfast buffet, restaurant/bar, and spa.

listings.name: Asia Hotel
listings.description: The rooms are well equipped and the rooftop restaurant and pool have nice views. Rooms from a slightly overpriced US$30, including a decent buffet breakfast.

listings.name: Holiday (Diamond) Hotel
listings.description: Exceptionally good value. The spotless, air conditioned rooms are well-furnished with modern amenities and include lockable wardrobes. The included breakfast is substantial. The staff are very attentive, and will learn your name. They will warmly welcome you back after each foray outside, and provide you with free drinks (lemon juice, corn water) every time you enter and whenever you sit in the lobby.

listings.name: Jade Hotel
listings.description: Has the same owner as Holiday Hotel, but simpler rooms. Pickup from train station included, if booked in advance.

listings.name: Hanh Dat Hotel
listings.description: Rooms with air conditioning, Wi-Fi and 32-inch LCD TV with satellite/ cable channels. Restaurant, business centre, fax and photocopying services.

listings.name: New Star Hotel
listings.description: Hotel offering 56 air-conditioned rooms, all of which have a cable television, an Internet connection and a minibar. Amenities include massage and sauna, an outdoor swimming pool and a souvenir shop.

listings.name: Orchid Hotel
listings.price: US$35, including a decent buffet breakfast
listings.description: Professional and personable staff. Clean, spacious and beautifully designed rooms. Free pickup from train.

listings.name: Park View Hotel Hue
listings.description: In the center of the city, near the Perfume River. It's a 10-min walk to Hue Citadel.

listings.name: La Residence
listings.description: Renovated, it tries to bring to life the French colonial era of the 1920s. It has the largest swimming pool and spa in Hue.

listings.name: Saigon Morin
listings.description: Hue's grand old hotel which has been open for over a hundred years. Excellent riverside location, whitewashed colonial charm and a pleasant inner courtyard, although the rooms could use a little fine-tuning.

listings.name: Sao Beach
listings.description: The prettiest beach on the island, with a restaurant/cafe and beach lounging.

listings.name: Ong Lang Beach
listings.description: Beautiful beach to watch the sunset. Most of it is managed and cleaned by some resorts, but you can lie on the sand with your towel no questions asked, or go to the partially rocky part on the north end, away from the resorts.

listings.name: Phu Quoc Prison History Museum
listings.description: Historical prison built by French and used during Vietnam War for POW.

listings.name: Sunworld Hon Thom Water Park
listings.description: A modern water theme park (opened in 2019) with massive water slides, swimming pools restaurants, and a beach offer snorkeling and scuba diving. A free buggy takes you from the cable car to the beach (turn right after you exit the cable car).

listings.name: Jerry's Jungle Tours
listings.description: Archipelago explorations by boat, snorkelling, fishing, day and multiday trips to islands, motorbike tours, bouldering, bird-watching, hiking and cultural tours around Phu Quoc.

listings.name: Flipper Diving Club
listings.price: Fun Dives US$65, for non-certified divers starting from USD85, PADI & SSI courses starting from US$300
listings.description: The only dive company on Phú Quôc that is a PADI resort and also a SSI center. Staffed by instructors from both organizations, they can provide training from beginner level to all the way up to divemaster. They are also environmentally aware and organize clean up days, actively try to raise awareness of divers and enforce a "no-touch" policy while diving.

listings.name: John's tour
listings.description: Snorkelling.

listings.name: Phú Quôc Explorer
listings.description: Snorkelling.

listings.name: Vietnam explorers
listings.address: DT 47 Group 2, Suoi May Hamet, Duong To Commune, Phu Quoc
listings.description: Formerly Rainbow Divers (as evidenced by the inherited marketing text and the recommendation by Rainbow Divers Nha Trang). The longest established dive centre on Phú Quôc. PADI-courses, snorkelling and diving are available in most European languages and in Vietnamese. Friendly staff and great and safe trips.

listings.name: Sunny Boat Trip
listings.description: Snorkeling.

listings.name: X-Dive
listings.description: Operates dives to the north and south of the island depending upon the conditions. They do not offer PADI courses.

listings.name: Phú Quôc Island Tours
listings.address: 1 Tran Hung Dao Street (near the Salinda Resort)
listings.description: English & Vietnamese tour guides taking you to the island hotspots by land and sea. Services include camping, kayak+camping, and National Park trekking.

listings.name: The Dog Bar
listings.address: 88 Tran Hung Dao, Dương Đông town
listings.description: Serves good burgers and pizzas, as well as a range of Western, Vietnamese, and seafood dishes. Watch live sports, play pool, or darts, or just listen to live music. You can book dive and snorkelling trips there with Rainbow Divers and Anh Tu. They have cold beer, mixed drinks and cocktails and a friendly English-speaking staff.

listings.name: Ganesh Indian Restaurant
listings.address: 97 Tran Hung Dao, Dương Đông town
listings.description: The food is OK, but not quite up to the standards you can experience in countries like the UK or Australia.

listings.name: Gio Bien Restaurant
listings.description: Offers a great selection of fresh seafood dishes and Vietnamese dishes. The beach is beautiful and metres away from your table. The caramelised fish hotpot for lunch or dinner is a treat.

listings.name: Night Market
listings.address: Võ Thị Sáu, Dương Đông town
listings.description: From 18:00 there are lots of small restaurants open on the street of the night market. It's the place to go for seafood.

listings.name: Ocean Bar and Grill
listings.description: Excellent service and food. The seafood is fresh and cooked to order and the staff are highly trained and attentive. Michelle, the owner, speaks to every customer about their meal and keeps a photo and book of comments from all patrons.

listings.name: Rory's Beach Bar
listings.description: As you walk past on the beach the Aussie owner, Rory, will tempt you with promises of ice cold beer ("Too cold to hold!") using his loud hailer. He delivers, with two draught beers on tap. There's plenty of room to sit and relax on the deck, around the bar or on the beach-front. Prices are mid-range with draught beer around 35,000 dong, cocktails hovering around 100,000 dong and meals averaging 120,000 dong.

listings.name: The Rabbit Hole Irish Sports Bar
listings.address: 118/2/1 Đường Trần Hưng Đạo, Khu Phố 7
listings.description: English-speaking staff, outdoor seating, air-conditioned indoors and free wifi. Western and Vietnamese specialties. A selection of big screens showing sports, pool table, a Professional UK darts board, regular poker games, a NES Classic with 30 classic games, Jenga, and Connect 4. Also serving Guinness, Magners’ Cider and many more Western and local beers, fine whiskeys and signature cocktails.

listings.name: Amigos Guest house
listings.description: Immaculate bungalows with hot/cold water, air-con, fridge, satellite TV, queen bed in each. On the beach and it has Amigos Restaurant and bar. Free Internet and weekly promotions ongoing. There is a children’s play area.

listings.name: Bamboo Cottages
listings.description: 15 concrete "cottages" with direct or partial sea views, and four wood houses built in the old Phu Quoc fisherman style. All the rooms are close to their private beach. They use solar panels and are surrounded by gardens and trees. Restaurant serves organic food and lots of vegan options (40,000-140,000 dong). Kayaking and snorkeling for free, motorbikes for rent.

listings.name: Cassia Cottage
listings.description: Cassia has seaview and garden cottages.

listings.name: Chez Carole
listings.description: Resort with one dozen bungalows, in a pretty remote location on the coast at the mouth of the Cua Can River, about 15 km north of Dương Đông and the airport. Access partly on slow, unpaved roads. There is a swimming pool, restaurant, bar, gardens. There is no beach, but small sandy islands at the mouth of the river are a short swim or boat ride away. Kayaking and canoeing. Good for a quiet short holiday, without no crowds nearby.

listings.name: Eden Resort
listings.description: The spacious guest rooms feature a contemporary design, with a largish bed, flat 32" TV (lots of channels, but most with quite poor picture quality), side table/desk, 2 armchairs, minibar/fridge, air conditioning and a balcony. The bathroom has a bathtub. The main building has elevators, which are nice if your room is on the 3rd floor. The resort is along a sandy beach and ocean, with a restaurant poolside and a small bar. There is free Wi-Fi, and a small gym. The site has nice smallish gardens. The beach south of the resort is undeveloped (there are a couple unfinished older buildings a…

listings.name: Lang Toi
listings.description: There are only two hostels on the most beautiful beach, Sao Beach, and this one offers air conditioning and hot showers. On a full-moon evening you can watch the moon rise from the sea as Sao Beach is on the east side of the island.

listings.name: Little Garden Bungalow
listings.description: Just south of Dương Đông town, the hotel has bungalows placed around its pool garden. There are trees all around ensuring shade all day long. Close to restaurants and Dương Đông town, some 500 m to the beach. Rooms have air conditioning and Wi-Fi. 26 rooms.

listings.name: Mai House
listings.price: USD50 low season, USD90 high season.
listings.description: Fourteen stylish, high quality thatched villas dotted around gardens on the beach, fully equipped with sun loungers. There's no fridge in the villas and no pool, but air-con, safe, tea/coffee maker, beach towel furnished, free Wi-Fi in lobby and restaurant. The restaurant menu is good. Breakfast included.

listings.name: Mango Bay Resort
listings.description: A peaceful resort between the sea on one side and a forest preserve on the other. The resort beaches are small, but the adjoining beach is as yet undeveloped for tourism and features a decent reef for snorkelling. This is a low-key resort, where the lawns are mowed by a herd of cows with wooden cowbells, and the spa opens directly onto the lawn running down the sea. Bungalows are set back from the sea and separated from each other. There is a vegetable and spice garden on the property, and much of the food served is grown there. There are several styles of bungalows, each with its own…

listings.name: Paris Beach Resort
listings.address: Cau Ba Phong, Cua lap, Duong To
listings.description: Nice staff, very friendly owners, and one of the cheaper resorts. Owned and run by a French/Vietnamese couple, both professors, who enjoy running a hotel and having guests. Food is great and prices all rather reasonable. If there is no room at Paris Beach, try Beach Club Resort right next door and vice versa.

listings.name: Peppercorn Beach
listings.address: To 8, Ap Chuong Vich, Ganh Dau
listings.description: On the quiet northern shores of Phu Quoc, Peppercorn has eight spacious air conditioned luxury bungalows sitting just metres from the beach. All bungalows have terrific views of the Cambodian and the Vietnamese mainland in the distance.

listings.name: Saigon Tourist Phu Quoc Resort
listings.description: The oldest large hotel on the island, close to the center of Dương Đông and most of the tourist restaurants.

listings.name: La Veranda
listings.description: 43 rooms and villas spread around a pool and French-style colonial building.

listings.name: Viet Thanh Bungalow
listings.description: Mosquito nets, hot showers. Free Wi-Fi (only front bungalows).

listings.name: Salinda Resort and Spa
listings.address: Cua Lap Hamlet, Duong To Commune
listings.description: 121 deluxe rooms, villas and a presidential suite, all with contemporary architecture.

listings.name: Dray Nur waterfall
listings.description: Impressive waterfalls and recreation area, especially recommended in wet season.

listings.name: Đray Sáp waterfall
listings.description: Another waterfall, about 300 m from Đray Nur. Looks less impressive in dry season, but still interesting area to explore.

listings.name: Eatu Café
listings.address: 22 KT Street, Ko Tam village, Eatu commune
listings.description: Fair trade coffee cooperative and manufacturer, funded by the European Union. Open for visits.

listings.name: Lady Jiangshan
listings.description: Breathtaking views from the hill top and halfway to the top. Well worth a visit on the way to Lak Lake.

listings.name: Lak Lake
listings.description: The mother lake of the Central Highlands.

listings.name: Trung Nguyên flagship restaurant
listings.description: Coffee, drinks and food available, nice gardens with a lot of coffee trees, artificial cave and pond. Coffee can also be bought here, beans or ground.

listings.name: Mehyco cafe
listings.description: Another cafe with a nice garden, belonging to a coffee manufacturing company.

listings.name: Ngoc Mai Guesthouse
listings.description: Great guesthouse/small hotel at the heart of the city. 200 m from the night market, plenty of restaurants around. Rooms with air-con, TV. Friendly staff speaking English and French. Indoor parking for motorbikes

listings.name: Thanh Ngoc
listings.description: Great little hotel, for 150,000 dong, inclusive air-con, TV and incredibly friendly and helpful owners. Indoor parking for motorbikes, too.

listings.name: Huong Khue
listings.description: Simple but clean. There are several other hotels on the same road. Rooms from 120,000 dong. Staff is helpful and friendly but knowledge of English is limited. You can take local buses to the center or walk for about 20 minutes.

listings.name: Tu Hung
listings.description: Good sized rooms. Clean bed and washroom. Allows parking (motorbike) inside the hotel.

listings.name: Coconut Candy Factory
listings.description: There are more factories around, e.g. Thanh Thanh Coconut Candies, 5km to the SE. You might get a chance to see women making the handmade candy.

listings.name: Explore the Delta
listings.description: Boat trips are one of the nicest ways to negotiate the network of channels, but the land in between the waters is just as fascinating. It's fun to follow some of the small trails along the channels, crossing streams on very basic bridges and walking past fruit and coconut orchards.

listings.name: Ninh Kiều quán
listings.description: Big seafood restaurant right at the beginning of town. Very popular with Vietnamese office workers and families.

listings.name: Hai Long Hotel
listings.address: 500a2 Nguyen Thi Dinh Street, Phu Tan Ward
listings.description: 20 rooms.

listings.name: Ham Luong Hotel
listings.address: Số 200 C, Đường Hùng Vương, P.5, TP
listings.description: One of the best hotels in Ben Tre with outside swimming pool, steam bath and sauna. Buffet breakfast is a mix of Asian and Western food. All rooms have Internet, TV with English channels. Laundry, fitness gym, karaoke, massage, jacuzzi, car rental, boat, bicycle, information service.

listings.name: Khach San Dong Khoi
listings.price: 150,000-240,000 dong. Strangely prices dropped if check-in after 16:00
listings.description: Hot water except in cheapest rooms. Free Wi-Fi, restaurant, karaoke, massage.

listings.name: Khach San Phuong Hoang
listings.description: Cold shower. Fan or air-con. Free Wi-Fi. Limited English-speaking staff.

listings.name: Nha Nghi 99
listings.description: Air-con, no Wi-Fi, limited English-speaking staff.

listings.name: Que Huong
listings.description: Good service, limited English and friendly. All rooms with hot shower and fresh towel.

listings.name: Khuổi Ky Stone Village
listings.description: A traditional Tày village known for its old stone stilt houses and yin-yang tiled roofs. Located near the Ban Gioc–Nguom Ngao area, it offers a quieter cultural stop between Cao Bằng's major natural sights. Some local households provide homestay accommodation.

listings.name: Thang Hen Lake
listings.description: Surrounded by mountains, this serene lake is at its best in the rainy season. During the dry season the lake shrinks and is not as impressive, but there are a few rafts that you can take. Walking in the nearby mountains brings you past local herders and farmers. There are no buses to Thang Hen, so the cheapest option is to hire a motorbike driver for the half-day trip. It's about 1 hour away and try to negotiate a round-trip price of 125,000 dong. No entrance fee.

listings.name: Ban Gioc Waterfall
listings.description: This breathtaking waterfall, the largest in Vietnam, straddles the China-Vietnam border. The water is particularly thunderous in the wet season but is still beautiful during the dry. You can take a raft out into the river to the base of the falls and greet Chinese tourists doing the same from the other side. Ban Gioc is about 90 km from Cao Bằng, about 2 hours away. The cheapest way to get there is to take a public minibus to Trung Khanh for around 70,000 dong. Once in Trung Khanh, the minibus driver may offer to take you the rest of the way to Ban Gioc Falls for an extra 150,000 dong, which…

listings.name: Nguom Ngao Cave
listings.description: Ask your driver to take you to Nguom Ngao before or after Ban Gioc. This immense cave holds a series of majestic, jaw-dropping caverns, filled with delicate, intricate formations of stalactites and stalagmites. In the low season, you may even have the cave to yourself, which is an experience probably not to be had elsewhere. Optional guides will helpfully point out particularly interesting rocks and bat roosts. 5,000 dong.

listings.name: Pac Bo
listings.description: An important revolutionary site about 52 km from Cao Bằng city, where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked after returning to Vietnam in 1941. The area includes the clear Lenin Stream, Karl Marx Mountain, caves, and forested walking paths, combining historical interest with striking natural scenery.

listings.name: God's Eye Mountain
listings.description: Located within the Non Nuoc Cao Bang UNESCO Global Geopark, this limestone mountain is famous for the large circular hole through its center. The surrounding valley is linked to the Thang Hen lake system and changes strongly with the seasons: in wetter months, water fills the basin, while in drier periods the area can open into a broad grassland landscape.

listings.name: Phong Nam
listings.description: A border commune famous for its poetic landscapes, featuring the Quây Sơn River, rice fields, and traditional Tày stilt houses. The area is especially scenic in harvest season, when the valley turns golden. Visitors can explore local village paths by bicycle, kayak on calm stretches of the river in some areas, or hike to viewpoints near Ngọc Côn for wide panoramas over the valley and surrounding limestone peaks.

listings.name: Bac Lam Hotel
listings.description: Near an elementary school, this hotel is in a peaceful area a few streets in from Kim Dong. Spacious rooms are comfortable and have air-con and mosquito nets. No WiFi.

listings.name: Bang Giang Hotel
listings.description: KimDong ward.

listings.name: Huong Thom Hotel
listings.description: 45-46 Kimdong.

listings.name: Sam Mountain
listings.description: Bike to Sam Mountain: rent a bike from your hotel (USD1-2) and ride 6 m to the base of Sam Mountain. It's an easy ride over flat paved and gravel road, just watch out for traffic. Walk on food from the base of the mountain, up the stairs to the top. Many viewpoints and cafe's with hammocks along the way to stop for a drink and a rest. Alternatively you can take a moto straight to the top of Sam Mountain, a great place to catch the sunset and see the views of Vietnam and into Cambodia.

listings.name: Tra Su Bird Sanctuary
listings.price: 75,000 dong per person for 1½ hour visit (includes both speed and row boat ride)
listings.description: As of January 2015 most hotels and travel agents are charging around USD34 for a two person trip to Tra Su (Includes moto drivers and boat fees). If you speak to any of the moto drivers around the covered market you should be able to hire one for around 150,000 - 200,000 dong per moto and can visit Sam Mountain or the Pagoda on the way back. Some of the drivers speak good English. Hiring a driver on your own will save about USD8-10 for a two person trip (depending on your negotiating skills).

listings.name: Thanh Tinh
listings.description: A nice and clean local restaurant that serves vegan food. Friendly and English-speaking staff. They can also prepare take-away meals (handy for the journey on the slow boat to Cambodia). They charged 95,000 dong for a 'com phan', almost three times the usual price (March 2011).

listings.name: Bay Bong
listings.description: Good food with a very long menu; locals and visitors eat here. The atmosphere isn't particularly romantic.

listings.name: Cherry Homestay
listings.description: Villa-style house, very clean rooms, lovely owner who will assist with all kinds of matters such as directions, recommendations, even free transfers to ATM and speedboat pier. Located on the border of town, but still in walkable distance to the center.

listings.name: Hang Chau II Hotel
listings.description: Good budget option, within walking distance from the market and the river. It's a bit impersonal, with a lack of decorative touches throughout the building, but it also has a stately 1960s ambiance, and the rooms are big. Parking is available. It's a popular destination for tour groups, so check in early.

listings.name: Trung Nguyen
listings.price: Rooms are small but very clean, with hot water, a/c, and television, and cost about USD16 (Jan 2015).
listings.description: Great staff.

listings.name: Motel Number 6 Thanh Mai
listings.description: For a budget place, the atmosphere is clean and relaxing. Potentional for bus station pick-up and Mekong slow boat/bus trip to Phnom Penh available.

listings.name: Victoria Chau Doc Hotel
listings.price: Rooms from USD99-155, river view suites USD144-220
listings.description: A luxury hotel where you'd least expect to find one, with no amenity left behind. Features 92 rooms, 4 suites, and total incongruity with its surroundings. Transfers to Phnom Penh via private speedboat are available.

listings.name: Lâm Viên park
listings.description: Nice park with ponds, gardens and birdwatching area.

listings.name: Bar New World
listings.description: Dancing.

listings.name: Bar Nguyen
listings.description: Dancing.

listings.name: Beaches
listings.description: Don't expect surfable waves, though!

listings.name: Caves
listings.description: There are a lot of caves around the island, though none of them are particularly impressive. Some cost money and may have optional guides. You can find them using the map or signs on the island.

listings.name: Ha Long Bay, Bai Tu Long Bay
listings.description: Organised 2- or 3-day trips into Ha Long and Bai Tu Long Bay for kayaking, caving, swimming and diving. Book via the honest and fair Mr. Lu at the post office. Prices ~US$45 per person for 2-day, 1-night trip (assuming 4 people in group).

listings.name: Monkey Island
listings.description: Several boats run day trips to nearby Monkey Island either in isolation or as part of a larger tour. The island apparently has monkeys, but only a few around the accommodation were in evidence. These animals are used to getting their food from either the guests or the bins, and therefore are not afraid of humans, so they might cause a problem. There is some accommodation on the island, which consists of eight small, but cosy, bamboo huts just behind a secluded beach. The food was nice, the drinks cheap, and the scenery was spectacular. There's some kayaking available, and a trail for walking,…

listings.name: National Park
listings.description: The domain of the endangered Cat Ba Langur, of which there are supposed to be only around 100 left. Things on offer include a walk to a peak viewing tower (1½-2 hr round trip; slippery and muddy if it's rained recently), a frog pond (probably better in the off (wet) season), a short nature walk near the frog pond, more stuff which you can probably find online.

listings.name: Visiting Lan Ha Bay
listings.address: Lan Ha Bay, Cat Hai, Hai Phong
listings.description: Visit Lan Ha Bay with Serenity Premium Cruise are among few cruises designed in the neoclassical Indochine Style with a harmonious combination of Tradition and Modernity.

listings.name: Mr. Zoom Hotel and Restaurant
listings.description: Mostly good meals, but if he offers you an enormous (2 kg) round-looking crab creature thing, save your US$35.

listings.name: Phuong Phuong Restaurant
listings.description: The restaurant has views of the sea, serves Vietnamese food and European food. Airy space, at an affordable price. Be wary of very long wait.

listings.name: Noble House
listings.description: Offers 2 for 1 cocktails and free pool.

listings.name: Flightless Bird Bar
listings.description: The original bar on the island, run by a New Zealander and going strong for 15 years. The drinks menu includes reasonably priced imported bottles of wine from various parts of the world as well as a straight to the point cheap drinks section. Darts upstairs.

listings.name: Rose Bar
listings.description: Awesome drink menu, most cocktails 40,000. Brand new with nice atmosphere, and a really helpful, friendly young owner. Best cocktail prices in town, if you're sick of drinking beer all the time. Open late, rare in Cat Ba.

listings.name: Hotel Phu Thanh
listings.description: Really nice, large, clean rooms. Has free Wi-Fi included and satellite flat screen TV. Good showers with hot water that actually have pressure. They also serve some great food in the restaurant during the busier summer months. Friendly staff and family-owned and run.

listings.name: Ngoc Hoa Hotel and Restaurant
listings.description: Rooms facing the bay, close to the ferry. Free Wi-Fi. Elevator. Fridge and air-con included. Family restaurant downstairs. Tours and motorbikes available at good prices if you ask, but the staff is not pushy. Their restaurant serves good simple Vietnamese food, soups, noodles, rice. Strong coffee and fruit smoothies. Big beer for under a dollar.

listings.name: Le Pont Hotel
listings.price: Dormitory US$3.50 per person, rooms US$4.50 per person, minimum two persons (Apr 2012)

listings.name: Song Chanh
listings.price: Double and twin rooms, low season US$10, high season US$15
listings.description: A great value hotel along the main strip in Cat Ba town. Very friendly staff who can also organise onward travel or tours around the island. Ask for Mr. Thuy, and go on the national park trek with his uncle.

listings.name: Sunflower One Hotel
listings.description: Many rooms have sea views. It is often used with Ha Long Bay boat tours when an overnight stay is requested on Cat Ba Island. It is a quality hotel with good food. It has Wi-Fi in rooms, but it can be somewhat unreliable. Its sister hotel, Sunflower Two, which is often used with cheaper Ha Long Bay tours, is about 1 km inland on the same road, and is not as nice.

listings.name: Phuong Phuong Hotel
listings.description: Many rooms with a view to the sea, the room is cheaper in the low season with US$7 included breakfast.

listings.name: Dive! Dive! Dive!
listings.description: Daily dive and snorkelling trips from a 15-m custom-built dive boat or 5-m speedboat. Opened in 2010 and affiliated with SSI, owned by an American. Having completed more than 1,000 dives on the islands, there is simply nobody who knows the diving better. They are the only full-time resident expats and the only fully Western-owned and operated business on the island. Turtle trips in season. Bicycles, snorkelling gear, and camping gear for rent. Buy today, dive tomorrow diving and medical insurance available. Stop in for tourist information. Also they are a good resource for bookings for all of…

listings.name: Rainbow Divers
listings.description: PADI dive centre operating out of the Six Senses Resort on Dat Doc Beach. They offer daily dive trips.

listings.name: Turtle Sanctuary
listings.description: The turtle tour can be booked at the national park office. You may see a turtle laying eggs. Turtle season is only from Jun-early September. Turtles are likely only nesting in Jul-Aug with a few hatchlings still coming out in September. The park will happily sell you tickets out of season and promise turtles. The trip is not cheap. Be aware and do not fall for this. Do not book a turtle tour outside of this time as it is very likely you will not see any. The national park will thoughtfully refund you 10% if this does happen. Overnight stays can be arranged. This office will also provide very…

listings.name: Con Dao Dive Center
listings.description: Con Dao Dive Center is a PADI Dive Center located on Con Dao Island, Vietnam. The center provides scuba diving, snorkeling, freediving, and PADI certification courses, operating with certified PADI instructors and regularly maintained equipment in accordance with PADI standards and local marine park regulations. The center also supports marine conservation initiatives, including sea turtle protection programs in Con Dao National Park.

listings.name: Noodle Shop
listings.description: For lunchtime, you can also find some local restaurants that serve good noodle soups for 15,000 dong. This is one of them.

listings.name: Phuong Han
listings.description: Popular with the tourist crowd. Atmosphere needs some work, but the food is good and it is reasonably priced. Very popular for lunch.

listings.name: Tri Ky
listings.description: Offers tasty, fresh seafood at reasonable prices, and has an English menu available, although offerings are relatively sparse.

listings.name: Bar200
listings.description: Near the market, and associated with Senses diving, serves decent Western food, cocktails and good breakfasts.

listings.name: A.T.C. Resort
listings.description: Slightly overpriced compared to the other hotels but the food is good.

listings.name: Saigon Con Dao
listings.description: Bungalows right on the beach at the end of town. Government-owned. Lacking in character, but is clean and has a nice swimming pool. The restaurant has views of both the ocean and the old Con Dao Prison Museum. A good variety of food, and excellent Vietnamese coffee. English menu available.

listings.name: Seatravel Con Dao Resort
listings.description: Bungalows right on the beach at the end of town, where the beach is quiet and nice, although sometimes littered. Sea Travel is a bit of a dump, with reports of rats in the rooms, but the large bungalows open right onto the beach and offer some of the best views and locations for Con Dao, especially on a budget. The manager knows some English and is helpful with relocating unsatisfied customers to the Con Dao Resort, which is further from the beach but offers more standard, less "rustic" rooms, as well as a pool.Has an open-air lobby that doubles as a restaurant, and offers outside seating…

listings.name: Six Senses
listings.description: Resort and spa. The beach is more private and cleaner than the larger stretch of beach shared by the other hotels, and the resort is arranged as private bungalows, with each bungalow having unobstructed views of the water. The resort is much more expensive than the other hotel options, but also offers visitors amenities not available at the other hotels. Airport transfer is US$20 per person. Has upscale dining options. If they are busy, they will turn you away even if the restaurant is empty.

listings.name: Ninh Kieu Park & Riverfront
listings.description: Ninh Kieu Park is a city park situated along the Can Tho River, stretching from the ferry terminal at Nguyen An Ninh Rd to the Ninh Kieu Hotel at the end of Hai Ba Trung Rd. Although the park sports some greenery, one of its most noticeable features is a public square surrounding a large statue of Ho Chi Minh. The other big attraction is Ninh Kieu Tourist Market, which houses souvenir vendors, cafes and restaurants. Just outside the market, you'll also find a ticket booth, selling boat trips up the river to places like Cai Rang Floating Market. The park is a busy place in the evenings, when…

listings.name: Can Tho Museum of Tarot
listings.address: 44 Đ. Nguyễn Khuyến, Tân An, Ninh Kiều
listings.description: An unusual institution in Southeast Asia, the Museum of Tarot is a small museum with what appears to be copies of almost every tarot deck ever published, along with various other artifacts related to western esotericism, including an impressionistic portrait of Aleister Crowley.

listings.name: Xuan Khanh Quarter
listings.description: In the 18th century the quarter was named Tham Tướng after General Tham Tướng who fought the Siamese troops who were advancing from Ha Tien in 1772. The name of the place was changed after the Vietnam War to reflect the ideology of the new regime in power.

listings.name: Munirensay Temple
listings.description: A beautiful Khmer pagoda that gives Can Tho a touch of Cambodia, recalling the region's heritage as part of the Khmer Empire.

listings.name: Chùa Ông (Ong Pagoda)
listings.description: Just across from Ho Chi Minh's statue in Ninh Kieu Park is a little pagoda, constructed in the 1890s. Apparently a secret hideout for communist revolutionaries during the Vietnam War, the pagoda is now considered a national monument. It's worth seeing if only for its artistic value, with its intricate altars featuring carved wooden bas-reliefs.

listings.name: Quang Duc Pagoda
listings.description: One of the biggest and most active Buddhist temples with monks living in the premises. Visitors are welcome at any time of the day. There are fewer people during the afternoon, when it is rather hot, but it gets very lively often in the evenings.

listings.name: Tham Tướng Church
listings.description: Nice little church built by the French.

listings.name: Tin Lanh Baptist Church
listings.description: Around 8% of Vietnamese are Catholics, but as this church demonstrates, Protestant denominations are also present.

listings.name: Canals
listings.description: The canal system around Can Tho is a fascinating travel network, much more relaxed than the bustling roads. Hire a small rowboat (probably with a small motor as well) that can take you through the small canals that the larger tour boats cannot navigate. Tours from 06:00-14:00, including two floating markets and various sites along the canals, can be found for less than 250,000 dong per person. Ask around at the riverfront and make sure to negotiate the price. Some boat operators will ask for more money to visit the canals. The price should already include them.

listings.name: Floating markets
listings.description: Floating markets make for a lively scene, where many goods are exchanged, and can be easily visited by small boats for about USD3/hour per boat. You can take a tour from Ninh Kiều Pier, where the "boat ladies" are charmingly eager to welcome you aboard. Starting prices (Sep 2011) are about USD10-20 for a 3- or 7-hr tour with either one market plus canals, or several markets plus canals. It can be bargained down to USD7 and USD15. Pay attention as there is a pushy old lady selling boat tours pestering tourists at the riverside. Best to get your tour directly from a boat owner. Non-packaged…

listings.name: Countryside Tour
listings.description: If you want to go out of city, get out off the noise and enjoy natural air, the tour is designed for you. This trip provides a general view of countryside life style and packed full of fun with a lot to see, do, experience and totally worth to see. You have a chance to visit orchard islet, enjoy tropical fruits, natural wind, know how people make their living from farming and ranching, specially cooking.

listings.name: Nam Bo Restaurant
listings.description: Beautiful restaurant set in a French style villa with Hau River view from second floor, good food and so is the service.

listings.name: Nem Nuong Thanh Van
listings.description: Famous for its "nem" or spring roll, grilled pork rolled in rice sheet with vegetable, herbs and served with dipping sauce.

listings.name: Pad Thai Tomato
listings.description: If you don't mind eating with a predominantly foreign clientele, this place is a must try. Apart from plenty of Vietnamese dishes, there are fairly authentic dishes form Thailand, Korea, Hong Kong and Macao. The food prices are reasonable, as is the beer. Local wines are available by the glass and service is snappy and friendly.

listings.name: Gony Spa Cafe Lounge
listings.description: Offers a variety of foods including pizza, pasta, and beefsteak as well as local food. It also offers shakes, smoothies, coffee, and ice cream.

listings.name: Hot Pot Alley
listings.description: Hot Pot Alley is home to about a dozen restaurants all offering the same specialty, Can Tho hot pot. Hot pots are prepared DIY on a small cooker on your table. As the soup gets cooking you add different vegetables, leaves, egg or rice noodles, tofu, and eggs. You only pay for the side dishes you use and you can order more of any dish you wish. You get free refills of the hot pot soup. Ask for "them nuoc" meaning more water. It might seem unusual to put in some of the leaves into the hot pot, but try and you will love it.

listings.name: Nam Bo
listings.description: In a classic building facing the river, serves very tasty Vietnamese as well as some Western foods such as pizza and spaghetti. The service is nice and efficient, and a surprising variety of languages is spoken there, from English to French to Dutch and even some Japanese.

listings.name: Sao Hom
listings.description: Serves a large palette of Vietnamese foods, and some Western food, too. The ambiance at night is special.

listings.name: Cafe Bar Eden
listings.description: Good for couples.

listings.name: International Roof Top Bar
listings.address: 93 Mau Than St, Xuan Ward, Ninh Kieu
listings.price: Beer USD1; spirits USD1; wine, USD1.80
listings.description: Beautiful view over the city. The place is run by a young Vietnamese-German couple who moved to Can Tho from Singapore. They love music from around the world. A cosy place to relax.

listings.name: Golf Club
listings.description: Upscale club with many businessmen preferring this place to chill out on the weekend.

listings.name: XK club
listings.address: 108B Tran Van Kheo St, Ninh Kieu District
listings.description: Nice red-black decor with banging sound system, but quite small, therefore more secure and chill than other clubs. Pretty and friendly go-go dancers.

listings.name: Xe Loi Club
listings.address: Hau Riverside Park, Bai Cat Zone, Cai Khe Ward, Ninh Kieu District
listings.description: The place to be on weekends. Spacious club, good lighting/sound system with laser to boot. Most fun happens from 23:00-02:00. Youthful and energetic, but can be quite a sketchy crowd.

listings.name: Hello 2 Hotel
listings.address: 31 Chau Van Liem St, Ninh Kieu
listings.description: Friendly and comfortable. Massage and spa in-house.

listings.name: Hotel Xoai
listings.address: 93 Mau Than St, Xuan Khanh, Ninh Kieu
listings.description: Young and friendly atmosphere. 23 compact rooms with double or single beds, private bathroom with shower, toilet, fan, air-con, phone. All rooms with windows. Fast free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel. Guests can relax on the roof terrace. Helpful and trustworthy staff, moderate prices for tours, no additional charge on bus bookings.

listings.name: Spring Hotel
listings.description: Very clean and friendly place. Rooms maintained and bed sheets changed daily. Enjoy meals any time you want at the nice sitting area by the big windows on each floor. The downside is distance from the centre and river (40 min on foot), but free bikes to ride around as well as motorbike rental. Staff are nice. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: 31 Restaurant
listings.description: One of several cheap and very simple places on this road. Rooms can be a bit smelly as the kitchen aromas waft upstairs. If you have an allergy beware of the dust from fans. Wi-Fi works at reception, but not in the rooms (most notably the back ones). Avoid booking bus and tours here as it seems a lot more expensive.

listings.name: Xuan Mai Hotel
listings.description: Location is good. Relatively clean, but some rooms with older beds are said to have bed bugs. Rooms have LCD TV with Vietnamese channels. Air-con available with top up charge. Bath with bathtub. Hot water might not work at night because of their water system. Check for rooms with windows. No English speaking staff.

listings.name: Mekong Delta Inn Backpackers Hostel
listings.address: 175 a Nguyen Van Cu An Hoa Ward Ninh Kieu Dist.
listings.description: dorms with 4 or 10 beds. air.con. hot water. free breakfast free wifi.

listings.name: Thanh Ha Guest House
listings.description: double room with own bathroom

listings.name: Hotel 31
listings.description: double room with own bathroom.

listings.name: Hien Guest House
listings.description: double room with own bathroom.

listings.name: Kim Lan Hotel
listings.description: Friendly, welcoming staff, some of whom speak fairly good English. Well-situated, with much of downtown area (including bus station, jetty and markets) within walking distance. Rooms are comfortable and well-furnished: private bathroom with shower & toilet, fan, air-con, phone. Some rooms do not have windows; front rooms face the street and can be noisy. Free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel. Breakfast is offered on top floor with a view over the city. They offer some daily tours to the floating markets and in the countryside (USD25-50) with a good guide.

listings.name: Kim Thơ
listings.description: Clean, with Wi-Fi and wired LAN in the rooms.

listings.name: Nam Bộ Boutique Hotel
listings.description: The Nam Bộ Boutique Hotel has one of the finest restaurants, l'Escale, in town. Quiet and overlooking the river.
