listings.name: Victoria Can Tho
listings.description: Luxury resort on Cái Khế Island, including a swimming pool, a spa, a ballroom, and a rice barge for a scenic breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

listings.name: Mekong Rustic Can Tho
listings.description: Surrounded by Vam Xang lush orchards.

listings.name: Muong Thanh Luxury
listings.address: Area E1, Cai Khe River Islet, Cai Khe Ward,Ninh Kieu District,Can Tho City, Vietnam
listings.description: Fine hotel with a pool and a rooftop bar, spa and a casino (not confirmed).

listings.name: Mã Pí Lèng River Gorge
listings.description: There are small tour boats here. The Mã Pí Lèng Pass above lies at an elevation of 1,500 meters.

listings.name: Mama's House Hostel
listings.address: No 368, 20 thang 8 street, 1st group, P. Nguyễn Trãi

listings.name: Ha Tien Vegas
listings.address: Hà Tiên, Vietnam International Border Prek Chak
listings.description: Hop over to the Cambodian side to visit, this casino/hotel. The entertainment resort has more than 100 slots, over 40 table games, Internet gaming and a Sports Book. For non-gamblers, Ha Tien Vegas Hotel provides a luxury hotel complemented by 24/7 room service, Chinese and international dining venues/cafes. Offers 24-hour shuttle service from the hotel and casino to downtown Hà Tiên.

listings.name: Ha Tien Fresh Seafood
listings.description: Right on the beach is a great local seafood restaurant with a very private upstairs area overlooking the coast.

listings.name: Metro 88
listings.description: Poolside entertainment.

listings.name: Oasis Bar
listings.description: Expat running the bar serving cold beer in cold glasses for less than 20,000 dong each. Also the only place where you can get cocktails, spirits and gin & tonic. They also serve coffee.

listings.name: Hai Phong City Museum
listings.hours: Open mornings and afternoons from 14:00. Open late evening Tue and Sun, closed Sat

listings.name: Naval Museum
listings.address: 353 St, Anh Dung Commune, Kien Thuy District

listings.name: Elephant Mountain An Lao
listings.description: Elephant mountain An Lao or Núi Voi is a complex of rocky mountains, undulating and meandering. It is around 20 km far from Hai Phong city center. People call this Elephant Mountain as it looks like a reclining elephant. Elephant mountain An Lao is located in Truong Thanh, An Tien and An Thang communes of An Lao district.

listings.name: Ngoa Van Hermitage Pagoda relic cluster
Haiphong Brewery
listings.description: Bia hoi, fresh from the brewery that is directly behind this location. Many beer stands here. Look for the bar to the right of the alley where motor bikes are carrying yellow kegs in and out of the brewery. Decent food in an open kitchen. 10,000 dong for a tall glass (500 ml), 4,000 dong for a regular. The beer is pleasant with a slightly sweet aftertaste. Way better than Hanoi beer! Arguably best beer in Vietnam. A must-visit if you are in town and thirsty.

listings.name: Amber bar
listings.description: Upstairs of the Haiphong Brewery. If you are looking for an Amber beer, then this is the place to go. Very delicious, but definitely more expensive than other local beers. 35,000 dong for a tall glass (500 ml), 25,000 dong for a regular.

listings.name: Classic Hoang Long Hotel
listings.price: USD70-135, but an introductory special slices the prices by 45%
listings.description: This is an exceptional hotel, in perhaps the tallest building in Haiphong. The bar/restaurant on the 17th floor has panoramic views of the city.

listings.name: Imperial Boat Hotel
listings.description: New centrally located luxury hotel.

listings.name: Somerset Central TD Hai Phong City
listings.address: Tower A, TD Plaza, Lot 20A, Le Hong Phong St, Dong Khe Ward, Ngo Quyen District
listings.description: This property offers studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments. Facilities include a gymnasium, outdoor swimming pool, children’s playroom, living room and library.

listings.name: Japanese Covered Bridge
listings.description: The bridge was constructed in the early 1600s by the Japanese community, roughly 40 years before they left the city to return to Japan under the strict policy of sakoku enforced by the Tokugawa Shogunate, and renovated in 1986. Today, it's the symbol of Hoi An. Entry is one coupon, but it's possible to cross back and forth several times without meeting a ticket-checker. If your scruples bother you, leave a tribute for the pig statue or the dog statue standing guard at opposite ends of the bridge.

listings.name: Quan Cong Temple
listings.description: Founded in the 15th century, this temple is dedicated to Quan Cong, a Chinese general who is remembered and worshipped for his qualities of loyalty, integrity and justice. Statues of him and several others are inside the temple.

listings.name: Thanh Ha pottery village
listings.description: Formed in the sixteenth century, Thanh Ha Pottery Village is one of the oldest pottery villages in Vietnam. This village is located right on the banks of Thu Bon River, about 3 km from Hoi An ancient town. Over five centuries, Thanh Ha pottery village still preserves its traditional pottery-making process, which manually shapes pottery by hand and foot pedal without using molds. This method creates a unique feature in this village’s ceramic products. Nowadays, Thanh Ha ceramic products are mainly used for decoration and display purposes.

listings.name: Museum of Hoi An History and Culture
listings.description: The museum contains some old black and white photos of Hoi An taken in the early 20th century. It also houses an old cannon, some two-thousand year old pots from the Sa Huynh period, and a case full of 9th-century bricks and tiles from the Champa period.

listings.name: Museum of Folk Culture
listings.description: Some may be put off by the bizarre-looking plaster sculptures of Vietnamese peasants, but this museum documents the dress and culture of rural Vietnam.

listings.name: Museum of Sa Huynh Culture
listings.description: The museum's main collection consists of pottery and urns from the 1st and 2nd centuries. Upstairs is another museum, the Museum of the Revolution. Its main collection consists of pictures from war heroes and a collection of weapons such as grenade launchers, machine guns and AK 47s.

listings.name: Museum of Trade Ceramics
listings.description: The dusty, unlabeled displays of broken pottery are eminently forgettable, but the house itself is nice enough, and it provides a good opportunity to explore the shape and layout of an old Hoi An home.

listings.name: Old house of Phung Hung
listings.description: Traditional two-story wooden house, inhabited over 100 years by eight generations; and the current one guides you around in hope of a tip.

listings.name: Old house of Tan Ky
listings.description: As above, a younger member of the family will provide a cup of tea and a "tour" that doesn't stray from the front room of the house, as you'd need to step over sleeping members of the older generation to go anywhere else. The design of the house shows how local architecture incorporated Japanese and Chinese influences. Japanese elements include the crab shell-shaped ceiling supported by three beams in the living room. Chinese poems written in mother-of-pearl are hanging from a number of the columns that hold up the roof.

listings.name: Cam Pho Communal House
listings.address: 52 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Phường Minh An

listings.name: Chinese Assembly Hall
listings.description: Pan-Chinese assembly hall jointly built by the Cantonese, Teochew, Hokkien (Fujian), Hainanese and Hakka communities.

listings.name: Quang Trieu Assembly Hall
listings.description: Built in 1885 for the Cantonese community, it has a calm courtyard with ornate statuary. Take a peek at the half-hidden back yard and its kitschy pastel dragon statues.

listings.name: Phuc Kien Meeting Hall
listings.description: Hokien (Fujian) meeting hall built in 1757.

listings.name: Trieu Chau Meeting Hall
listings.description: Teochew community meeting hall built in 1887. It's near the Fujian hall, also occupying the block.

listings.name: Hai Nam Assembly Hall
listings.description: Hainanese community meeting hall built in 1875.

listings.name: Minh Huong Communal House
listings.description: Built by the Minh Huong, Chinese Ming Dynasty loyalists who were given refuge in Vietnam after refusing to submit to the new Manchu Qing rulers of China. Their descendants are today assimilated into the ethnic Vietnamese and no longer identify as ethnic Chinese.

listings.name: Hoi An Art Craft Manufacturing Workshop
listings.description: Folk music performances are offered Tu-Su at 10:15 and 15:15.

listings.name: Hoi An Traditional Art Performance House
Bamboo Circus
listings.description: A small-scale Cirque du Soleil-style show of acrobatics and dance with traditional and modern Vietnamese themes in a 300-seat theatre. Excellent visuals and choreography, enthusiastic young performers. Buy tickets online, at the theatre, or at many hotels. It's a small theatre, so the cheap seats still have a good view.

listings.name: Hoi An memories show
listings.description: A big musical-esque show on the history of Hoi An, from early settlers until the golden era as an important trading port. Huge stage, very good lighting effects and several hundred actors active at the same time. Situated on an island in the river. The whole island area surrounding the stage is a renaissance theme park with the same topic of the history of Hoi An. Leading up to the main show, there are mini-shows with reenactments and dance performances in different places around the theme park. Tickets can be bought when entering the island via the two bridges, or online (sometimes cheaper…

listings.name: Hoi An Silk Village
listings.description: Revived 300-year-old Champa silk traditions. Half day tours encompassing the entire silk process, from silkworms to dressmaking. Showroom in a converted Quang Nam-style house with 100 different ao dai, representing all of the 54 different minority groups in Vietnam. Also a spacious colonial-style restaurant serving local dishes and a silk showroom where professional tailors custom design and make garments for visitors.

listings.name: Central Market
listings.description: Has a food court with several stands serving Hoi An specialities and typical Vietnamese food like pho, and spring rolls. It has a few stands catering to tourists with English-speaking staff and menus, and stands catering mostly to Vietnamese which serve rice and side dishes.

listings.name: Banana fritters stall
listings.description: Delicious banana fritters in dough. They squish the banana, then dip it into liquid dough and finally fry it. Freshly made, and not lying around the whole day like you often see in the center — many locals stop by with the motorbike, so they are constantly making new ones.

listings.name: Thiên Bảo Quán
listings.price: 6,000 dong per wrap, vegetables and sauce free
listings.description: Serves the probably most inexpensive Bánh Xèo in all Vietnam, and is very authentic in addition. It actually seems to be vegan, but they also serve meat sticks if you are looking for additional taste. You won't find any fancy lighting or comfortable Western sized chairs here, just the regular tiny plastic chairs and tables. But the experience rolling the wrap parts, and dipping it into the delicious gravy is well worth the trip here.

listings.name: Cao lầu Không Gian Xanh
listings.description: They serve Cao lầu, Hoành Thánh Mỳ (Wonton), Bánh Bao Bánh Vạc (White Rose) and Cơm Gà. However, the portion size can be disappointing and they are very pushy about ordering drinks.

listings.name: Ba Dam Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.description: Great vegan Vietnamese food selection, there are so many options to choose from. The vegetarian Pho is amazing. Family restaurant hidden in an alley. Very friendly staff.

listings.name: Phở Tùng
listings.description: They serve super nice Pho Bo, for many who may not know how to eat their side dish vegetable, the boss can teach you how to blend with the sauce prepared for it. The owners are super lovely.

listings.name: Madam Khanh - The Banh Mi Queen
listings.description: How they prepared the meat is different to elsewhere. The chili sauce and pate are so unique. Delicious and fresh. The vegetarian option is fire.

listings.name: White Rose
listings.description: The shop that makes most of the "white rose" dumplings served all around town.

listings.name: Quán Mười
listings.description: Besides Mì Quảng, they also serve delicious Cao lầu.

listings.name: Quán Cô Mai
listings.description: They offer Mì Quảng and Mì Ga. Watch out though, they might claim that eggs are extra, which they are not — just point to the picture of the menu.

listings.name: Bale Well Restaurant
listings.price: Set menu 110,000 dong, Bánh Xèo 50,000 dong
listings.description: Set menu: bánh xèo, pork savoury pancakes; barbecued satay pork loin, wrapped in a lettuce leaf, with side salad. Steep price for a few rice pancakes.

listings.name: Bazar Cafe & Restaurant
listings.description: New in town, serves the best Vietnamese and Mediterranean barbeque in the garden. Comfortable lounge, cocktails and shisha inside the traditional wooden house.

listings.name: Dingo Deli
listings.description: This delicatessen offers an extensive selection of gourmet foods through the restaurant and European grocery store. Attractive ambience, and the aroma of freshly brewed coffee. A wooden constructed adventure play ground for children to play on overlooks paddocks with buffalo and the Thu Bon River.

listings.name: Red Bridge Restaurant & Cooking School
listings.description: Next to the Thu Bon River within 2 acres of tropical gardens. Offers a wide range of Vietnamese Food, in an open air restaurant. Cooking Classes begin around 08:00 at the Hai Scout Cafe for an Italian-style coffee then a tour of the market to shop for fruit & veg. Booking for dinner is essential. They sometimes close early if there are no customers. They offer cocktails as well as the usual beers and a wine list.

listings.name: Son Hoian
listings.description: Very popular stopping point for those cycling back from the beach.

listings.name: Temari
listings.description: Authentic Japanese cuisine from the Kobe area, using high-quality ingredients.

listings.name: Thành Nam Quán
listings.price: Plates from 50,000 dong, mains from 80,000 dong
listings.description: Tiny Vietnamese restaurant where everything is delicious.

listings.name: Thanh Restaurant
listings.description: Great Vietnamese and Western food. Excellent grilled fished in banana leaf and nice river view.

listings.name: Madam Kieu
listings.price: Set menus from 500,000 dong for two
listings.description: You're definitely paying a premium for the location, but this atmospheric restaurant serves excellent renditions of Hoi An and central Vietnamese favorites, and the river views and people watching from the wraparound balcony on the 2nd floor are hard to beat. Air-con seating available as well. Live music on the 1st floor on weekends.

listings.name: BB Lounge
listings.address: 13 Nguyen Hoang St an Hoi islet
listings.description: The new bar, lounge and club in town, located on the third floor above Bamboo Buddha restaurant. Nice selection of cocktails, rum shooters and tapas. Live music and regular DJs, dance floor. Sky balcony, open late.

listings.name: Dive Bar Restaurant
listings.description: Great bar in a traditional house with a back garden, pool table, Wi-Fi. Plays many kinds of music on request, with music once a week. Great choice of cocktails and beers, wine by bottle or by glass. Food: small tapas, Vietnamese salads, pasta, lasagne, hamburgers, seafood, rice salads.

listings.name: Rosie's cafe
listings.description: A lovely cafe tucked in a peaceful alley of Nguyen Thi Minh Khai. Signature drink is cold-brew coffee which is less acid than hot brewing and cold pressed juice. Not only the food and drink, but also the space to relax and enjoy the atmosphere of Hoi An old townal.

listings.name: Why Not Bar
listings.description: Late night bar near old town. Not to be confused with the much different bar/club of the same name in Nha Trang. This very small 3-storey bar advertises free drinks and cheap all-you-can drink specials. Patrons do not come to this bar until at least midnight, when the rest of the town has closed down. Open until late.

listings.name: Melody Boutique Villa
listings.description: 4-bed dorms (though no curtains), clean sheets, swimming pool, free bicycles, and Wi-Fi of course. Flood-safe. Many inexpensive eateries and markets around.

listings.name: Hoang Trinh Hotel
listings.description: Average value hot. Great hotel in good location and scenic setting. Well furnished en suite rooms with cable TV with excellent reception, air-con, ceiling fan, fridge, Wi-Fi and balcony restaurant with an impressive view. Has bicycles for hire for 15,000 dong next door and motorbikes also. The staff are friendly, and they provide complimentary small snacks as well as a welcome dinner.

listings.name: Quynh Long Villa
listings.address: 28 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Phường Minh An
listings.description: Very nice family run hotel with swimming pool 5 minutes walking from the center but in a quiet area even at night. Large and well furnished rooms with terrace, comfy beds, air-con, fan, Wi-Fi. Breakfast on request for 50.000 dong. Bicycles are free. The friendly lady speaks very good English, can organize transport from/to the airport and tours with a driver around the area.

listings.name: Betel Garden Homestay
listings.description: A bit out of the city centre and a beautifully landscaped garden with several species of areca and betel trees, complete with songbirds and fish in small ponds. Staff are incredibly friendly and try to make you feel at home, including complementary fruit in your room each day and the free bicycles. Their area also offers a nicely laid out secluded pool area, as well as two covered dining areas the 20 guests. The Vuon Trau Family organises a complimentary dinner together with their guests twice a week, offering free beverages (including beer) and excellent food.

listings.name: Hoi An Pho Library Hotel
listings.description: A beautiful small hotel with modern marble baths and the added bonus of in-room Wi-Fi. The deluxe rooms even have computers. The room service menu is packed full of local delicacies and the hotel features the only rooftop swimming pool in Hoi An. Breakfast is included in the price. What really makes this hotel are the staff, welcoming, helpful and professional, with excellent English.

listings.name: Nhi Nhi Hotel
listings.price: Standard/superior room: Single 680,000/795,000 dong, double or twin 800,000-1,020,000 dong. Family room 2,540,000 dong.
listings.description: Affordable, nice rooms and swimming pool. Near a local market but a bit far from tourist sites. Bargain to get good price. Normally price doesn't include breakfast.

listings.name: Villa Orchid Garden Riverside
listings.description: The name Orchid Garden originates from the owner's long held passion for orchids, with more than 30 varieties of orchid in the garden. The homestay has four secluded bungalows built in traditional Vietnamese architecture, surrounded by a variety of tropical trees, and equipped with modern convenient facilities. Each bungalow is named after a type of orchid found around the garden. Orchid Garden also has a traditional sanctuary for worshiping ancestors and for family activities.

listings.name: Palm Garden Beach Resort and Spa Hoi An
listings.description: A charming beachfront resort with 216 rooms and bungalows. It is 30 km from Danang International Airport and 5 km to Hoi An Ancient town.

listings.name: Hotel Royal Hoi An
listings.description: A French colonial style boutique hotel with Japanese architecture influence in the quiet area 5 minutes of walk from the Ancient Town of Hoi An. 119 rooms are of MGallery standard by Accor hotels, overlooking Thu Bon river, pool and Hoi An town. There are one outdoor pool, two restaurants, one chic bar, one spa, complimentary bikes and gym.

listings.name: Anantara Hoi An Resort
listings.description: French colonial style architecture with rooms overlooking the Thu Bon River at the east end of Hoi An, a short walk from the Old Town but just far enough away that a quiet night's sleep is practically assured. Rooms are large, many are bi-level with a sitting area, and have air-con, but the restaurant and bar are open to the breezes.

listings.name: Victoria Hoi An Beach Resort and Spa
listings.price: Internet rates from US$125, walk-up rates from US$165, honeymoon suites US$210–300

listings.name: Bahnar Orphanage
listings.description: Visitors and donations welcome.

listings.name: Catholic Seminary
listings.description: Houses a small minority museum, but the colonial-style building itself is well worth a visit.

listings.name: Montagnard Church
listings.description: Built in 1913 and restored in the 1990s. It is remarkable for its blending of local artistic tradition and Christian symbols: Bahnar villages, elephants, a scale model of a rong.

listings.name: Kon Tum Tourist
listings.description: If you are on a tight itinerary, it might be good to fix things beforehand, since they are often crowded with tour groups. Though some of the Bahnar villages actually form a part of Kontum's eastern and western edge, the ones farther away are more interesting. Highlights would be the different kinds of rong, the cemeteries of the Jarai, and joining a rice-wine party with the locals.

listings.name: Dakbla Restaurant
listings.description: Separate from the hotel of the same name, Dakbla is nicely themed with decorations from the surrounding minority peoples. Wide variety of food including local and Western staples, excellent wild boar. Popular with tourists. English spoken.

listings.name: Nghia
listings.description: Solid vegetarian option with rice, pho, and bun dishes.

listings.name: Cafe Eva
listings.description: Home to a local artist and a lot of his oeuvre is on display in the garden and the three-storey house resembling a stilt house. The place is a favourite among Vietnamese locals. The owner, Mr. An can also share in-depth knowledge of the Montagnards' culture and arrange day tours of Bahnar villages or explorations of indigenous culture, with local homestays.

listings.name: Sunrise Café
listings.description: Quiet two-storey café with good coffee and honest and nice staff.

listings.name: Hoang Thinh Hotel
listings.description: Simple hotel in the south of the city along the same road as the wooden church (Nguyen Hue). Huge discounts for Vietnamese. Exterior rooms are very noisy. Windowless rooms reasonably quiet.

listings.name: Hoang Van Hotel
listings.description: Broken English-speaking staff. Free Wi-Fi. Minibar prices only just above the street price. Restaurant downstairs. Bath tub. Air conditioning. Quiet location on a quiet street close to the Dak Bla River just after crossing the southern bridge. Hot water not always hot in some rooms.

listings.name: Hong My Hotel
listings.description: Fairly nice hotel with standard rooms with TV. Maybe the best value in Kon Tum.

listings.name: Hotel Thinh Vuong
listings.description: Clean mini hotel. All rooms have hot water, air-conditioning, Wi-Fi, mini-bar and a TV. The deluxe rooms also have a balcony and PC. Off road parking for motorbikes. Breakfast for 35,000 dong.

listings.name: Poussiere de Vie Cottage
listings.description: Two cottages, about ten persons maximum in each.

listings.name: Dong Xuyen Hotel
listings.description: Biggest hotel in town.

listings.name: Long Xuyen Hotel
listings.description: Good restaurant.

listings.name: Nha Tro
listings.description: General term for room for rent. Very cheap, but only if you want to live like a Vietnamese student.

listings.name: Nhà hàng Nhật Bản Sakura Deli
listings.description: Japanese restaurant of good quality.

listings.name: Cong To Vo
listings.description: An archway on the beach. Good place to see sunset.

listings.name: Đỉnh Thới Lới
listings.description: An extinct volcano with great view of the whole island.

listings.name: Hồ Thới Lới
listings.description: A freshwater lake on top of the extinct volcano.

listings.name: Chùa Hang
listings.description: A Buddhist pagoda inside a mountain cave, overlooking the sea.

listings.name: Poshanu Cham Tower
listings.description: The Poshanu Cham Tower in Phu Hai ward is a derelict remainder of the ancient Cham culture that was built in the 8th century. It is still in use for religious and social gatherings by the local Cham population, especially during the annual Kate festival.

listings.name: Fish Sauce Plants
listings.description: Where the famous nuoc mam (fish sauce) is produced. Big jars harbor the concoction that, after months in the blazing sun, is sold all over Vietnam to add some spice to the food.

listings.name: Red Sand Dunes
listings.description: The famous Red Sand Dunes on the main coastal road a short distance north of the fishing town at the north end of Mui Ne Bay, about 10 km from the main resort strip. The whole region is fairly sandy, with orange sand threatening to blow onto the coastal road in some spots. The dunes that visitors visit are about 50 ha (1/2 km²) of open sand on a hillside with ten-meter undulations, staffed by dusty children with plastic slides, who will offer instruction and assistance if you want to slide on the sand. Caution is recommended since a number of tourists have lost money, cameras or cell phones…

listings.name: Fishing harbor
listings.description: If you are staying on the resort strip in Ham Tien or Phu Hai wards, don't miss out to visit this once quiet "fishing village" but nowadays bustling town, at the northeast end of Mui Ne Bay. The coastal road leads straight into the town (with a left turn required at the first red light to continue up the coast). If you arrive during the dry "winter" season, don't miss the harbor overlook at the entrance to Mui Ne with a splendid view of hundreds of colorful fishing boats moored in the bay. The boats move to the other side of the "Shelter Cape" (English translation of "Mui Ne") during the…

listings.name: Mui Ne Market
listings.description: Further along into town, just off the main road, there is a colorful local market.

listings.name: Fairy Stream
listings.price: 10,000 dong (although entrance is officially free) and 5,000 dong for motorbike parking. Free from the north
listings.description: The Fairy Stream is a little creek that winds its way through bamboo forests, boulders and the dunes behind the village, in parts resembling a miniature version of the Grand Canyon. Local children will want to accompany you to show you the way (and of course earn a dollar or so), but since you're just following the stream, there's little need. For the most part, the stream is about ankle-deep and no more than knee-deep even at its deepest. It is sandy with few stones and can be walked comfortably barefooted. You can climb up the red sand hills overlooking the river valley and even walk there…

listings.name: White Sand Dunes
listings.description: The White Sand Dunes are approximately 45 km away from the Ham Tien tourist strip to the northeast, and some 24 km from the Red Sand Dunes and nearby resorts on the east side of the Mui Ne peninsula. Trips are offered by any tourist agency along the resort stretch for 4WD or quad drives, as well as by some resorts with their own vehicles. While too far away for a bicycle trip especially in summer, a motorbike trip can bring you there. Make sure to bring an international driver's licence if you do not own a Vietnamese one — driving without Vietnamese driver's license is illegal in Vietnam.

listings.name: Bo Ke Street
listings.address: 122 Nguyễn Đình Chiểu, Phường Hàm Tiến, Thành phố Phan Thiết, Bình Thuận
listings.description: This is a street full of local cafes that serve BBQ seafood. Prices are very cheap and choice is wide. Scallops with onion and garlic sauce are must-to-have here. If you're a fussy about hygiene, don't bother coming here.

listings.name: Joe's
listings.address: 86 Nguyen Dinh Chieu St, Ham Tien
listings.description: Joe's is the only place open 24/7 in Mui Ne. It's a cosy old farmhouse cafe offering Western fare. A Canadian developed the menu, and the pancakes with maple syrup (50,000 dong including coffee) are great. The sandwiches with home cut fries and salad (60,000 dong) are also recommended. Two movies are shown each evening in the pillow-filled loft. Free Wi-fi, exhibits and live performances. A great place to have your bus pick you up at 02:00 when you head out and great for a chill spot for after party breakfast or a romantic glass of wine. A 24-hr supermarket is part of the complex. Joe is on…

listings.name: Dragon Beach - Lounge Bar & Club
listings.description: Mui Ne's biggest disco with two dance floors, a pool, circular bar and its own access to the sea.

listings.name: Nirvana Beach Club (Line Up Bar)
listings.description: Bar and nightclub popular with independent travelers. It has a large dance floor, good sound system, good food and friendly staff. During happy hour from 18:00 to 21:00 some cocktails cost just 30,000 dong, and for all cocktails you buy you get a second for free.

listings.name: Lan Anh
listings.description: Local guesthouse in the village, a couple of kilometres from the resorts and beaches, but close to shops, market and street food stalls. Perfect for experiencing local life. Owner family can barely understand English but are nice. Room with 2 double beds, fan, fridge, toilet, and TV. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Thien Son
listings.description: Guest house just down the road from Joe's cafe with clean, large rooms. Very friendly people, though English is limited.

listings.name: The Bay
listings.description: Simple bungalows with A/C and warm water. On a side street a bit off the beach.

listings.name: Mui Ne Hills Bliss
listings.description: Different room categories from backpacker dorms to standard rooms and sea view rooms.

listings.name: Grace Boutique Resort
listings.description: Has the look of a Mediterranean villa. There are only 14 rooms, all with sea views. Well-trained staff, a beautiful garden, and a charming pool. Rates include daily breakfasts. Discounts are offered during the low season and for long-term stays. It is advisable to book well ahead during the holidays.

listings.name: The Sailing Bay Beach Resort
listings.description: 192 rooms with sea views, all-day restaurant, open-air beach club, a grand ballroom that accommodates 400 guests and a fully equipped board meeting room for 40 guests. On-site water sports facility with a professional international team managing board sailing, kite surfing and other activities.

listings.name: Anantara Mui Ne Resort
listings.address: Mui Ne Beach, KM10 Ham Tien Ward, Phan Thiet City
listings.description: The resort includes 89 rooms, suites and pool villas designed according to Vietnamese tradition.

listings.name: Blue Ocean Resort
listings.description: Has various rooms and bungalows. Only metres from many of the kite surfing schools, particularly Windchimes, which is directly outside the property.

listings.name: Cham Villas Boutique Luxury Resort
listings.description: Has 6 villas with beach front view and 12 villas with garden view. Each villa has a king size bed, bathtub overlooking a small private garden, and a large private patio with comfortable club chairs and a day bed.

listings.name: Pandanus Resort
listings.description: 134 renovated rooms including 24 bungalows with outdoor bathtub in a relaxing beachside environment: 10 ha of lush tropical gardens within walking distance of the Red Sand Dunes. Phan Thiet's largest free-form swimming pool, 2 restaurants, 3 bars incl. lounge with live entertainment, two live bands, spa (indoor and outdoor). Weekly seafood BBQ buffets by the pool, all Inclusive package, weddings, special events, team building, tours and excursions, transfer service. Complimentary bicycle rental. Daily complimentary walking tour of Mui Ne fishing town, free shuttle service to Mui Ne, Fairy…

listings.name: The Cliff Resort
listings.address: 5, Phu Hai Ward, Phan Thiet, Binh Thuan
listings.description: A resort complex that has many different room designs in different prices, the more big and beautiful they are, the more expensive they are. All guests can enjoy the big pool in the middle and can have access to the Mui Ne beach. The location is near Phan Thiet.

listings.name: Mandala Cham Bay Mui Ne
listings.address: DT716, Mui Ne, Phan Thiet City, Binh Thuan Province
listings.description: 508 rooms with design lines between modern and classic.

listings.name: Oolong Tea Plantations and Heart-shaped Tea Hill
listings.address: Thao Nguyen and Van Son wards
listings.description: These extensive commercial tea plantations cover thousands of hectares and grow Shan Tuyet, Bat Tien and imported oolong tea varieties. The tea rows are carefully trimmed into concentric curves or distinctive heart shapes. The plantations are a prominent agricultural landscape and a popular place for landscape photography on the plateau.

listings.name: Na Ka and Mu Nau Plum Valleys
listings.price: VND 20,000–40,000 per person for entry to orchards during blossom and harvest seasons
listings.description: These limestone valleys cover more than 100 hectares and specialize in Moc Chau's local plum variety. From late January to mid-February, the valleys are covered in white plum blossoms. The ripe plums are harvested from May to early June.

listings.name: Dai Yem Waterfall
listings.address: Ban Vat, formerly Muong Sang Ward, now part of Moc Chau Ward
listings.description: A natural waterfall fed by the Bo Co Lam and Bo He streams, it cascades more than 100 m over nine moss-covered limestone tiers. The water flows most strongly during the rainy season, from May to September. The nearby Love Glass Bridge spans a deep gorge.

listings.name: Ban Ang Pine Forest
listings.description: This natural pine forest covers more than 43 hectares and surrounds two tranquil freshwater lakes. Visitors can cycle around the lakes, walk beneath the tall pine trees and visit nearby high-tech strawberry farms where they can pick fruit.

listings.name: Pha Luong Peak
listings.price: Forest ranger and guide fees vary by tour
listings.description: This limestone mountain rises to 2,000 m near the Vietnam–Laos border and is mentioned in the poem Tay Tien by Quang Dung. Its summit is a huge, flat rock outcrop projecting into the open air, with sheer cliffs hundreds of metres high and panoramic views of forests across the border in Laos.

listings.name: Bach Long Glass Bridge
listings.address: Muong Sang, Moc Chau, Son La
listings.description: Bach Long Glass Bridge has been recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's longest glass-bottomed bridge, with a total length of 632 m. It consists of a 290 m bridge spanning two mountains and a 342 m cliffside walkway connecting the sections.

listings.name: Bat Cave
listings.address: Bat Cave, Residential Group 7, Moc Son Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: This is a karst cave in a limestone mountain. Local people have known about the cave for a long time, and various legends are associated with it. It was also used as a shelter during the resistance war against the French. Archaeologically, however, it is considered to have been discovered in 1952.

listings.name: Primitive Village, Hang Tau
listings.address: Ta So, Moc Chau, Son La
listings.description: Known as the "primitive village" or the "village of three no's" (no grid electricity, no mobile phone signal, and no internet), it is located about 20 km from the center of Moc Chau town.

listings.name: Tuan Gu Cuisine Restaurant
listings.address: Nguyen Luong Bang Street (National Highway 6), Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: Serves characteristic dishes of Northwest Vietnamese cuisine.

listings.name: Ban Vat Hong Market
listings.address: Ban Vat, Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: Ban Vat Market is located in Ban Vat, Moc Chau, and serves as a gathering place for local residents and visitors on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings each week. The market operates from around 17:30 to 22:00, with stalls selling food, local specialties, and handicrafts. Visitors can sample highland cuisine, watch cultural performances by local villagers, and learn about the traditional way of life of the Thai ethnic community.

listings.name: Moc Chau Island Resort and Bach Long Glass Bridge
listings.address: Na Lun Residential Group, Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: Moc Chau Island Resort & Bach Long Glass Bridge is set amid the dramatic mountains, lush green valleys, and rolling hills of the Moc Chau Plateau. The resort offers a range of accommodation options, including hotel rooms and bungalows, with views of the surrounding natural landscape. The complex also features restaurants, recreational areas, photo spots, and other facilities for visitors seeking accommodation, sightseeing, and photography opportunities.

listings.name: Glenda Tower Moc Chau Hotel
listings.address: 565 Tran Huy Lieu Street, Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: An upscale four-star hotel in the centre of Moc Chau.

listings.name: Thao Nguyen Resort Moc Chau
listings.address: Hoang Quoc Viet Street, Thao Nguyen Ward
listings.description: A large four-star resort spread across a hillside, with nearly 100 detached villas, a year-round heated indoor swimming pool, an outdoor tennis court, a children's play area and a restaurant serving highland cuisine.

listings.name: Mường Thanh Holiday Moc Chau
listings.description: Mường Thanh Holiday Moc Chau is located in the Thao Nguyen area, providing convenient access to the main tourist attractions of the Moc Chau Plateau. The hotel offers comfortable guest rooms, a restaurant serving a variety of dishes, conference and event facilities, and services to support guests during their stay. With its modern design, the hotel is suitable for tourists, families, and business groups.

listings.name: Royal Mausoleums
listings.address: Long Hưng, in Gò Công town
listings.description: The mausoleum complex comprises the tomb of 19th-century duke Pham Dang Hung. The architecture is a blend of Western style, Chinese and traditional Hue.

listings.name: Vinh Trang Pagoda
listings.description: Vinh Trang Pagoda is in a large garden in My Phong Commune. The architecture of the pagoda is a harmonious combination of Asian and European types of architecture, creating the splendid, but simple features of this Buddhist pagoda. Vinh Trang Pagoda is the greatest pagoda of Tien Giang Province.

listings.name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
listings.description: These four brick towers were built by the Cham civilization between the 7th and 12th centuries to honour Yang Ino Po Ngar, mother of the kingdom, and the aroma of incense emanating from within makes it clear that this remains a religious site for the local Buddhists of Nha Trang today. The longevity of these last vestiges of a once-dominant SE Asian civilisation should impress temple enthusiasts even if the insensitive restoration and surrounding mass of tourists don't. The small complex sits on a hill which enjoys views across Nha Trang's fishing village. It is a 20- to 25-min walk (or short…

listings.name: Long Son Pagoda
listings.description: At this pagoda, you will see a 24-m-tall white Buddha. The pagoda was established in 1963 to honour the monks and nuns who died demonstrating against the Diem government. Beware of scammers claiming they are students studying in the temple, demanding that you offer a donation to the school before going up the pagoda. These students have no affiliation with the school and entry to the pagoda is free.

listings.name: Nha Tho Nui Cathedral
listings.description: On a hill overlooking the city, the cathedral shows the influence of French Catholicism. The Nha Trang area still has a strong Catholic population. There are Catholic shops around the cathedral.

listings.name: Alexandre Yersin Museum
listings.description: This is a scientific museum of Swiss-born Dr. Alexandre Yersin (1863-1943), who arrived in Vietnam in 1891 to study infected animals. He later produced a serum from horses and buffaloes. In this museum, you will be able to view all of his work as well as his equipment. Yersin never went back to Switzerland and spent the rest of his life in Nha Trang. Don’t try to take pictures. Do respect the rules as they're quite serious here.

listings.name: Khánh Hòa Museum
listings.description: Exhibition presents Cham statues and artifacts of the ethnic minorities of the Nha Trang area. One of the rooms is devoted to Ho Chi Minh and his personal belongings.

listings.name: National Oceanographic Museum of Vietnam
listings.description: This is like an aquarium with popular and rare species of the sea. A good place to bring kids as they will get to see sharks, turtles, coral reefs, lion fish, sea horses, and many other creatures.

listings.name: Impressions Museum
listings.description: Not really a museum. 3D art paintings to interact with. Great for selfie addicts, but don't go alone! Ideally go as group of 3 or more. Two is OK, but it will be difficult to take photos of the two of you together. Not easy to find, it's on the other side of the old airport from the main tourist area. Receives mixed reviews, many consider it over-priced.

listings.name: Diên Khánh Citadel
listings.description: Citadel was built by French officer Olivier de Puymanel for Nguyễn Ánh in 1793. It housed royal palace, private houses, warehouses and jail. It was fenced by walls of 3.5 m height, surrounded by moats of 4-5 m deep and 10 m wide. It was built with 6 gates, but only 4 of them remain.

listings.name: Fairy Spring waterfalls
listings.price: 10,000 dong per person, 3,000 dong per motorbike
listings.description: Fairy Spring is a small, cool stream and swimming hole much visited by local kids on weekends. The swimming hole is at the end of a short jungle walk. It is a pleasant place to visit in summer. In winter the water is too cold to swim. The stream's source is the area of Hồn Bà, the highest peak in the province. Bottled and canned drinks are available, but no food is sold here yet. The area is slowly being developed and will eventually become a resort with a hotel, bungalows, and restaurant.

listings.name: Ba Ho Waterfalls
listings.description: A series of three waterfalls and a fast flowing river tucked away in the forest. There are limited amenities, although you can buy food like rice, chicken, beers and soft drinks. Taxis are available in Nha Trang to take you there, but it's not too difficult to find yourself and with good weather it's a pleasant drive, if you are confident on a motorbike. It's a good one hour trip from Nha Trang by motorbike through some rough, off-road tracks (especially in the wet season). The turn off from the main highway north of Nha Trang can be easy to miss (a stone pillar), but most locals along the…

listings.name: Hon Ba Nature Reserve
listings.description: At the summit of Hon Ba mountain at 1,514 m above sea level.

listings.name: Monkey Island
listings.description: Catch a ferry to Monkey Island (the pier is 1 km further north of island), which is full of monkeys, has a 10:00 circus and simple go-cart track.

listings.name: Swimming pools
listings.description: People come here to swim in the sea, but there are also a number of swimming pools. Louisiane Brewhouse has a good one that is free to use. Hiring a soft chaise longue costs 40,000 dong. The Yasaka Saigon Nha Trang Hotel coffee shop in Yersin St has a small shady pool for free use. A number of mid-range hotels also have pools, some of which can be used by non-guests. Sea and Sun Hotel has a nice rooftop pool and costs 70,000 dong for non-guests. There is another large public pool at Yersin st, opposite the hospital, for 30,000 dong. Another option is Central Park on Tran Phu, near Louisiane…

listings.name: Water Puppet Theater
listings.description: Water puppetry is a Vietnamese original folk art that dates back as far as the 11th century when it began in the villages of the Red River Delta area of northern Vietnam. Today's Vietnamese water puppetry is a unique variation on the ancient Asian puppet tradition.

listings.name: Gyms
listings.description: There is a large gym in town called Nha Trang Body Building Club, part of a leisure complex that includes badminton and tennis courts, basketball area and football pitch. Daily pass 20,000 dong; monthly pass, 200,000 dong. Besides, Novotel Hotel also has gym memberships for non-guests, which provide access to the swimming pool, sauna and relaxation room. A daily pass costs 200,000 dong, one-month pass 1,400,000 dong, 3-month pass 2,700,000 dong. Monthly passes include one free massage; ask about this when purchasing. The Sheraton Hotel probably has the best gym in town with excellent views,…

listings.name: 10 pin bowling
listings.description: On the 3rd floor of the Nha Trang Centre shopping and entertainment complex.

listings.name: roller blading
listings.description: On the 2nd floor of the Nha Trang Centre, shopping mall.

listings.name: Nha Trang Beach
listings.description: The city's main beach, south of the Cai river, is about 6 km long and lined with a beautiful, well-maintained promenade containing walking paths, gardens, monuments and leisure spaces. The beach itself has a broad strip of sand, and the calm waters are extremely inviting for swimming - but care is needed, as the waters get deep very quickly. While Nha Trang's beach is hardly one of the most beautiful beaches of Southeast Asia, it can still provide one of the best urban beach experiences in the region. You will see many female vendors walking along the beach selling fruit and hot, steamed…

listings.name: Bai Duong Beach
listings.description: North of the Cai river, Bai Duong beach is smaller than in the main tourist area. It is a beautiful beach, but the sewage channels make it somewhat less appealing. The beach is mostly popular among Vietnamese visitors, and hence quite empty during peak sunshine hours. Near the beach there are several seafood restaurants catering to Vietnamese tourists. It can be reached using bus #4.

listings.name: Hon Chong
listings.description: Scenic rock formations in the sea. The disposition of the rocks, as well as the sculpture of a giant fist mark in one of them, is mysterious and a source of several folk tales. You can climb the rocks and get some nice views of Bai Doung Beach and the nearby islands. It can be reached using bus #4.

listings.name: Hòn Tre island
listings.description: Has several nice beaches, but almost of all them are of exclusive access to guests of the Vinpearl resorts. The exception is the small beach in front of the Vinpearl Land's waterpark, which is accessible for those who bought a ticket to Vinpearl Land. The beach offers waterports and contains a Russian restaurant.

listings.name: Doc Let Beach
listings.description: Located in the Ninh Hòa district north of Nha Trang, Doc Let is a beautiful, long beach with shallow, crystal-clear waters. The water has weak waves, but it is still excellent for swimming. Local fisher families sell and prepare seafood they will cook for you on the beach for a very reasonable price. The southern part of the beach contains the Ninh Hòa fishing village, where the north of the beach contains some relatively inexpensive resorts or it still underdeveloped. The best parts of the beach are the ones in front of the resorts, with the rest unfortunately with a lot of rubbish thrown by…

listings.name: Long Beach
listings.description: It's in the Cam Lâm and Cam Ranh districts, 20 km south of Nha Trang. Bai Dai is in the middle of a frenetic process of development, with upscale resorts being built nonstop in the beachfront. Even so, the beach is very long and it is still possible to find yourself alone if you walk enough. It has beautiful blue waters, soft sand and it is pleasant to walk upon as it is less steep than the beach in Nha Trang, but rubbish can also be a problem in areas which are not in the front of resorts. Seafood is served at many shacks with deckchairs right on the beach. Probably best to go by motorcycle.…

listings.name: Vinpearl Amusement Park
listings.price: Adult 600,000 dong; children under 1.4 m tall 450,000 dong; elderly above 60 430,000 dong; children under 1 m: free
listings.description: From the harbour you can take the cable car over to the island where Vinpearl Resort and Vinpearl Land are located. They have a small tivoli and some restaurants, attractions here include Underwater World (aquarium), water park with water slides and wave pool, amusement park with roller coaster, pirate ship, bumper cars, cinema, arcade machines and a laser show at night time, usually 19:00. All included in the one price.

listings.name: 100 Egg Mud Bath
listings.description: Amusement park featuring mud baths, pools, hydrotherapy showers, jacuzzi and a big garden.

listings.name: I-Resort
listings.description: Offers mud and mineral baths, waterfalls and a lot of pools.

listings.name: Thap Ba Hot Springs and Mud baths
listings.price: US4 USD mineral pool, US12.50 USD mudbath
listings.description: Costs 50,000 dong for the hot swimming pool and waterfall, 100,000 dong for shared mud bath (if you are 5-8 people you will probably get put in the same tub), shower, hot/cold water jets, hot Jacuzzi, and the hot waterfalls and swimming pool. A massage by trained masseuses and entrance to the hot swimming pool costs 150,000 dong. There is also a package for 500,000 which included a massage among other extras. A VIP spa package will cost you US100 USD or more. If you carry on a further 500 m past the mud baths you arrive at a railway bridge across the river that connects to a tunnel. It's a…

listings.name: Yang Bay tourist park
listings.description: At the Yang Bay waterfalls the Vietnamese have built up a concrete beach, and sort of eco park with a zoo. It used to be a lot nicer before they built it, but it is still a very nice place to visit. You can swim there, and walk around in the area. Just to mention, tourist park receives a lot of negative reviews.

listings.name: Hòn Tằm
listings.address: Hon Tam island - Vinh Nguyen ward
listings.description: The only mudbath services on island in Vietnam. It takes about 6 minutes from Tam pier to the Hon Tam island by cano. The entrance fee is from 350,000 vnd (15$) for full-package service.

listings.name: Biking and Rafting Tour
listings.description: Combination fast 30-km downhill biking passing through an ethnic village and meeting Raglai people. Then a 12-km rafting trip down the Cai River.

listings.name: Surfing Shack
listings.description: Bar, restaurant and surf club/school.

listings.name: Huyền Hương - Bánh Căn 37
listings.description: A friendly family serving mixed or pure plates of Bánh Căn with 6 pieces and mango salad at no extra charge.

listings.name: Mê Linh 68 - Bánh Hỏi
listings.description: Authentic and inexpensive Bánh Hỏi.

listings.name: Mì Quảng 82
listings.description: Not so authentic dish, but the eatery is very authentic though.

listings.name: Roasted Duck Shop 69
listings.description: Delicious noodles and roasted duck.

listings.name: Bánh Căn Ba Thua
listings.description: Good Bánh Căn, a unique taste, special fish cakes and a delicious cake soup.

listings.name: Ẩm Thực Chay - Bồ Đề Sao
listings.description: Great place for vegetarian dishes.

listings.name: Phở Bò Hà Nội
listings.description: Delicious pho and known for their dishes with rice noodles.

listings.name: Cheers Sports Pub
listings.description: Western home style food and big TVs to watch sport events.

listings.name: Lac Canh
listings.description: What’s different about this long established restaurant (25 years) is that you get to cook, yourself, and both locals and tourists seem to love it. It's famous for its thinly sliced beef, marinated in chilli source that you cook with your own mini tabletop BBQ. Large San Miguel bottled beers are served by San Miguel-attired servers for 18,000 dong.

listings.name: Truc Linh 2
listings.description: Asian and Western food. Especially popular for seafood. Truc Linh has been here for years but the original corner one is now the location of a new high rise hotel.

listings.name: Nha Trang Seafood
listings.description: Serves fresh and scrumptious seafood. Inexpensive prices and good service.

listings.name: Louisiane Brewhouse
listings.description: Microbrewery with locally brewed beers, restaurant with fresh cakes and tarts, sushi, quality pizzas, steaks, Vietnamese food and seafood. Pool table, live music and own loungers right at the beach or pool available. Chaises longues at either the pool or beach are 40,000 dong per day. Even if you get a chair on the beach, you still have pool access. They have a sampling tray of beer for 100,000 dong.

listings.name: Sailing Club
listings.description: This restaurant serves Japanese, Indian, Vietnamese, and Italian food. Crowded at night, when it turns into bar.

listings.name: Alley Cafe
listings.description: Cheap drinking bar and cafe popular with English-speaking expats.

listings.name: Altitude Rooftop Bar
listings.description: For a great view of Nha Trang at night, perhaps visit the second highest bar in Nha Trang.

listings.name: Skylight Nha Trang
listings.price: Entrance 50,000-250,000 dong depending on time and day of the week, price includes 1 drink
listings.description: 360˚ skydeck & rooftop club. Besides, it also features a skywalk, pool deck and an international restaurant - Chef's Club on the 43rd floor.

listings.name: Crazy Kim Bar
listings.description: If you are young and wild, this is the place to be.

listings.name: SinhTo20
listings.description: This place has a very good yoghurt and many kinds of cocktails. Prices are reasonable.

listings.name: Why Not Bar
listings.description: Long-running and still one of the most popular late night bars for the young Western backpacker crowd in Nha Trang. It's been transformed into a much more upmarket establishment and is more popular with Asian tourists.

listings.name: Sữa hạt Green-T
listings.address: 36/1 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, phường Vĩnh Hòa, thành phố Nha Trang
listings.description: Green T nut milk is made entirely from nature with nuts: Lotus, Walnut, Cashew, Sesame, Almond, bringing the whole thing, suitable for everyone in the family. Green T nut milk is made with all hearts and enthusiasm with the desire to bring quality, complementary and safe products to everyone in the family, especially children and adults.

listings.name: Alpaca Coffee
listings.description: A small homestyle cafe with a good-quality Italian and Mediterranean food and drinks. They also have vegetarian and healthy food. Located upstairs above the green A-mart store. 20% off drinks when ordered with a meal. Its more of an eating place and often gets full, so the drinks discount is probably there to deter customers just buying drinks only.

listings.name: Iced Coffee
listings.description: Coffee shop in similar style to the large chains such as Starbucks and Costa Coffee, i.e. espresso styles, lots of comfy seating inside and out with upstairs seating too. They also sell cakes and pastries and have a small food menu too.

listings.name: Lava Coffee
listings.description: More of a Vietnamese-style coffee shop but with both comfortable air-con and alfresco dining areas.

listings.name: Azura Gold Hotel
listings.description: Great new hotel close to the beach, has small pool and gym with massage chair on the 10th floor. 9 floors with 6 rooms per floor and 2 elevators. Wi-Fi and TV in the rooms, some of which have ocean views. Staff speak good English here.

listings.name: Blue Star Hotel
listings.description: Old mini hotel close to the beach. Six floors with an elevator.. Wi-Fi for the rooms, some of which have ocean views.

listings.name: Ha Tram Hotel
listings.description: In mini hotel alley, close to beach and main tourist area in quiet and safe location. All rooms have air-con, en suite with hot water, cable TV, Wi-Fi and fridge. Hotel has 15 rooms on 6 floors and has an elevator.

listings.name: Khách Sạn Hồng Hà
listings.description: Six floors with elevator. Free and good Wi-Fi for the rooms. Staff sleeping in the lobby for 24/7 access. Sometimes issues with charges for damages to the room that are pre-existing.

listings.name: Nha Khach Thai Nguyen Guest House
listings.description: Not far from the beach, the owner is a nice and friendly woman. While you stay there she will make you feel at home, if you want to share local life. Free coffee, free Wi-Fi and cable TV.

listings.name: Nha Trang Inn & Suites
listings.description: Elevator, free Wi-Fi, free HBO in every room. Conveniently close to the bus stations Phuong Nam and Phuong Trang so can transit easily to other city. The manager speaks English and Czech. This place has changed its name in 2015.

listings.name: Pho Bien Hotel
listings.description: Renovated in 2014, in mini hotel, all 19 private rooms have air-con, en suite, cable TV, fridge and Wi-Fi. This place is clean and has a terrific location. Room 503 (double) has a big balcony with fabulous sea views. They also have a dorm room with 2 separate bathrooms and adjacent rooftop terrace with sea views.

listings.name: La Suisse Hotel
listings.description: It has Internet access including Wi-Fi in all rooms and three computers in the reception area. They have an elevator. Free breakfast included in their rooftop lounge. Free pick up from train and bus stations with own minivan.

listings.name: Sami Hotel
listings.description: Mini hotel refurbished in 2019, has 15 en-suite rooms with air-con, cable TV, wifi, fridge and telephone.

listings.name: Thanh Ngoc 2
listings.description: All rooms equipped with TV, air-con and spacious beds.

listings.name: Truong Giang hotel
listings.description: A budget hotel with essential amenities and facilities. Quiet and clean.

listings.name: Cozy Condos and Apartments
listings.description: For those who prefer a cosy home to a hotel room, this is the place to stay. Close to city centre and beach, quiet and safe location (near Military Hospital). Single rooms with large double beds, living room, kitchen and balcony. Fully equipped, including large refrigerator, oven, micro wave oven, kitchenware, in-room safe, washing machine with separate drying area. etc. Wi-Fi, domestic phone calls and international TV channels free of charge. 24-hour security, guarded parking lot, elevator, café bar on top of building.

listings.name: Nha Trang Lodge Hotel
listings.description: Most rooms overlook the beach giving you an extraordinary sea views. Rooms are equipped with phones, satellite TV, a minibar, etc. Service is great.

listings.name: Que Huong Hotel
listings.description: Within walking distance of the beach. There is a nice restaurant accompanied by a pool hall and disco. Great amenities offered as well as the services. Average quality as per internet reviews.

listings.name: Starlet Hotel
listings.description: This place has a bit of a business feel, but its very clean rooms have classy, attractive decor, if lacking a bit in character. Many of the rooms offer balconies with fantastic city and sea views, its location is great, and the included breakfast buffet is nothing to turn your nose up at. There is free Wi-Fi in the rooms, a good selection of reasonably priced room service, and it has a pool and gym. The staff is very friendly, and you can change foreign currency at the front desk at decent rates.

listings.name: Vien Dong Hotel
listings.description: Well-known and affordable, with all the basic amenities needed plus some live entertainment at night.

listings.name: Citadines Bayfront Nha Trang
listings.description: Offers 310 studio and one-bedroom apartments. The property has a restaurant and bar, outdoor swimming pool, gym and yoga room.

listings.name: Evason Ana Mandara & Six Senses Spa
listings.description: If you don’t mind the price, this is the spot to go all out and get the once-in-a-lifetime royal treatment.

listings.name: Diamond Bay Resort & Spa Nha Trang
listings.description: This extremely spaciously laid-out resort hosted the 2008 Miss Universe pageant. Hotel rooms, suites and villas. Enormous pool (non-chlorinated) spa, fitness, several restaurants & bars, tennis, expatriate chef and expatriate GM. Two private beaches.

listings.name: Novotel
listings.description: Luxury hotel. Awesome staff, food, room, Internet. Small pool, but the ocean is less than 100 m away.

listings.name: Sheraton Nha Trang Hotel & Spa
listings.description: Luxury hotel with swimming pool, gym and open air bar on 28th floor with great views across Nha Trang beachfront.

listings.name: Sunrise Nha Trang Beach Hotel & Spa
listings.description: This resort is all polished marble and white columns with 10 floors. It has a great view of ocean-side as well as the sky from its glass rooftop.

listings.name: Vinpearl Resort
listings.description: Luxury hotel with the biggest pool in Vietnam. Guests have unlimited access to the water park.

listings.name: Yasaka Saigon-NhaTrang Hotel
listings.description: Japanese/Vietnamese hotel. Service here is very friendly, and it has all the amenities you would need. It is just walking distance to the beach.

listings.name: Liberty Central
listings.description: 4-star modern hotel with 227 guest rooms over 20 floors with sea views. Has a good buffer breakfast for 180k dong.

listings.name: Doc Let Beach Resort
listings.price: 250,000-420,000 dong depending on how close to the beach they are
listings.description: The best-known place and closest to the mainland. Though it started out as a traveller's secret, it quickly became a destination for domestic tourists, especially during weekends and holidays. If you take a Vietnamese partner, they won't let you stay in the same room unless you can prove you are married.

listings.name: Jungle Beach Resort
listings.price: US25 USD including meals for rooms with shared bath; US35 USD including meals for rooms with a private bath
listings.description: Run by a Canadian-Vietnamese couple, all meals are included. If you are looking for a beautiful beach in a very remote and quiet location then this could be your paradise. Keep in mind that they don't have hot water here. This resort also charges US20 USD for transportation each way. Extra drinks will cost from 15,000-20,000 dong.

listings.name: Paradise Resort
listings.price: Bungalows are US45 USD for 2 people, US25 USD for one. Meals included, and prices for drinks are reasonable. Water, fruits, coffee and tea are free.
listings.description: Run by an elderly gentleman and his Vietnamese family. Vladimir is a very interesting, jovial guy and his family cooks up wonderful food. Beer is cheap, and you just mark a chit on a sheet on the refrigerator to keep track of your total. The beach in front is beautiful and usually deserted except for some village children. It is very easy to sleep a week away there in a hammock kissed by sea breezes. There is usually various travellers there to socialise with at meals and in the evenings. You can rent a motorbike in Nha Trang for the easy ride up to Doc Let. Any buses can also drop you on the…

listings.name: White Sand Doclet Resort & Spa
listings.description: Adjacent to Doc Let Resort is this more upmarket resort with private beach, large swimming pool, gym, spa, restaurant.

listings.name: Six Senses Ninh Van Bay
listings.description: Private resort, suitable for whomever wants to get away from everything.

listings.name: Memento Resort
listings.description: In the middle of the rice fields you will find this little family-owned resort. If you like a traquil place and want to enjoy the countryside, then this is the place for you. They also have a swimming pool. Based on reviews, people in general like this place.

listings.name: Bich Dong Pagoda
listings.price: Free. Parking 20,000 dong, or free on the square in front of the entrance bridge if you buy a drink for 25,000 dong, or leave the bike farther away from the entrance. The lady charging the fee may try to overcharge by implying that it also includes the entrance to the temples, but this is a lie
listings.description: Three temples carved into a limestone mountain, dating from the 15th-century reign of Le Thai To. The lower temple has a stone next to it that resonates when tapped, plus a Buddha footprint. The middle temple has an 18th-century bell, a cave and resonating pillars. The top temple has a view of the surrounding countryside, which is good for sunsets.

listings.name: Hidden Valley (Secret Cave)
listings.price: Cave tour 30,000 dong, boat tour 50,000 dong
listings.description: Only very few tourists wander into this secluded valley. There is a shop selling some drinks and ice cream, but which might be closed. There is a boat advertising a tour into a 350m deep cave, a wide peaceful field with some goats and then there is the 15min walking tour through a cave. The guide babbles about in Vietnamese only, shows various fossil shells and funny shaped wall markings, stalagmites and stalactites and even turns your head into the right direction to look using his hands.

listings.name: Mua Cave
listings.price: 100,000 dong entrance fee + 10,000 dong bicycle/motorbike parking fee
listings.description: The cave here is an afterthought; the main draws are the two hilltop viewpoints. 500 steps will lead you to the first peak, an unimpressive temple with incredibly stunning views over Tam Coc and Ninh Binh’s countryside, including a large lotus flower field at the bottom (should bloom in June/July). On the second slightly higher peak, there is a long dragon statue which you can climb around. Caution when arriving by bike or motorbike: On the street leading up to the entrance gate there are multiple places trying to convince you that they're the official parking spot, some even utilizing…

listings.name: Thung Nham Bird Park
listings.address: Hai Nham, Ninh Hai, Tam Coc
listings.description: Entrance ticket includes two boat rides, one in a cave with sleeping bats and one to the conservation bird park. Some very beautiful flower gardens, tree areas and bamboo bridges. You are allowed to bring your own bicycle inside and cycle around. Useful too as its about 1.3km from ticket office to park entrance with a steep hill to get over.

listings.name: Dundj Valley
listings.description: A quieter limestone valley located beyond the main tourist routes of Tam Coc, with rice fields, small waterways, and surrounding karst formations. The area is characterized by a rural landscape where visitors may encounter farming activities, grazing animals, and narrow paths connecting small plots of land. In some parts of the valley, waterways extend into natural cave sections, including a longer water cave noted locally for its clear water and its connection between areas of the valley. The surroundings include a mix of open fields, forested sections, and agricultural land, offering a more…

listings.name: Tam Coc Museum
listings.description: A small museum presenting aspects of traditional Vietnamese rural life. Exhibits include rice cultivation, grain processing, and traditional tools used in farming communities.

listings.name: Bai Dinh Temple
listings.hours: 07:00 to 20:00, entrance to the large tower until 17:00
listings.price: Free entrance, motorbike parking 15,000 dong, shuttle e-mobiles with fee
listings.description: Huge Buddhist complex, the largest in Vietnam, with the largest pagoda tower of Vietnam (100 m high, has elevator). Most of it was built between 2003 and 2010, so it's in exceptionally good shape. A visit can easily take 4 hours due to the sheer size of the complex. At night, most buildings are lit up, creating absolutely magnificent sights. Access is free but notoriously difficult without taking a shuttle e-mobile from the parking lot, because the parking lot is 3 km from the entrance, at the completely opposite end of the precincts. For the shuttles, there are several options. If you want…

listings.name: Hoa Lu Ancient Capital
listings.price: 20,000 dong. Entrance to Xuyen Thuy cave is 15,000 dong
listings.description: The ancient capital during Dinh (968-80) and Le dynasties (980-1009). Little remains from this period, but there are a few large temples and monuments built from the 1600s on: the temple of Dinh Tien Hoang, the temple of King Le Dai Hahn, Nhat Tru Pagoda, and on top of a hill, Dinh Tien Hoang's tomb. Consider a guide, as there is little interpretive information (or even useful maps) onsite. There are also boat trips on the river to Xuyen Thuy cave, less spectacular than other caves in the area.

listings.name: Khe Coc Island
listings.price: 20,000 dong, 300,000 dong combo ticket with Trang An
listings.description: The former filming location of the village from Kong: Skull Island, repurposed in 2024 as an outdoor cultural museum. There isn't much there yet.

listings.name: Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh
listings.address: Cuc Phuong - Bai Dinh Rd, Ky Phu commune, Nho Quan district
listings.description: It was built by the animal welfare organisation Four Paws opened for visitors in 2019. It covers 5.5 ha, and plans to expand to 10 ha and open an education centre. Different from other sanctuaries, visitors will not be able to enter the whole sanctuary. A path leads the visitors above some enclosures to allow them to observe the bears from a distance.

listings.name: Phat Diem Cathedral
listings.description: Cathedral known for its scale and its oriental style. Completed in 1891. One of the earliest areas to be reached by missionaries; Portuguese priests were here in 1627.

listings.name: Tam Coc
listings.hours: Daily, last boat starts at 17:30 summer, 16:30 winter
listings.price: 150,000 dong per boat (maximum 2 foreigners per boat), plus admission of 120,000 dong per person
listings.description: The most famous landscape of Ninh Binh. Boats begin at the village of Van Lam and proceed through a scenic landscape dominated by rice fields and karst towers. The route includes floating through three natural caves (Hang Cả, Hang Hai, and Hang Ba), the largest of which is 125-m long with its ceiling about 2-m high above the water. Vast limestone cliffs rise out of the rice paddies.

listings.name: Trang An
listings.price: 250,000 dong. Parking fee of 15,000 dong for motorbikes or free for bicycles
listings.description: The most extensive waterway tour in Ninh Binh. Many tourists prefer this trip to Tam Coc as there are many more caves to pass through and not as many hawkers. After buying a ticket, find your way to the boarding area, and decide on your route. (Do not agonize over your decision, as each route includes plenty of temples, caves, and landscapes.) Each is about 3 hours, so make sure to carry sun protection, water and some nibbles (restrooms are available at each temple stop). An employee will pair you to a boat with a rower, and fill the boat with about four passengers (smaller parties will be…

listings.name: Trung Tuyet Restaurant
listings.description: A few tables on the street and one of the few restaurants in the city that caters to Westerners. The menu offers 3 or 4 sizes of portions at different prices, however even the small sized portions are larger than in other towns. Coffee 20,000 dong, Fruit salad 30,000 dong. Yogurt 8,000 dong. Chicken with noodles 50,000 dong.

listings.name: Pho bò 24
listings.description: A small restaurant for locals with the food cooked in front of you. A few tables on the street and few inside. Soups and noodle for 25,000 dong and 30,000 dong. Have an English menu.

listings.name: Aroma Indian Restaurant
listings.description: Indian restaurant which is one of the few in town to have air-con. Excellent Indian food and snappy service. Enormous nan breads! Very reasonable prices given the quality.

listings.name: Chookie's Beer Garden
listings.description: Great place to relax and have a drink and something to eat away from the main street. Good burgers, salads and Smoothies. Plenty of vegan options too. Has a nice veggie garden and play area. The have another outlet called Chookie Coop, near Mua Cave.

listings.name: Thang Long Restaurant
listings.address: Chi Phong hamlet, Tay Hoa Lu
listings.description: Large restaurant serving local mountain goat dishes, com chay (crispy rice) and hill chicken. Several big dining halls take tour groups, and there is a car park. Set menus can be arranged in advance.

listings.name: Green Papaya Home Stay
listings.address: Ngo 212, No. 54 (still listed on Google as Van Thanh No. 54)

listings.name: Ngoc Anh Hotel
listings.description: Family hotel, friendly staff, good location, rooms are clean, all rooms have air-con, en suite bath, cable TV with good reception, Wi-Fi. Deluxe rooms also have a computer, a fridge and balcony. There are 2 modern computers in the reception/restaurant area. The cheaper rooms are at 26 Luong Van Tuy and the more expensive at 30 Luong Van Tuy.

listings.name: Queen Mini Hotel
listings.description: Near the train and bus station. It's popular, especially with French visitors, and often full. Rooms are clean enough, but can have insects. Wi-Fi in the lobby, but it doesn't reach all the rooms. The owner's refrain is "You pay now". They are affiliated with the Good Food Restaurant across the street. Be warned: there are four hotels sharing this name, and it's not clear if all of them are related: The Queen Mini (this one), the Queen Hotel (across the street, upscale and owned by the same family as the Queen Mini), the New Queen Mini Backpacker's Hostel (on the same street, often has grille…

listings.name: Thanh Binh Hotel
listings.description: Some members of the staff are somewhat helpful and friendly. Possibility to rent motorbikes for USD6/day. Breakfast is not included.

listings.name: Po Klong Garai Temple
listings.description: A Hindu Cham religious complex built towards the end of the 13th century. The temple is architecturally in the Thap Mam style.

listings.name: Ninh Thuận Museum
listings.address: Mười Sáu Tháng Tư, Kinh Dinh
listings.description: A museum showcasing Vietnam's modern history.

listings.name: April 16th Park
listings.description: A prominent public space in the heart of the city. The park features a lake and many green spaces which people use for recreation, exercise and just enjoying the fresh air.

listings.name: Binh Son sea park
listings.description: A spacious coastal area where visitors can swim, stroll, and take photos among the lawns, flower gardens, and stone-paved walkways.

listings.name: Sorrento Beach Club Vietnam and Kite Centre
listings.address: Ninh Hai Phan Rang, Thap Cham, My Hoa
listings.description: Serves both Vietnamese and international cuisine.

listings.name: Chu Ngo Chicken Rice
listings.description: Serves chicken rice, pork rice, chicken pho and other dishes.

listings.name: Huong Bien Guesthouse & Hotel
listings.description: Clean guesthouse further along the road once it has turned to dirt past the Sai Gon - Ninh Chu Hotel in Ninh Chu. As of June 2012 the owners were building a brand new extension next door with some rooms available.

listings.name: Sai Gon - Ninh Chu Hotel
listings.address: 19 An Dương Vương, TT. Khánh Hải, Ninh Hải
listings.description: A 4-star Ninh Chu beach branch of the Sai Gon hotel chain. Has more than 120 rooms.

listings.name: Vạn Thủy Tú temple
listings.description: A whale worship/cult temple that is a tradition among the Vietnamese fishing community.

listings.name: Mom's Bun Dau 62 pieces
listings.description: They serve a mixed meat platter which is very popular with the locals and comes at an incredible price. You enjoy it just with strong fish sauce or roll the available pieces and salad into rice paper and dip it into sweet, salty sauce. (Use the cucumber pieces to make the rice paper moist a little, so it can be rolled better.).

listings.name: Street Coffee
listings.description: Cà Phê Đen for 12,000 dong.

tieu_de: Vườn quốc gia Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng
Vườn quốc gia Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng
Vườn quốc gia Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng

listings.name: General museum of Quảng Ngãi Province
listings.description: Contains cultural artifacts of Sa Huynh & Champa civilizations, and other ethnic minorities of Quẚng Ngãi Province.

listings.name: Ly Son Island
listings.description: Ly Son Island is 26 km (14 nautical miles) from Sa Ky Port. The island is about 10 km² and known as the Garlic Capital of Central Vietnam. There are traces of the ancient Sa Huynh and Champa cultures on the island. The local people live by farming and fishing. There are several beautiful spots on the island such as Cave Pagoda, An Hai Village temple, Hoang Sa Museum, and two volcanic mouths Gieng Tien and Thoi Loi.

listings.name: My Khe Beach
listings.description: My Khe Beach is one of the best beaches in Quẚng Ngãi. It is about 8 km long with fine, white, and smooth powdery sands. Behind the beach is a green poplar forest creating a green space of hundreds hectares running along the internal tourist area. My Khe Tourist Resort is in this area. There are several food stalls erected along the beach, catering mostly to locals. This beach has yet to experience the rapid developments that plagued other resort areas in Vietnam.

listings.name: Mỹ Lai Massacre Memorial Museum
listings.description: A memorial to 504 victims killed in 1969 by US forces in the My Lai incident. The site is a solemn place and also the main reason foreign visitors choose to stop by this province. To get to the museum is easy; you just need to take the local bus (line: SAKI) from Quang Ngai downtown, in front of the Hotel Khách Sạn Hùng Vương (address: 45 Hùng Vương, tp. Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Ngãi, Vietnam). This 15-20 minute trip will cost 10,000 dong each way (Dec 2015).

listings.name: Sa Huynh Beach
listings.description: Sa Huynh is a beautiful beach with clear water and golden sand. Sa Huynh is also called Sa Hoang, means "gold sand" as the color of the sand is not white like some other places but is a glittered yellow sand. A popular stopover location for travelers to spend a few days on the beach, bordered by coconut groves and rice paddies, before continuing their journey.

listings.name: The Long Wall of Quẚng Ngãi
listings.description: A version of the Hadrian's Wall. Discovered in 2005, the Long Wall of Quẚng Ngãi is a majestic architectural construction that remains in its original state. Built over 500 years mainly with stones and earth, with an average high of 2 m, the wall spans over 113 km with several forts, roads, and military depots. The Wall was constructed in the early days by the Viet settlers when this region was Vietnam southern frontier. It later was upgraded and fortified by the Nguyen Emperors. The wall was built to regulate trade and defense with the hostile Champa civilization in the south.

listings.name: Thien An Mountain
listings.description: Squared in shape likes a seal hence the name Thien An (Heaven's Seal). This small mountain is revered by the locals as a spiritual place. A three-century-old pagoda sits near the top and at the summit is the tomb of the region's famous anti-colonial hero Huynh Thuc Khang.

listings.name: Thien But Mountain
