listings.description: Travelers to Quẚng Ngãi often inquired about Thien But Mountain along with its higher cousin Thien An Mountain. However, Thien But Mountain is more renowned in poetry rather than in reality. A small hill that rises 60 m high above the coastal plains. On a clouds covered day, Thien But Mountain looks like a calligraphy brush with its tip dipped into the clouds hence the name Thien But (Heaven's Brush). If visiting on a cloudy day, one can take a look to see whether Thien But Mountain is as poetically described. If so, then it is truly a spectacular treat.

listings.name: Bike ride Co Luy Commune
listings.description: Visitors often ask where Co Luy Commune is. This area was once renowned in poetry and claimed to be second only to Hue for its bucolic, rustic rural charms. The area is slowly giving way to development. However, one can still find its coconut groves, its swaying pine trees, and meandering streams. Folks come here just to see whether it is as described in the poetry they once heard in schools. Some riverside cafes have popped up along the rivers to take advantage of the place's new-found attraction.

listings.name: Ngoc Anh Hotel
listings.description: Centrally located in downtown (near restaurants, and shops), hot shower, TV, WiFi, A/C, motorbike available for rent

listings.name: Dong Hung Hotel
listings.description: short walk from the bus station, wifi on every floor, A/C, hot shower, TV, fridge (of course everything disconnects when you unplug the key), many stairs to climb.

listings.name: Cocoland River Beach Resort & Spa
listings.description: 4-star resort by the ancient port.

listings.name: Petro-Song Tra Hotel
listings.description: Has room service, a concierge and a cafe.

listings.name: Khach San Phuc Hung
listings.address: 44-45 Lạc Hồng, Vĩnh Lạc, Rạch Giá, tỉnh Kiên Giang, Vietnam
listings.price: 350,000 dong for standard aircon double, 550,000 dong for VIP double
listings.description: A nice place near the ocean. No views. Free WiFi with a free computer in the lobby as well. Rooms are nice, brand new and have a flat panel TV. Map is on the website.

listings.name: Lang Du Inn
listings.description: double room with own bathroom.

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary
listings.description: A Roman Catholic church established by the French and constructed between 1926 and 1935. Mass is held on weekdays at 19:00 and on Sunday at 09:00, and the adoration of the sacrament is held at 18:30.

listings.name: Hàm Rồng Resort
listings.description: A hillside attraction with great views and various gardens such as an orchid garden and a European garden, ethnic minority dance performances, and restaurants.

listings.name: Sa Pa Culture Museum
listings.description: If you have time, the museum is worth visiting to learn about the history of Sa Pa, and the costumes and traditions of the ethnic minorities of the region.

listings.name: Sa Pa Square
listings.description: The square is hard to miss. It is a centre of local activity. Often in the evenings, you may see the locals gather for shopping and selling, or playing a game of foot-badminton in groups. You may see dances in the square.

listings.name: Cát Cát village
listings.price: Admission: 70,000 dong, 30,000 dong for children under 10 year-old
listings.description: This walk provides a good chance to observe Vietnamese farming and farm animals, and there are excellent views. It's a few kilometers' walk from Sa Pa. You're not likely to get lost: just walk down the road out of Sa Pa, which should be marked on maps. After a while, you'll find a path which descends the hill to your left. This path runs through the village before climbing another hill back to the road. The walk back up can be difficult (it is steep in parts), but once you get back onto the road there are plenty of enterprising locals ready to take you back to Sa Pa on motorbikes (40,000 dong…

listings.name: Hoàng Liên National Park, Love Waterfall and Silver Waterfall
listings.price: Hoàng Liên National Park: 70,000 dong; Silver Waterfall: 20,000 dong
listings.description: Love Waterfall (Thác Tình Yêu), which lies within (Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên; declared an ). It takes 30 minutes to walk from the entrance of the park to the waterfall. The path is paved with flat but slightly uneven stones and has many steps going up and down. there are many shaded areas for rest along the way. Silver Waterfall (Thác Bạc), regarded by some travellers as less picturesque than Love Waterfall, is alongside the road between Sa Pa and the entrance to Hoàng Liên National Park. You have to take a few hundred steps up to see the waterfall.

listings.name: Massage
listings.description: Numerous shops along Cầu Mây Street, the town's main street, provide foot and body massages. Many hotels also offer in-room massages.

listings.name: Phan Si Păng
listings.description: At 3,143 m (10,312 ft), Phan Si Păng or Fansipan is the highest mountain in (Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam), and lies within the Hoàng Liên National Park (Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên). Hikes to the summit lasting from 1-3 days can be arranged from tour companies in Sa Pa. Most of them recommend taking the 2- or 3-day options; few guides will take tourists on the round trip in a single day. A very small village offering accommodation and food is around 1,500 m (4,920 ft), and there is an overnight camp at 2,800 m (9,190 ft). Most booked trips will include the use of these facilities in their price…

listings.name: Fansipan Legend
listings.price: 750,000 dong, 550,000 dong for children between 1 and 1.4 m; 100,000 dong for the funicular from Sapa Town (Hotel Coupole) to the Moang Hoa cable car station; 70,000 dong for the funicular from the cable car to the peak
listings.description: The cable car up Fansipan offering a rather less strenuous route up the tallest mountain in Indochina. The views are often obscured by the fog.

listings.name: Paragliding over Mường Hoa Valley
listings.description: Tandem paragliding flights with an experienced pilot over the rice terraces of Mường Hoa Valley; no previous experience is needed. The best time is the rice season: the terraces are bright green in July and August, then turn yellow from late August, and by September and early October much of the valley is golden just before harvest. From the air you can follow the curves of the terraces around the hills, with Hmong and Dao villages and the Mường Hoa river below. Flights at other times of year are possible but the fields are less striking. Flights depend on wind and weather and may be…

listings.name: Sa Pa Lake
listings.description: The lake is within walking distance of the city center. At the lake you can rent a pedal boat for 40,000 dong for 30 minutes, or 80,000 dong for an hour. Pedal boats are available only on weekends and when the weather is good.

listings.name: The Hill Station Signature
listings.description: Refined local (mostly Hmong) food in small dishes - the speciality, if they have found fresh fish that day, is their raw trout. Perched on the edge of the valley, some tables have views right across it. A few decent options for vegetarians.

listings.name: The Hill Station Deli
listings.description: Fine wine, cheese and cold cuts of meat along with a few western style hot and cold dishes. Home-made hams and pâté. Punto Italia coffee.

listings.name: Little View Restaurant
listings.description: A popular, low-priced restaurant. Serves outstanding local and decent Western dishes to a mixed local and foreign clientele. Features some unique dishes in addition to the fixtures available at any other Sa Pa restaurant. Try the hot pot with salmon.

listings.name: Marketplace food stalls
listings.description: Food stalls selling good noodle soup for 10,000 dong, fried rice for 15,000 dong and the other usual Vietnamese fare for around 30,000 dong. It's a great experience to dine with the locals.

listings.name: Rose Garden Sa Pa
listings.description: A mid-range restaurant. They have freshly baked baguettes and hamburgers from their own bakery. The desserts, ice cream, cakes, and cookies, are sweet delicacies at an affordable price.

listings.name: Hoa Tam Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.description: One of the rare vegetarian restaurants in town, hidden in a small street close to the church, down the stairs.

listings.name: Hmong Sisters Bar
listings.description: Has a pool table, darts and a computer with free Internet.

listings.name: Cong Caphe
listings.description: Coffee place that also serves some food. Lots of drinks available: coffee, tea, coconut milk (the one with coffee being their signature drink), yoghurt & beer. Food includes pizza, cocooned sweet potato & bamboo-cooked rice. Nice chilling atmosphere (thanks to the music & quite big space available). Staff speak decent English. While drinks & food are modern, entering the place you feel like you've travelled back in time thanks to the outfits worn by the staff, and the old newspapers & books. Live music on Friday, Saturday & Sunday nights (19:00-23:00). Happy hour everyday from 17:00 to 20:00…

listings.name: Chau Long Sapa Hotel
listings.description: A large hotel with clean, pleasant rooms that is popular with group tours. It has a restaurant, lounge and bar, an indoor heated swimming pool, a fitness centre, and a business centre. Rooms in the old wing are cheaper. No additional charge for Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Fansipan View Hotel
listings.description: A nice relaxing hotel with boutique interiors.

listings.name: Green Bamboo Sa Pa
listings.description: It serves a cheap and good breakfast at USD2.50. Rooms in the main and old wings of the hotel which are above the ground floors offer breathtaking views of the Fanxipan mountains.

listings.name: Pistachio Hotel
listings.description: In contemporary European architecture style, the upper floors have beautiful views of the hills and valleys. Amenities include a spa, gym, pool, karaoke room and bar.

listings.name: Lotus Hotel
listings.description: Nice rooms, tea, TV, hot water, restaurant and for some rooms, a fireplace and a nice view. The staff are a little cold. Hotel closes each night at 23:00.

listings.name: Pumpkin Hotel
listings.description: Very friendly and helpful staff. Good-sized rooms with desks and computers. The hotel may try to charge extra for a space heater for 150,000 dong. If you are staying here as a part of an ET Pumpkin tour, make sure to get an assurance (in writing, if possible) that your space heater will be included in the price.

listings.name: The Royal Hotel
listings.description: Some rooms provide a nice view over the valley or the town, and many open on to a small balcony. It has an attached café offering standard back-packer fare such as banana or chocolate pancakes. Can help with travel arrangements.

listings.name: Sapa Paradise View Hotel
listings.description: A good value three-star hotel. The décor is nothing to scream about but the rooms are comfortable, clean and well-stocked. Some of them have an interesting aerial view of the village. Breakfast is usually included in the cost of the room, and the hotel provides a complimentary fruit basket, bottles of water, a daily afternoon smoothie and snack, Wi-Fi (including a desktop computer in the room), and boots for hiking. The staff are attentive and friendly. In-room massages can be arranged. The four-story hotel does not have any lifts, but the staff will help carry your luggage.

listings.name: Thai Binh Sa Pa Hotel
listings.description: In a quiet part of Sa Pa and within five minutes' walk of the market and restaurant street. Free Internet in the lobby and Wi-Fi in rooms. Electric heater and electric mattress available in the room. The hotel manager, a local teacher and education officer, and the female receptionist are very friendly and speak good English. They are able to book local tours, buy train tickets at Lào Cai train station for you, and transport you to and from the train station.

listings.name: Topas Eco Lodge
listings.price: About USD99 per night for a detached bungalow
listings.description: Perched on beautiful grounds on a hill with stunning views of the surrounding valley. Spacious, detached bungalows, each with its own balcony, which can be a comfortable double or accommodate a small family. The "eco" part of the title comes partly through the lodge hiring local staff and using solar power and hot water in all the bungalows.

listings.name: Little View Homestay
listings.description: Good value home stay at USD17 per night. New building has great views and balconies with shared area on the top floor. Very clean. Hard beds. Friendly owners who speak good English. You need to walk down a lot of stairs to reach the homestay. Follow the main tourist street (Ngõ Cầu Mây) to the end where the motorbike parking is, walk down the stairs and follow the signs.

listings.name: People's Committee Hall
listings.description: Built as the Hôtel de Ville, it's a striking cream and yellow French colonial building beautifully floodlit at night. No entry, but the statue of Uncle Ho in front is a very popular place for photos.

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh Museum
listings.description: The museum, housed in a French colonial-era building, narrates the history of Ho Chi Minh City from pre-history to the present and also has exhibits on local culture and traditions. Outside, on the museum grounds, you will find cars and military vehicles of historical significance. The museum also relates the life of the modern-day father of Vietnam. The exhibits include various personal possessions of Ho Chi Minh but are mainly photographs. You may find it a little jingoistic.

listings.name: Museum of Vietnamese History
listings.address: 2 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1
listings.description: The museum has a fine collection of Vietnamese antiquities. Read up on Vietnamese history first or you'll have no idea what you're looking at. Outside, the Botanical Gardens are very nice and a good place for a cheap lunch away from the crowds. Six times a day, you can see a 20-minute water puppet show (adult 50,000 dong, child 35,000 dong). It's quite amusing, even for adults.

listings.name: Independence Palace
listings.description: This is a restored 4-floor time warp to the 1960s left largely untouched from the day Saigon fell to the North; construction started in 1962 and finished in 1966. It was South Vietnam's presidential palace. The war ended on 30 Apr 1975 when Tank 843 crashed through the gate. A replica of that tank is now parked on the lawn outside. Be sure to check out the aggressively 1960s recreation room on the third floor, featuring a circular sofa, and the eerie basement, full of vintage 1960s phones, radios and office equipment, supposedly left exactly as it was found when the North took over. There is…

listings.name: War Remnants Museum
listings.description: The museum was opened in a hurry, less than five months after the fall of the South Vietnamese regime. It has moved to new premises with 3 storeys of exhibits and various US military hardware (tanks, jets, helicopters, howitzers) on display outside the building. This disturbing display of man's cruelty during the Vietnam (American) War includes halls full of gruesome photographs, a simulated "tiger cage" prison and jars of deformed foetuses attributed to contamination by Agent Orange. An exhibit on the 3rd floor tells the story of the war journalists from all over the world who documented,…

listings.name: Southern Women’s Museum
listings.description: Often overlooked by tourists, this museum celebrates the women’s role in the society, economy, and revolutionary history of the southern part of the country. It offers informative exhibits that include photographs, historical documents, and artifacts such as statues, combat equipment used by women, paintings and dioramas, tools used in the traditional production of textiles, and ao dai worn by famous women. As of a February 2018, the second floor had an exhibit on the history of the ao dai and another on textile production, the third floor detailed women’s revolutionary contributions, and the…

listings.name: FITO Museum of Traditional Vietnamese Medicine
listings.description: A small museum owned by the FITO company (they produce traditional pharmaceuticals) about the history of traditional medicine in Vietnam. The rooms are filled with items ranging from ingredients to tools used to produce and prepare Vietnamese medicine. Each ticket includes an informative tour of the museum and the opportunity to sample some products. The bottom floor also has a gift shop with competitively priced and high-quality traditional remedies.

listings.name: The Geological Museum of Vietnam
listings.address: 2 Đ. Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1
listings.description: A rare gem and a must see for geology & natural history enthusiasts. This 3-story building houses a collection of earthly artifacts (and even some non-earthly ones), including a few rare examples. Sadly in a state of neglect with poor lighting and little to no interpretive text. You can read more about it here.

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
listings.address: 97A Phó Đức Chính, Phường Nguyễn Thái Bìn, District 1
listings.description: Museum displaying art mainly from the 20th century by Vietnamese artists. Two floors of permanent collections are in the main building and the first floor of the second building has a special exhibitions space. The architecture of the French colonial buildings that house the museum is another impressive feature. They were designed by a French architect for the Hua family.

listings.name: Saigon Opera House
listings.address: 7 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City
listings.description: An opera house built by the French during the colonial period, and without a doubt one of the finest performance venues in Southeast Asia. In modern times it is home to the critically acclaimed AO show, an acrobatic show that fuses Vietnamese traditions with modern Cirque Nouveau performances. Occasionally hosts classical music performances when the AO show is not being performed.

listings.name: Ton Duc Thang Museum
listings.address: 5 Tôn Đức Thắng, Bến Nghé, District 1
listings.description: A museum detailing the life and achievements of politician Ton Duc Thang, known for his role as president. The first floor has a special exhibit (as of February 2018 about his time on the infamous prison island of Con Dao) and the second floor has a biographical display featuring artifacts, dioramas, and photographs telling the story of his life; there is also a painting gallery.

listings.name: The Venerable Thich Quảng Đức Monument
listings.address: intersection between Cach Mang Thang Tam & Nguyen Dinh Chieu streets
listings.description: A monument dedicated to the Buddhist monk Thich Quảng Đức, who self-immolated at the site in 1963 in protest against the persecution of South Vietnam's Buddhist majority by the Roman Catholic-dominated Ngô Đình Diệm government.

listings.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
listings.description: A Taoist temple considered by many to be Saigon’s finest, dedicated to the Jade Emperor, the king of the gods in Chinese mythology. Built by Cantonese immigrants in 1909. Check out the room filled with unusual figurines, to the left of the main hall. There are many turtles in a concrete pond in the courtyard. A calm place to rest from the city noise.

listings.name: Xá Lợi Pagoda
listings.address: 89 Bà Huyện Thanh Quan, Võ Thị Sáu, Quận 3
listings.description: The largest Buddhist temple in Ho Chi Minh City, and the headquarters of Buddhism in South Vietnam prior to the Fall of Saigon, said to house relics of the Gautama Buddha. During the Vietnam War, it was known for being a centre of resistance against the oppression of Buddhists by the Roman Catholic-dominated Ngô Đình Diệm government, and was raided several times by the South Vietnamese military in 1963.

listings.name: Giác Lâm Pagoda
listings.address: 565 Lạc Long Quân, Phường 10, Tân Bình
listings.description: Built in 1744, this is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Ho Chi Minh City. On the temple grounds is a bodhi tree that was gifted by a Sri Lankan monk in the 1950s. There is also a 7-storey tall pagoda that is said to house relics of the Gautama Buddha that were gifted by the same monk that gifted the bodhi tree.

listings.name: Central Mosque
listings.description: One of 12 mosques in Ho Chi Minh City, the Central Mosque was built in 1935. It was constructed for worshipers from southern India then resident in Saigon, but now Muslims from as far as Pakistan and Indonesia come to pray. Friday has the biggest congregations. The shaded veranda and cool stone floors make it an ideal place to sit, read, or even nap in the heat of the day. As with most mosques, remember to take your shoes off before entering and dress conservatively if you wish to enter.

listings.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
listings.hours: It is closed for renovations as of Feb 2020
listings.description: A French-built Catholic cathedral in the city center.

listings.name: Mariamman Temple
listings.address: 45 Trương Định, Phường Bến Thành, Quận 1
listings.description: Hindu temple build by Tamil Indian immigrants in the late 19th century. Although most of the Tamils fled Vietnam following the Fall of Saigon, the temple remains in active use, and today most of the devotees are ethnic Vietnamese or Khmers.

listings.name: Phung Son Tu Pagoda
listings.description: Dedicated to the god of happiness and virtue. The pagoda is dusty and dwarfed by high-rises under construction nearby, but the small, sculpted grounds are a good place for a rest from the hectic city.

listings.name: Quan Am Pagoda
listings.description: The oldest pagoda in town, dedicated to the Buddhist Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara (known as Quan Am in Vietnamese), home of a lot of incense and a cheerful puppy. It was built by Hokkien immigrants in the traditional Hokkien architectural style.

listings.name: Thien Hau Pagoda
listings.description: Dedicated to Lady Thien Hau, the Chinese sea goddess (known as Mazu in Chinese), who left two giant turtles to keep an eye on things in her absence. A festival is held in her honour on the 23rd day of the March lunar month. Don't miss the gorgeous sculptures in the walls of the courtyard outside the temple. It was built by Cantonese immigrants in the traditional Cantonese architectural style.

listings.name: Bitexco Financial Tower
listings.price: Adult 240k VND, child (4-12) / senior (65+) / disabled 160k VND
listings.description: Skydeck viewing platform (daily 09:30-21:30) with a 360° panorama of the city.

listings.name: IMAX cinema
listings.description: Vietnam's IMAX cinema.

listings.name: Landmark 81
listings.price: No entry fees but has parking fees for vehicles
listings.description: The highest tower of Vietnam with 81 floors which is 461.3 m, it has a big mall inside which includes a CGV cinema. Landmark 81 are also surrounded in a complex of apartments as part of Vinhomes' Tan Cang, or Central Park. Access the views by paying for SkyView (top 3 floors; 300k/500k weekdays/weekends, children/elderly half price; 200k for VND students on weekdays) or by patronizing one of the restaurants/cafes/lounges on the upper floors (prices vary, but tend to be 100k+ VND, high for Vietnam but about average for global HCOL cities; these are accessible through the Marriott Autograph…

listings.name: Dai Nam Tourist Park
listings.address: Hiệp An Ward, Thủ Dầu Một city, Binh Duong
listings.price: Adult/child between 1 m and 1.4 m: zoo 80,000/50,000; amusement park 100,000/50,000 dong; waterpark 100,000/60,000 dong; all three 200,000/120,000 dong
listings.description: This is one of the largest tourist attractions in Vietnam. It features the Dai Nam Van Hien Temple, an entertainment site, open range zoo, shopping areas, hotels, local and Western cuisine, and the largest man-made mountain range in Vietnam. Costing over 50 billion dong to build, this park is the beginning of mass tourism in Vietnam, although it is aimed at tourists and locals, and comes highly recommended. Transport options to the park are quite convoluted. As the park is new, online information is scarce. According to the locals, it is very much worth a visit, purely just to view the temple.

listings.name: Dam Sen Water Park
listings.price: Admission is based on height and time of arrival; under 0.8 m free, others 40-110,000 dong (90,000 after 16:00)
listings.description: Close to the city centre. This water park offers some unique water slide experiences, including the amazing "Space Bowl". Restaurant, health services and animatronic dinosaurs are on the premises.

listings.name: Twenty-Three September Park
listings.description: Running along Phan Ngu Lao St are a number of parks which fill up with locals before sunset, after work. They play a variety of games which you can participate in: badminton, kicking a shuttlecock and women's group aerobics to music are all very popular, and are great to watch. If you sit down by yourself in the open area near the Ben Thanh market a number of young university age locals will come and ask to practice English with you, this is a great way to spend an evening and the best way to meet intelligent interesting youth, they will question you either individually or in groups and share…

listings.name: Nguyen Hue Flower Street
listings.description: Beautiful assortment of flowers during Tet (Lunar New Year) along the popular boulevard in District 1.

listings.name: Ben Thanh Market
listings.description: It's a rather touristy market where you still can enjoy the most authentic Vietnamese pho.

listings.name: Bánh Mì 37
listings.description: Absolutely delicious even though a bit different than the traditional. Popular among locals, there might be a queue.

listings.name: Pho 24
listings.description: Clean modern chain found everywhere in Ho Chi Minh City. Excellent beef noodle soup, very cheap. Watch out for the fake Pho 24/24 on Pham Ngu Lao St, which does not belong to the chain and serves terrible and expensive food.

listings.name: Pho Quynh
listings.description: Their specialty is pho. Locals come regularly and lucky backpackers stumble upon it. It is air-conditioned on the second and third floors. They also have decent banh mi bo kho, which is beef stew with carrots, served with French baguette.

listings.name: Nhà Hàng Chay Ngọc Thọ
listings.description: Incredible range of delicoius veggie options, but also meat and chicken. Clean place, friendly staff, tasty food and satisfying portions.

listings.name: Nhà Hàng Asian Kitchen
listings.description: Very good place for delicious and diverse food, big choice. Kinda hidden, kinda great. Also lots of vegetarian options.

listings.name: Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa
listings.description: Banh Mi with local taste. Fresh bread (Vietnamese baguette) with various choices.

listings.name: Bún Chả 145
listings.description: Typical restaurant in the most amazing street of the city. Very good place for Bun Cha. As of February 2026, it is closed for renovation.

listings.name: The Lunch Lady
listings.description: The famous Lunch Lady was featured on Anthony Bourdain's show. Different noodle dish every day.

listings.name: Barbecue Garden
listings.description: A barbecue restaurant offering both Vietnamese and international foods.

listings.name: Bi Saigon
listings.description: Extensive menu with a choice between Vietnamese, Italian, Mexican and other styles. Open plan kitchen so you can see your food being prepared.

listings.name: Hoa Khai Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.address: 124 126 Nguyen Cu Trinh St, Cu Trinh Ward, District 1
listings.description: Tasty Vietnamese vegetarian food although with surly service. Be careful of being charged for unexpected items, such as the disposable hand towels that are presented to you without asking as you sit down.

listings.name: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát
listings.description: Restaurant selling Hủ tiếu Nam Vang, a flat rice noodle dish that is a specialty of the city. The dish is often called "Cambodian noodles" in English, even though it cannot be found in Cambodia.

listings.name: Quan An Ngon
listings.description: Two different restaurants operate with the same name within a few blocks of each other, one at 160 Pasteur Street, and the other long = 106.6975984 on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia across from the Reunification Palace. Set in atmospheric old French villas, with similar menus Vietnamese food, including regional specialities prepared in numerous independently-operated food stalls around the perimeter. Both are popular and both tend to be jammed at peak hours requiring a wait for a table. (The name literally means "restaurant of delicious eating".) The one on Pasteur has dozens of kerosene lamps burning for…

listings.name: Bloom Saigon Restaurant
listings.address: 3/5 Hoàng Sa, P. Đa Kao, Quận 1
listings.description: Temporarily closed as of August 2022. Non-profit restaurant run by Aid to Children Without Parents (ACWP) and serves as a culinary training facility. Very nice staff, excellent food, terrace on the 3rd floor. Situated a bit in the North and in a small calm community. Worth to go by foot, 20 mnin walk from the Jade Pagoda.

listings.name: Au Lac do Brazil
listings.description: Just to prove that Saigon has everything, here is a Brazilian-style churrascaria (all-you-can-eat restaurant featuring barbecued meat), with live Latin music Tuesday to Saturday. They also have a new outlet in Sky Garden II, Phu My Hung, District 7. It's a larger and less crowded one with usually better service.

listings.name: The Deck Saigon
listings.address: 38 Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien, An Phu, District 2
listings.description: The only posh restaurant on the banks of the river. Modern fusion cuisine using the local ingredients.

listings.name: Anan Saigon
listings.address: 89 Tôn Thất Đạm, Bến Nghé, District 1
listings.description: A premier fine dining restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, one of only two in Vietnam to be ranked among Asia's top 50 restaurants. Reservations essential.

listings.name: The Olive Grove Saigon
listings.description: Mediterranean cuisine.

listings.name: Halal@Saigon
listings.description: Vietnamese, Malaysian, and vegetarian cuisine prepared to halal guidelines. Has a Malaysian owner and there are several Malaysian staples on the menu, however it is primarily Vietnamese, with a wide range of dishes from around the country.

listings.name: Lion City Cafe and Restaurant
listings.description: Certified halal, serves halal food on 2nd floor.

listings.name: Bobby Brewery Coffee
listings.description: Nice place with good beverages. Used to show movies on 2nd and 3rd floor. Now reopened as La Cantina.

listings.name: Cafe 5 Sao
listings.description: Plays loud techno music. Attractive, but pretentious crowd.

listings.name: Cafe Napoly
listings.description: The decor is Roman ruins-lite (they meant "Napoli"), but the menu is typical for an upscale Vietnamese cafe: coffee, fruit drinks, ice cream, and a simple menu including eggs and rice dishes. Piped music is nice, not too loud by day (though louder at night), prices are decent. Outdoor terrace in the front, air-con section on the ground floor, and evening lounge-bar on the upper floor. Next door to the louder, more trendy and possibly pretentious Cafe Nam Sao.

listings.name: Cafe Saigon
listings.description: Italian coffee, foods, free Wi-Fi, relaxing & modern music.

listings.name: Chao Ba Ca Phe
listings.description: This place has a really authentic and wonderful cafe sua da served by the famous "grandma" for about 8,000 dong. A little tricky to find.

listings.name: Chot Nho Café
listings.address: 189 Nguyen Van Troi, Phu Nhuan District
listings.description: Reasonable prices, good menu. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Fresco Coffee
listings.description: Free Wi-Fi, play hill song music.

listings.name: Givral Café
listings.description: In the French tradition, with fresh pastries, collared waiters and elaborate portions of ice cream. Well-located, but over 20,000 dong for the simplest cup.

listings.name: Hideaway Café
listings.description: As its name implies, this place is hidden away and a good place to read, or have a quiet conversation or meal. Decent Western menu, although slightly pricey.

listings.name: Highlands Coffee
listings.description: Highlands Coffee is a Vietnamese chain that is ubiquitous in Ho Chi Minh City. They offer a variety of coffee drinks reasonably priced (25,000-60,000 dong, depending on your order) with consistent quality.

listings.name: M-Comic
listings.description: A rather hard to find coffee shop. Upstairs is like a bedroom with a couple of beds. Arrive early if you want to occupy one. It has a large selection of magazine and comic books to choose from. Only serves Vietnamese drinks, and the staff only speak a little English. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Old Saigon Coffee
listings.description: Reminiscent of HCMC in the past. It has a great view of Dong Khoi St. All the drinks and foods are typical Saigon. The staff are quite decent.

listings.name: Regina Coffee
listings.description: Vietnamese coffee or cappuccini. They have a skilled Japanese espresso master who knows how to brew coffee. French mixed with Asian design with brick walls. It is marketed towards tourists and all proceeds go to the church around the corner.

listings.name: Trung Nguyen
listings.description: The Vietnamese version of Starbucks, but with much better coffee. They have locations all over the city, but are not well represented in the heart of the tourist district. Prices start around 40,000 dong for a basic cuppa, although there are plenty of variations including the infamous weasel coffee (cà phê chồn), made from coffee beans collected from civet excrement; however, a quick Google search about the conditions in which the civets are kept may further dissuade some from sampling.

listings.name: Chill Sky Bar
listings.description: Rooftop bar at AB Tower in District 1 along September 23 park. This is the place to see and to be seen. Drinks are expensive at 200,000 dong and up. If you are around the September 23 park at night you will see the lights and hear the music blasting from the top of the AB tower. Look for the spotlights shooting into the sky.

listings.name: The Rabbit Hole Irish Sports Bar
listings.address: 111 Pham Viet Chanh, Ward 19, Binh Thanh
listings.hours: 15:00 to 02:00 Mon — Fri and 10:00 to 02:00 Sat and Sun
listings.description: Irish Sports bar.

listings.name: Acoustic Cafe
listings.description: Though only 1 km from the heavily touristed centre, this club is completely outside the tourist orbit, and offers an interesting view of local life. The all-Vietnamese house band performs every night, mostly American music, and it's always jammed with student-aged groupies. For some reason, they address the crowd in English between songs, even though half the crowd doesn't understand. On weekends, at least, you need to arrive by 19:30 to have any hope of getting a seat. If your hobby is rock ballad or hard rock, you should go on Friday night.

listings.name: Banana Pub
listings.description: Park View. Pool table, darts, friendly staff, beautiful people, loads of food. Stays open late depending on the crowd. Worth a trip from Q1 to experience the expat scene.

listings.name: Carmen
listings.description: The house band has changed some personnel but is still good, specializing in flamenco, salsa and Latin pop, and with an eclectic mix of other popular songs thrown in. Cocktails 110,000 dong, shots 80-85,000 dong, but with no entrance charge. It's popular and fills up on weekends.

listings.name: Ice Blue
listings.description: Centrally located English pub, complete with darts board and warm beer. Friendly, but shuts at midnight.

listings.name: Khong Ten
listings.description: Large cabaret featuring some of the biggest Vietnamese celebrity singers in Vietnam. The headliner is often familiar to the locals from television. Most overseas visitors may not like the musical style as it is mostly the mellow-to-melancholy, soft-jazzy, love-ballady style favoured by the middle and older generation of Vietnamese. But it's pure Vietnam, and very popular with both HCMC residents and Vietnamese expats on trips home.

listings.name: Lion's
listings.description: Brewery, restaurant offering German food, with tasty beers and cocktails. The outside terrace is a nice place to chill out, and the inside restaurant is very welcoming with its two beer tanks and cosy bar.

listings.name: Lush
listings.description: A nightclub in the Western style, with loud music and minimalist too-cool decor. Drink prices on par with most Saigon nightclubs. Mixed crowd (Vietnamese, tourists and expats), pretty good food but has a small dance floor. Ladies night on Tuesday offers free drinks for ladies until midnight. Be sure to arrive early as it gets very busy from around 22:30 and it is difficult to get served at the bar.

listings.name: Metallic Bar
listings.description: House band plays covers of Metallica, Guns 'n Roses and other popular rock bands nightly between 21:00 and midnight.

listings.name: Peaches
listings.description: Great place to enjoy a few drinks with friends. Friendly staff, Asian food. Quite low key in comparison to other PMH bars.

listings.name: Polo
listings.description: Mixture of expats and locals, starts getting busy quite early. Music from the 1980s to the present. Noisy and smokey.

listings.name: Q Bar Saigon
listings.description: Established in 1992 under the Opera House. Mix of locals, tourists and expats in a grotto-like uber-chic setting that could as easily be in Soho as Saigon. Open till late every night. Great cocktails, though at very high prices, similar to the roof-top bar of the Caravelle Hotel across the street. It's the cool place to be seen if you have a lot of Uncle Hos in your pocket. Terrace and Indoor areas. DJ nights.

listings.name: Rio Saigon
listings.description: A Brazilian flowery decor-themed bar/pub with a Filipino house band playing pop/rock such as Bon Jovi and Skid Row.

listings.name: Saigon Pho
listings.description: This little hole in the wall is only a stone's throw from Allez Boo, but much more expat orientated. Open until late.

listings.name: Serenata and Soi Da
listings.description: Two open-air cafe-bars with live music in villa-style settings, which attract few if any tourists but typify what most Vietnamese consider a pleasant evening out. Both feature a mix of classical chamber music, Vietnamese lounge songs, American FM classics and the odd French song.

listings.name: The Tavern
listings.address: SB8-1 My Khanh 2 (H4-2) Nguyen Van Linh, Phu My Hung District
listings.hours: Opens for breakfast, closes at midnight
listings.description: Western food with fish & chips and burgers.

listings.name: Velvet
listings.description: Nice ambiance & music. Latest chic bar in town. Gets very busy, and at weekends you will need a booking.

listings.name: Xu Bar
listings.description: Great wine list. Nice ambiance & service.

listings.name: Alibi
listings.description: Very cosy atmosphere, with sofas lining the walls and beautiful decor. Good food & drinks selection, nice music, and a mix of both locals & expats. Friendly staff, and the management's always there to make you feel welcome and make sure you get what you are asking for.

listings.name: Allez Boo
listings.description: For those who have been here before, you'll find the original bar is now Highlands Coffee and an all new Allez Boo has opened on the opposite corner. It's shiny and brand-new, but retains the same feel as the original. There's a bar with air-con on the 2nd floor with DJ-type music, and an airy rooftop patio. Quite similar to its sibling establishment, Go2 Bar.

listings.name: Apocalypse Now
listings.description: Legendary and still packed on weekends, although aside from a few movie references it's not all that much to look at. Stays open late. Now opened their 2nd floor for DJ, dancing, drinks with less crowded atmosphere.

listings.name: Catwalk
listings.description: All-in-one place with a massage parlour, disco, KTV, and a mini-casino. Price is on the expensive side, but it is a sight to behold.

listings.name: Go2 Bar
listings.description: The main backpacker bar while Allez Boo was closed, still a great meeting place. It's impossible to miss the four floors of neon lights on the outside. Large patio on the sidewalk at street level, a cosier bar on the second floor with occasional live music or big-screen sports, plus a rooftop patio (with retractable roof) with individual BBQs up a steep set of stairs on the 5th floor.

listings.name: Oblivion
listings.description: Late night venue with lots of character, claims to be Saigon's premier music bar and it's hard to argue, assuming, that is, you have a taste for non-chart buzzy British guitar and obscure dark US/European stuff. You have to ask for happy pop, though if you're spending enough it'll sometimes get an outing. Like most Saigon bars, it attracts its share of working girls. If you're not interested, simply say you're not and you'll be left alone.

listings.name: Pasteur Street Brewing Company
listings.address: 144 Pasteur, Bến Nghé, District 1 (this is the original location, but others can be found throughout the city)
listings.description: A cozy bar that specializes in craft beer microbrews. A large selection of their own beers that run between 50,000-300,000 dong per glass (though most are 105,000 for a regular size). They also serve food and bar snacks. Mostly expats and tourists with a laid back yet classy atmosphere. The original tap rooms are down an alley off Pasteur Street, but there are clearly marked signs to guide you from the street.

listings.name: 163 Cyclo Bar
listings.description: Two doors down from the Duna Hotel. Thumping music until 02:00 with friendly staff. Sex workers catering to Western men here. If you're not interested, just gently let it be known.

listings.name: Le Pub
listings.description: Always busy after 18:00, famous for its strong drinks, daily dollar-specials (e.g., Tuesday USD1 for vodka mixers all night) and friendly staff. It has the same owner as Le Pub in Hanoi. The Pub Quiz (almost every Tuesday) is very popular with expats, especially the English teachers. Get there early or it's too packed to find a place to sit down. Indoors and outdoor tables available.

listings.name: Rex Hotel Rooftop
listings.description: They serve a buffet dinner at the dinner hour, which gradually gives way to drinks and music. Acts change over time, but have included a Filipino band playing FM classics and a Vietnamese group playing Latin and flamenco. It's a pleasant place to get above the city noise and enjoy some fresh air. Cocktails around 140,000 dong.

listings.name: Saigon Saigon
listings.description: A pleasant, breezy bar with a great view of the city. Great live band (Cuban) playing inside every night. Cool, quiet ambience on the terrace. Attracts an expense-account crowd due to the prices.

listings.name: Seventeen Saloon
listings.description: American Wild West-themed bar, live music every night and other entertainment. Drinks are expensive.

listings.name: Sheridan's
listings.description: Small, cosy Irish-themed bar with imported draft beer and live music. Brits will appreciate the great food tasting of home (or the closest you'll get here).

listings.name: Vasco's
listings.description: Live music on some nights of the week and a typical bar atmosphere for tourists and expats. Drinks from 50,000 dong, including sales tax, tip not necessary.

listings.name: VIBE Billiards & Lounge
listings.address: 02 Sương Nguyệt Ánh, Phường Bến Thành, Quận 1
listings.description: Professional billiards tables and a spacious lounge. Food and drinks and you can customise the billiard table lights from a special lighting system.

listings.name: ZanZBar
listings.description: Casual-upscale, the clients tend to come for the great choice of wines-by-the-glass (huge walk-in wine cellar), or for the cocktails (premium brands) and good selection of imported beers. Can remain open after midnight, depending on the number of customers.

listings.name: An Phuong 2
listings.description: A friendly family-run guesthouse, very clean and homely. Free Internet, cheap laundry and all rooms have double glazing.

listings.name: Blue River Hotel
listings.price: USD25 for a room without a view. USD30 for a room with a view that may or may not have a balcony
listings.description: Amazing small hotel in an alley off Pham Ngu Lao. They can arrange an airport pickup for USD15, although an official taxi from the airport counter will cost USD8. Some staff members speak English and the service is good.

listings.name: Dai Huy Hoang Hotel
listings.description: Comfortable rooms with air-con, fan, free Internet and breakfast. Friendly staff.

listings.name: Diep Anh
listings.description: Very friendly owners. Rooms with air-con, refrigerator, cable TV, en suite bath, and Wi-Fi. Very reasonably priced minibar.

listings.name: Duna Hotel
listings.price: From USD12 for a single room with no window to USD30 for a triple with a window facing the street.
listings.description: All rooms have air-con, satellite TV, a fridge, elevator. Pleasant staff. The front door is locked around 23:00-24:00.

listings.name: Hanh Hoa Hotel
listings.description: Vietnamese styling, with bamboo interiors, rattan beds and wooden floors.

listings.name: Hotel Bi Saigon
listings.description: Clean, comfortable, and terrific staff. In-room Internet access for USD3/day. The lobby houses the La Table de Saigon restaurant.

listings.name: Ly
listings.description: Family-run guest house with friendly staff who speak English. Air-con, hot water, cable TV with international channels, baggage storage, laundry service, big beds. with balconies.

listings.name: Ly Loan
listings.description: Family-run guest house in a small, safe, quiet alley. Some English is spoken. Rooms are spacious and nicely furnished. With air-con, hot water, big beds and some with balconies. Free Internet and Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Mai Guest House
listings.address: Hem 104 Bui Viên or 241 /41 Phạm Ngũ Lão, District 1
listings.price: Doubles USD12, doubles with balcony USD15
listings.description: Friendly family. Tucked in a side alley from Pham Ngu Lao or Bui Viên next to My Home Guest Home. Small balcony. Clean apartments with aircon and Wi-Fi. 15,000 or 30,000 dong per kg for 24 hr or express laundry.

listings.name: My Home Guest House
listings.price: Singles USD12, doubles USD18, triples available
listings.description: Friendly staff and clean. The buses from up north drop you right near this hostel. Air-con, hot water, comfortable beds, free Wi-Fi. Free bananas at all times and they do laundry. Tourist bars and clubs are a couple hundred metres away.

listings.name: Nam Chau
listings.description: Nice and very clean.

listings.name: Galaxy Boutique Hotel
listings.address: 269/19 De Tham Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1

listings.name: Ngoc Minh Hotel
listings.description: Clean hotel with friendly staff, free Internet and Wi-Fi. Elevator. 5 storeys, garden on top floor and free breakfast.

listings.name: Nguyen Khang Hotel
listings.description: Good staff, free Internet with PC in lobby and Wi-Fi in rooms. Free breakfast served on the ground floor from 07:00-10:00. Clean, tastefully simple in decoration, rooms are rather small but have air-con, fan, TV, fridge, and those at the front have large windows. Visa and Mastercard accepted.

listings.name: PP Backpackers
listings.description: Run by a friendly Englishman, offers clean dorms and rooms, can book tours and offers a big breakfast for USD1.

listings.name: Rainbow Hotel
listings.description: Large, bright albeit somewhat worn rooms, and those at the front have a nice view.

listings.name: Tam Anh Guesthouse
listings.description: A clean and secure family-run guesthouse. Good air-con, free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Tan Dat My Hotel
listings.description: Large rooms with a view, air-con, Wi-Fi, fridge, cable TV and a free rooftop breakfast next to the Dam Sen Park. French bakery 30 m away. American-style supermarket 10 min walk on the same street.

listings.name: Thanh Guest House
listings.address: 84/9 Bui Vien, Pham Ngu Lao, District 1
listings.description: Warm and friendly guesthouse. Lobby inside the house with comfy sofa, cable TV and Internet. Free Wi-Fi throughout. Trips and tours can be booked at reception.

listings.name: Thien Hong Hotel
listings.price: Air-con room with no window, USD15
listings.description: Helpful and friendly owners, free Wi-Fi, TV in rooms with many channels including international.

listings.name: Ty Mon
listings.description: Friendly owners, very good basic rooms with air-con, TV, decent furniture and fridge. Very cheap price, mostly used by Vietnamese people. A bit far out from centre.

listings.name: Xuan Spring Hotel
listings.description: Air-con, refrigerator, cable TV and private bath with hot shower and free Internet. Online bookings. Good service.

listings.name: Mi Linh Hotel
listings.address: B38A Bach Dang Street Ward 02 Tan Binh District.
listings.description: a/c standard double room with own bathroom and cable tv. Free Wifi. a good clean place to stay near the HCM Airport.

listings.name: Lee Hostel Home For Backpackers
listings.description: 20 bed dorm with air.con and hot water free wifi. free breakfast. Some complaints that they will insist on holding your passport hostage even after you've paid, various other scammy practices.

listings.name: Bich Hong Guest House
listings.description: Fan and a/c double rooms with own bathroom.

listings.name: Kim Loan Guest House
listings.description: Fan double with own bathroom.

listings.name: 4 Guest House Thanh
listings.description: Fan double room with own bathroom.

listings.name: Christina's Saigon
listings.address: 212/2B Nguyen Trai St., Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1
listings.description: A flashpacker guesthouse and bed & breakfast. The studios are beautifully designed with modern bathrooms. Booking is only available through Airbnb.

listings.name: Asian Hotel
listings.address: 146-148-150 Dong Khoi St, Ben Nghe District
listings.description: Every room has air-con, cable TV, and Internet.

listings.name: Platinum Boutique Residence and Hotel
listings.address: 270 Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1
listings.description: Lovely modern, clean hotel. Rooms come with double-glazed windows, LCD flat screen TVs, and wall-mounted air conditioning controls. The suite has a spa bath. Free Wi-Fi and friendly staff.

listings.name: Dai Nam Hotel
listings.description: Breakfast and free in-room Wi-Fi. Houses the Gossip Nightclub.

listings.name: Asian Ruby Select Hotel
listings.address: 122F-122F1 Bui Thi Xuan, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1
listings.description: All rooms and suites have air-con, TV with satellite channels, IDD telephone, coffee/tea maker and minibar. Bar, cafe, spa and massage services, business centre, gym and high speed Internet access. Annoyingly, housekeeping have a tendency to knock on bedroom doors early in the morning, but then don't make up the rooms until early afternoon.

listings.name: Nhat Ha Hotel
listings.address: 252 BC Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1
listings.description: 57 rooms decorated with traditional Vietnamese handicrafts. IDD telephone, satellite TV, mini-bar, and air-con.

listings.name: Sanouva Hotel
listings.address: 175-177 Ly Tu Trong St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1
listings.description: Air-con, 32" LCD TV with cable, Internet, and IDD telephone. Restaurant, bar, café, car rental, travel bookings, tour services and safes.

listings.name: Spring Hotel
listings.description: Clean, boutique hotel that is walking distance to major attractions such as Ben Thanh Market and the cathedral.

listings.name: Thuan Thien Hotel
listings.address: 277 Le Thanh Ton St, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1
listings.description: Air-con rooms, cable TV, DVD, coffee/tea maker, minibar and a private toilet and shower with bath. Internet, dry cleaning, and laundry service and a travel agency for booking tours.

listings.name: Y Thien
listings.description: Full service hotel with a range of clean rooms with large baths. Sizes from tiny and windowless (yet functional), to full wall window overlooking the city and streets. The 4th floor room to the right of the elevator is USD20–25. Cable TV, air-con, fan, refrigerator, elevator, all night guard for bikes, hotel safe. A good option if you don't want to stay in the backpacker area and are willing to pay a little more.

listings.name: Somerset Vista Ho Chi Minh City
listings.address: No. 628C Hanoi Highway, An Phu, District 2
listings.description: The property has apartments ranging from two- to four-bedroom with kitchenette, washing machines and dryers. They have an on-site tennis court.

listings.name: An An Hotel
listings.description: Clean, popular, and offers comfortable rooms with double glazing in the centre of the action on De Tham. Free Wi-Fi in room and lobby.

listings.name: An An 2 Hotel
listings.price: From USD22 (with window) for standard single, USD25 for double and USD36–50 for superior and luxury with balcony. The prices can be lowered if you stay for 4 or more days (e.g., USD20 for double for 6 days)
listings.description: This is the (much newer) sister hotel to An An hotel.

listings.name: Continental Hotel
listings.description: An old-school colonial hotel dating back to 1880 and the setting of Graham Greene's novel The Quiet American. Beautiful garden courtyard, huge rooms, nice balcony views. On the minus side, there is no pool and traffic noise can be irritating,.

listings.name: Hotel Đông Đô
listings.description: New hotel with clean and comfortable rooms.

listings.name: The First Hotel
listings.address: 18 Hoang Viet St, Ward 4, Tan Binh District
listings.description: Luxury hotel, 104 air-con rooms, cable TV, mini-bar, shower with bath, and Wi-Fi. Casino and ballroom, fitness room, tennis court, swimming pool, airport transfer, and car rental.

listings.name: Ho Sen Hotel
listings.address: 4A-4B Thi Sach St, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1
listings.description: Clean and comfortable rooms with air-con and bar fridge. Right around the corner is the Apocalypse Now Club. Breakfast included, free Wi-Fi in the lobby, while connections are a little patchy in the rooms.

listings.name: Mekong Lodge
listings.address: 196/1/20 Cong Hoa St, Tan Binh District
listings.description: A good hotel for those who love nature.

listings.name: Rex Hotel
listings.description: Another old standby, former haunt of the press corps and site of the daily "Five O'Clock Follies" news briefing during the Vietnam War. The 5th floor rooftop beer garden is famous and its symbol, the golden crown, is rotating again. The rooms are very pleasant and there is a swimming pool on the roof. Buffet breakfast.

listings.name: Thien Thao Hotel
listings.description: A small hotel with thin walls but also clean and comfortable with air-con rooms, bathtubs, local and cable channels on a large plasma TV, and minibar fridge. About 20 min walk away from the heart of District 1. Bakery and several restaurants less than 5 min away, free Wi-Fi in the rooms and three computers in the lobby.

listings.name: Xuan Loc Hotel
listings.description: Clean and comfortable rooms. Breakfast available. Internet and computers are provided.

listings.name: M Village
listings.description: A chain with a number of furnished short/long-term stay apartment rentals scattered throughout the city (both in and outside of touristy areas) that supports hotel-like bookings (as little as 1 night, no extra charges). Typically includes free self-service, first come first serve laundry machines and a small in-room kitchenette. English is a bit spotty, but serviceable with Google Translate and properties prefer/offer 24/7 communication via Whatsapp.

listings.name: Caravelle Hotel
listings.description: In-house restaurants and spas. 7 km from the airport. During the war it was home to many war correspondents and the rooftop bar served as their watering hole. Today, it is also known for the afternoon tea served at its Café de l'Opera.

listings.name: Hotel Majestic
listings.description: Luxury hotel that got its start in 1925, and though it has undergone a number of renovations since, it maintains the same basic look outside. Rooftop bar serves mediocre ice cream and drinks. Has a non-smoking wing.

listings.name: JW Marriott Hotel & Suites Saigon
listings.address: Hai Bà Trưng/Góc Đ. Lê Duẩn, Bến Nghé, Quận 01
listings.description: Dinner buffet from USD40. Can walk to city center. Formerly Intercontinental Saigon

listings.name: Mövenpick Hotel Saigon
listings.address: 253 Nguyen Van Troi St, Phu Nhuan District
listings.description: Luxury hotel in Phu Nhuan, 10 min away from the exhibition centre and international airport and 20 min from HCMC centre. 251 rooms and suites. All rooms are equipped with individually controlled air-con, TV, minibar, safe, hairdryer. Broadband Internet in all rooms.

listings.name: Park Hyatt Saigon
listings.description: Luxury hotel which features a collection of contemporary Vietnamese art, a variety of non-smoking dining options including an al fresco setting, an Italian restaurant, Opera, the signature Vietnamese/Western restaurant, Square One, Park Lounge that serves afternoon tea, and a martini bar, 2 Lam Son. The hotel has a 20 m pool, fitness centre, and the Xuan Spa.

listings.name: Renaissance Riverside Hotel
listings.description: On the river and near the main tourist-shopping district, a block off of Dong Khoi.

listings.name: The Reverie Saigon
listings.description: 286 rooms and suites furnished with Italian designs, five high-end restaurants, a spa, swimming pool, fitness centre and an executive lounge.

listings.name: Saigon Domaine Luxury Residences
listings.address: 1057 Binh Quoi Street, Ward 28, Binh Thanh District
listings.description: Luxury serviced apartments. Cable TV, radio, air-con, safe, hair dryer, Internet, phone, mini–bar and coffee/tea maker. Swimming pool, fitness room, sauna, business facilities and currency exchange. Car rental and airport and city transfers.

listings.name: Sheraton Saigon
listings.description: It has a Prada shop in the arcade. Restaurants are around USD40 for an all-you-can-eat buffet dinner, wine included.

listings.name: Sherwood Residence
listings.description: Sherwood Residence is a luxury serviced apartment in HCMC. The property offers two and three bedroom apartments for short- and long-term. A private restaurant serves Western and Asian cuisine. On Pasteur Street, Sherwood Residence is within walking distance to the War Remnants' Museum and guests can take the free hourly shuttle to the business district.

listings.name: Sofitel Plaza Saigon
listings.description: 290-room hotel in the city center. Airy, if slightly small rooms, comfy beds, free wired Internet. Several restaurants, including a buffet and a breakfast spread.

listings.name: Somerset Chancellor Court Ho Chi Minh City
listings.address: 21-23 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai St, District 1
listings.description: The serviced residence is in the heart of the business district. It offers 172 apartments ranging from studios to three-bedroom. Each apartment is fully furnished with an open kitchen concept, contemporary Western style decor and balcony.

listings.name: Thao Dien Village
listings.address: 195 Nguyen Van Huong St, Thao Dien Ward, District 2
listings.description: A colonial-style boutique hotel in tropical gardens on the banks of the river. 22 rooms, spa and health club. 4 restaurants; Ngon (Vietnamese), Villa Romaine (Italian), Chaba (Thai), and Tama-Gawa (sushi bar). Every Saturday at 19:30 there is a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show on the riverside outdoor terrace of Ngon Restaurant.

listings.name: Windsor Plaza Hotel
listings.description: A high-end hotel with 386 rooms in Cholon (Ho Chi Minh City's Chinatown). Several restaurants including an extensive Western and Asian buffet on 4th floor; a Chinese restaurant serving live seafood, southern Chinese cuisine and dim sum; and a rooftop international restaurant that has panoramic views of Cholon. Guests can take the free hourly shuttle to the business district. Free Wi-Fi in public areas.

listings.name: Bat Temple
listings.description: The monastery, while pleasing on its own, the main draw here are the fruit bats that live in the trees behind the temple. The monks protect them from the farmers in the area who consider them both a pest and a delicacy. Arrive about 1/2 hour before sunset to see the show begin. Any xe om in town can bring you here. There is also a Buddhist crematorium across the road from the temple.

listings.name: Clay Pagoda
listings.description: This monastery was decorated by a monk sculptor who spent 60 years designing and installing thousands of statues into a colorful cacophony of Buddhist kitch. Notable features are: pillars with dragons on them, a baby white elephant, a white tiger, and golden turtles in the pond out back.

listings.name: Ngã Năm (5 fork intersection) Floating Market
listings.description: Busiest at 05:00-06:00, but the market is held all day and all night on one fork of the river. You can rent a boat to go around for as little as USD2-3.

listings.name: Hung
listings.description: This place has an extensive menu in Vietnamese. Drawing pictures sometimes helps, or bring a phrasebook along. The food is wonderful, and the open-air pavilion has a nice atmosphere. The staff is very helpful.

listings.name: Khánh Vi
listings.description: Spacious restaurant, extensive menu, individual dishes from 65,000-150,000 dong. Attentive service.

listings.name: Le Phong
listings.description: Cheap and cheerful hotel, with air-con rooms. Clean and modern, it is a charming place with quirky fish tanks and a pleasant long-time owner.

listings.name: Oolong Tea Plantations and Heart-shaped Tea Hill
listings.address: Thao Nguyen and Van Son wards
listings.description: These extensive commercial tea plantations cover thousands of hectares and grow Shan Tuyet, Bat Tien and imported oolong tea varieties. The tea rows are carefully trimmed into concentric curves or distinctive heart shapes. The plantations are a prominent agricultural landscape and a popular place for landscape photography on the plateau.

listings.name: Na Ka and Mu Nau Plum Valleys
listings.price: 20,000–40,000 dong per person for entry to orchards during blossom and harvest seasons
listings.description: These limestone valleys cover more than 100 hectares and specialize in Moc Chau's local plum variety. From late January to mid-February, the valleys are covered in white plum blossoms. The ripe plums are harvested from May to early June.

listings.name: Dai Yem Waterfall
listings.address: Ban Vat, formerly Muong Sang Ward, now part of Moc Chau Ward
listings.description: A natural waterfall fed by the Bo Co Lam and Bo He streams, it cascades more than 100 m over nine moss-covered limestone tiers. The water flows most strongly during the rainy season, from May to September. The nearby Love Glass Bridge spans a deep gorge.

listings.name: Ban Ang Pine Forest
listings.description: This natural pine forest covers more than 43 hectares and surrounds two tranquil freshwater lakes. Visitors can cycle around the lakes, walk beneath the tall pine trees and visit nearby high-tech strawberry farms where they can pick fruit.

listings.name: Pha Luong Peak
listings.price: Forest ranger and guide fees vary by tour
listings.description: This limestone mountain rises to 2,000 m near the Vietnam–Laos border and is mentioned in the poem Tay Tien by Quang Dung. Its summit is a huge, flat rock outcrop projecting into the open air, with sheer cliffs hundreds of metres high and panoramic views of forests across the border in Laos.

listings.name: Bach Long Glass Bridge
listings.description: Bach Long Glass Bridge has been recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's longest glass-bottomed bridge, with a total length of 632 m. It consists of a 290 m bridge spanning two mountains and a 342 m cliffside walkway connecting the sections.

listings.name: Bat Cave
listings.address: Bat Cave, Residential Group 7, Moc Son Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: This is a karst cave in a limestone mountain. Local people have known about the cave for a long time, and various legends are associated with it. It was also used as a shelter during the resistance war against the French. Archaeologically, however, it is considered to have been discovered in 1952.

listings.name: Primitive Village, Hang Tau
listings.address: Ta So, Moc Chau, Son La
listings.description: Known as the "primitive village" or the "village of three no's" (no grid electricity, no mobile phone signal, and no internet), it is located about 20 km from the center of Moc Chau town.

listings.name: Ta Xua Cloud-hunting Area and Hang Dong Dinosaur Spine
listings.description: This high mountain range lies between Son La and Yen Bai provinces. Its sheltered basin-shaped valleys trap dense cloud formations from October to April. The main attraction is the Dinosaur Spine at Ban Chong Chua, a narrow ridge path with steep drops on both sides. Other popular viewpoints include Dolphin Rock and the Lonely Cat-apple Tree.

listings.name: Ngoc Chien Valley and Traditional Pomu Stilt Houses
listings.description: This highland commune lies at an average elevation of 1,800 m in a valley surrounded by mountains and terraced rice fields. Ban Luot and Ban Na Tau are notable White Thai villages with hundreds of traditional stilt houses built from pomu wood, weathered to a greyish-brown colour over time. The area also has natural hot springs emerging from underground at temperatures of 50–60°C.

listings.name: Son La Hydropower Plant
listings.description: This underground hydropower plant has an installed capacity of 2,400 MW and is the largest of its kind in Southeast Asia. It was completed in 2012. The massive 138 m-high roller-compacted concrete dam, nearly 1,000 m long, spans the Da River and creates a reservoir with a capacity of more than 9.2 billion m³.

listings.name: Da River Lake and Pa Uon Bridge
listings.price: Tourist motorboat hire: VND 100,000–200,000 per person
listings.description: The expansive Da River reservoir has deep-blue water surrounded by winding limestone mountains, earning it the nickname "Ha Long Bay of the Northwest". A major engineering landmark is Pa Uon Bridge, whose tallest pier rises 98.6 m from the riverbed to the bridge deck, making it the tallest bridge pier in Vietnam. Attractions along the lake include Linh Son Thuy Tu Temple, dedicated to Nang Han, and a heart-shaped island developed for ecotourism.

listings.name: Son La Prison Special National Relic
listings.address: Khau Ca Hill, To Hieu Ward
listings.description: This historic site was built by the French colonial administration in 1908 using stone and brick to imprison Vietnamese revolutionaries. The complex includes dark underground cells, collective prison blocks, guard towers and the historic To Hieu peach tree, associated with the steadfast spirit of the communist revolutionary. The Son La Provincial Museum is nearby and displays cultural artefacts from Thai and Muong communities.

listings.name: Northwest Square and Ho Chi Minh Monument
listings.address: Chieng Coi Street, Chieng Coi Ward
listings.description: This central square covers nearly 20 hectares. Its imposing bronze monument, "Uncle Ho with the Ethnic Peoples of the Northwest", stands in front of a granite bas-relief depicting ban flowers and scenes of Thai xoe dancing and other folk cultural activities. The site also includes a temple dedicated to Ho Chi Minh and modern fountains.

listings.name: Co Noi Junction Historical Relic
listings.description: This strategically important location played a major role during the 1954 Dien Bien Phu Campaign. It was hit by thousands of tonnes of bombs dropped by French aircraft seeking to cut the main supply route. The site includes an 18 m-high monument to the Youth Volunteer Corps, commemorating the sacrifices of transport workers and frontline civilian support personnel.

listings.name: Dong Hai Moc Chau Restaurant
listings.address: 210 Tran Huy Lieu Street, Moc Chau Ward
listings.description: Specialises in traditional Northwest Vietnamese cuisine, including pa pỉnh tộp, Moc Chau bê chao, hill chicken grilled with mac khen pepper, and stir-fried mèo mustard greens with garlic.

listings.name: Suoi Hen Restaurant
listings.address: Chu Van Thinh Street, To Hieu Ward
listings.description: Set in a traditional wooden stilt-house-style building, the restaurant serves ethnic Thai dishes such as Da River grilled fish, stream moss soup and crispy roasted free-range village pork.

listings.name: Tuan Gu Cuisine Restaurant
listings.address: Nguyen Luong Bang Street (National Highway 6), Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: Serves characteristic dishes of Northwest Vietnamese cuisine.

listings.name: Ban Vat Hong Market
listings.address: Ban Vat, Moc Chau Ward, Son La Province
listings.description: Ban Vat Market is located in Ban Vat, Moc Chau, and serves as a gathering place for local residents and visitors on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings each week. The market operates from around 17:30 to 22:00, with stalls selling food, local specialties, and handicrafts. Visitors can sample highland cuisine, watch cultural performances by local villagers, and learn about the traditional way of life of the Thai ethnic community.

listings.name: Muong Thanh Luxury Son La Hotel
listings.address: 2 To Hieu Street, To Hieu Ward
listings.description: A luxury five-star hotel with 154 modern rooms offering panoramic views of Khau Ca Hill. Facilities include a year-round indoor swimming pool, gym, spa and wellness centre, and a restaurant serving an international-style breakfast buffet.

listings.name: Thao Nguyen Resort Moc Chau
listings.address: Hoang Quoc Viet Street, Thao Nguyen Ward
listings.description: A large four-star resort spread across a hillside, with nearly 100 detached villas, a year-round heated indoor swimming pool, an outdoor tennis court, a children's play area and a restaurant serving highland cuisine.

listings.name: Moc Chau Island Resort and Bach Long Glass Bridge
listings.address: Na Lun Residential Group, Moc Chau Ward
listings.description: Moc Chau Island Resort & Bach Long Glass Bridge is set amid the dramatic mountains, lush green valleys, and rolling hills of the Moc Chau Plateau. The resort offers a range of accommodation options, including hotel rooms and bungalows, with views of the surrounding natural landscape. The complex also features restaurants, recreational areas, photo spots, and other facilities for visitors seeking accommodation, sightseeing, and photography opportunities.

listings.name: Glenda Tower Moc Chau Hotel
listings.address: 565 Tran Huy Lieu Street, Moc Chau Ward
listings.description: An upscale four-star hotel in the centre of Moc Chau.

listings.name: Ta Xua LuTre Homestay
listings.address: Ta Xua Village, Ta Xua Commune
listings.description: A rustic wooden homestay with glass balconies and a café overlooking the Ta Xua sea of clouds. It serves charcoal-grilled dishes and hotpot made with local black chicken.

listings.name: Bich Dong Pagoda
listings.price: Free. Parking 20,000 dong, or free on the square in front of the entrance bridge if you buy a drink for 25,000 dong, or leave the bike farther away from the entrance. The lady charging the fee may try to overcharge by implying that it also includes the entrance to the temples, but this is a lie
listings.description: Three temples carved into a limestone mountain, dating from the 15th-century reign of Le Thai To. The lower temple has a stone next to it that resonates when tapped, plus a Buddha footprint. The middle temple has an 18th-century bell, a cave and resonating pillars. The top temple has a view of the surrounding countryside, which is good for sunsets.

listings.name: Hidden Valley (Secret Cave)
listings.price: Cave tour 30,000 dong, boat tour 50,000 dong
listings.description: Only very few tourists wander into this secluded valley. There is a shop selling some drinks and ice cream, but which might be closed. There is a boat advertising a tour into a 350m deep cave, a wide peaceful field with some goats and then there is the 15min walking tour through a cave. The guide babbles about in Vietnamese only, shows various fossil shells and funny shaped wall markings, stalagmites and stalactites and even turns your head into the right direction to look using his hands.

listings.name: Mua Cave
listings.price: 100,000 dong entrance fee + 10,000 dong bicycle/motorbike parking fee
listings.description: The cave here is an afterthought; the main draws are the two hilltop viewpoints. 500 steps will lead you to the first peak, an unimpressive temple with incredibly stunning views over Tam Coc and Ninh Binh’s countryside, including a large lotus flower field at the bottom (should bloom in June/July). On the second slightly higher peak, there is a long dragon statue which you can climb around. Caution when arriving by bike or motorbike: On the street leading up to the entrance gate there are multiple places trying to convince you that they're the official parking spot, some even utilizing…

listings.name: Thung Nham Bird Park
listings.address: Hai Nham, Ninh Hai, Tam Coc
listings.description: Entrance ticket includes two boat rides, one in a cave with sleeping bats and one to the conservation bird park. Some very beautiful flower gardens, tree areas and bamboo bridges. You are allowed to bring your own bicycle inside and cycle around. Useful too as its about 1.3km from ticket office to park entrance with a steep hill to get over.

listings.name: Dundj Valley
listings.description: A quieter limestone valley located beyond the main tourist routes of Tam Coc, with rice fields, small waterways, and surrounding karst formations. The area is characterized by a rural landscape where visitors may encounter farming activities, grazing animals, and narrow paths connecting small plots of land. In some parts of the valley, waterways extend into natural cave sections, including a longer water cave noted locally for its clear water and its connection between areas of the valley. The surroundings include a mix of open fields, forested sections, and agricultural land, offering a more…

listings.name: Tam Coc Museum
listings.description: A small museum presenting aspects of traditional Vietnamese rural life. Exhibits include rice cultivation, grain processing, and traditional tools used in farming communities.

listings.name: Bai Dinh Temple
listings.hours: 07:00 to 20:00, entrance to the large tower until 17:00
listings.price: Free entrance, motorbike parking 15,000 dong, shuttle e-mobiles with fee
listings.description: Huge Buddhist complex, the largest in Vietnam, with the largest pagoda tower of Vietnam (100 m high, has elevator). Most of it was built between 2003 and 2010, so it's in exceptionally good shape. A visit can easily take 4 hours due to the sheer size of the complex. At night, most buildings are lit up, creating absolutely magnificent sights. Access is free but notoriously difficult without taking a shuttle e-mobile from the parking lot, because the parking lot is 3 km from the entrance, at the completely opposite end of the precincts. For the shuttles, there are several options. If you want…

listings.name: Hoa Lu Ancient Capital
listings.price: 20,000 dong. Entrance to Xuyen Thuy cave is 15,000 dong
listings.description: The ancient capital during Dinh (968-80) and Le dynasties (980-1009). Little remains from this period, but there are a few large temples and monuments built from the 1600s on: the temple of Dinh Tien Hoang, the temple of King Le Dai Hahn, Nhat Tru Pagoda, and on top of a hill, Dinh Tien Hoang's tomb. Consider a guide, as there is little interpretive information (or even useful maps) onsite. There are also boat trips on the river to Xuyen Thuy cave, less spectacular than other caves in the area.

listings.name: Khe Coc Island
listings.price: 20,000 dong, 300,000 dong combo ticket with Trang An
listings.description: The former filming location of the village from Kong: Skull Island, repurposed in 2024 as an outdoor cultural museum. There isn't much there yet.

listings.name: Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh
listings.address: Cuc Phuong - Bai Dinh Rd, Ky Phu commune, Nho Quan district
listings.description: It was built by the animal welfare organisation Four Paws opened for visitors in 2019. It covers 5.5 ha, and plans to expand to 10 ha and open an education centre. Different from other sanctuaries, visitors will not be able to enter the whole sanctuary. A path leads the visitors above some enclosures to allow them to observe the bears from a distance.

listings.name: Phat Diem Cathedral
listings.description: Cathedral known for its scale and its oriental style. Completed in 1891. One of the earliest areas to be reached by missionaries; Portuguese priests were here in 1627.

listings.name: Tam Coc
listings.hours: Daily, last boat starts at 17:30 summer, 16:30 winter
listings.price: 150,000 dong per boat (maximum 2 foreigners per boat), plus admission of 120,000 dong per person
listings.description: The most famous landscape of Ninh Binh. Boats begin at the village of Van Lam and proceed through a scenic landscape dominated by rice fields and karst towers. The route includes floating through three natural caves (Hang Cả, Hang Hai, and Hang Ba), the largest of which is 125-m long with its ceiling about 2-m high above the water. Vast limestone cliffs rise out of the rice paddies.

listings.name: Trang An
listings.price: 250,000 dong. Parking fee of 15,000 dong for motorbikes or free for bicycles
listings.description: The most extensive waterway tour in Ninh Binh. Many tourists prefer this trip to Tam Coc as there are many more caves to pass through and not as many hawkers. After buying a ticket, find your way to the boarding area, and decide on your route. (Do not agonize over your decision, as each route includes plenty of temples, caves, and landscapes.) Each is about 3 hours, so make sure to carry sun protection, water and some nibbles (restrooms are available at each temple stop). An employee will pair you to a boat with a rower, and fill the boat with about four passengers (smaller parties will be…

listings.name: Trung Tuyet Restaurant
listings.description: A few tables on the street and one of the few restaurants in the city that caters to Westerners. The menu offers 3 or 4 sizes of portions at different prices, however even the small sized portions are larger than in other towns. Coffee 20,000 dong, Fruit salad 30,000 dong. Yogurt 8,000 dong. Chicken with noodles 50,000 dong.

listings.name: Pho bò 24
listings.description: A small restaurant for locals with the food cooked in front of you. A few tables on the street and few inside. Soups and noodle for 25,000 dong and 30,000 dong. Have an English menu.

listings.name: Aroma Indian Restaurant
listings.description: Indian restaurant which is one of the few in town to have air-con. Excellent Indian food and snappy service. Enormous nan breads! Very reasonable prices given the quality.

listings.name: Chookie's Beer Garden
