listings.description: Great place to relax and have a drink and something to eat away from the main street. Good burgers, salads and Smoothies. Plenty of vegan options too. Has a nice veggie garden and play area. The have another outlet called Chookie Coop, near Mua Cave.

listings.name: Thang Long Restaurant
listings.address: Chi Phong hamlet, Tay Hoa Lu
listings.description: Large restaurant serving local mountain goat dishes, com chay (crispy rice) and hill chicken. Several big dining halls take tour groups, and there is a car park. Set menus can be arranged in advance.

listings.name: Green Papaya Home Stay
listings.address: Ngo 212, No. 54 (still listed on Google as Van Thanh No. 54)

listings.name: Ngoc Anh Hotel
listings.description: Family hotel, friendly staff, good location, rooms are clean, all rooms have air-con, en suite bath, cable TV with good reception, Wi-Fi. Deluxe rooms also have a computer, a fridge and balcony. There are 2 modern computers in the reception/restaurant area. The cheaper rooms are at 26 Luong Van Tuy and the more expensive at 30 Luong Van Tuy.

listings.name: Queen Mini Hotel
listings.description: Near the train and bus station. It's popular, especially with French visitors, and often full. Rooms are clean enough, but can have insects. Wi-Fi in the lobby, but it doesn't reach all the rooms. The owner's refrain is "You pay now". They are affiliated with the Good Food Restaurant across the street. Be warned: there are four hotels sharing this name, and it's not clear if all of them are related: The Queen Mini (this one), the Queen Hotel (across the street, upscale and owned by the same family as the Queen Mini), the New Queen Mini Backpacker's Hostel (on the same street, often has grille…

listings.name: Thanh Binh Hotel
listings.description: Some members of the staff are somewhat helpful and friendly. Possibility to rent motorbikes for USD6/day. Breakfast is not included.

listings.name: Hoa Hung Hotel
listings.description: En suite double rooms with TV.

listings.name: Lam Kinh Hotel
listings.address: Đông Hương new urban zone, Thanh Hoa City
listings.description: Four-star hotel.

listings.name: Phù Đổng Hotel
listings.description: Three-star hotel.

listings.name: Long Anh Hotel
listings.description: A modern, large three-star hotel.

listings.name: Cultural museum of Vietnam ethnic minority groups
listings.description: Kind of a smaller version of the ethnographic museum of Hanoi.

listings.name: Đài phun nước TP. Thái Nguyên
listings.description: Multi-colored fountain right in front of the cultural museum that is a gathering point in the evening.

listings.name: Quảng trường Võ Nguyên Giáp
listings.description: a nationalist type monument with hourglass-like obelisk and town square.

listings.name: Cua Tu Waterfall
listings.description: somewhat dirty forest waterfall

listings.name: Phuong Hoang Cave
listings.description: Riverine cave system and karst formations.

listings.name: Thai Hai Reserve Area of Ecological Houses-on-stilts Ethnic Village
listings.address: Khu du lịch Thái Hải, Thịnh Đức
listings.description: Stilt village ethnic tour.

listings.name: Tan Cuong Tea Cultural Center
listings.address: Tân Cương, Thành phố Thái Nguyên
listings.description: Tea farm tours.

listings.name: Nui Coc Lake
listings.address: Tan Thai Commune Dai Tu District
listings.description: a lake featuring an amusement park on a hill, water park, boat rides, extreme sport activities, sunsets behind tea plantations, and musical water performances. Kind of like a Vietnamese ecotourism area on steroids with concrete Buddhas and dragons everywhere.

listings.name: Habana Hotel Thai Nguyen
listings.address: 318 Quang Trung, Tân Thịnh, Thành phố Thái Nguyên
listings.description: Clean multi-story hotel with pool, spa, restaurant, free breakfast, wifi, spa.

listings.name: Duy Tung/Van Thanh Hotel
listings.description: Has nice rooms.

listings.name: Phuong Dong Hotel
listings.description: OK simple room with motorbike parking and Wi-Fi. Some rooms have a balcony. Not much English.

listings.name: Cao Dai Temple
listings.description: Most tourists arrive for the noon mass. There is a balcony that runs along the walls halfway up. This is where you can watch the service. It is a very nice view. There is an orchestra of approximately 10 musicians whose music is traditionally Vietnamese. A choir of approximately 20 lead the congregation in the prayers. The musical mix of the hymns is very unusual with a blend of Western and Vietnamese. In the front of the temple is the Divine Eye in the shape of a triangle of justice. It is surrounded by flowers on a cosmic globe. On the altar sit 3 glasses of wine, a cup of water and a cup…

listings.name: Dau Tieng Reservoir
listings.description: It was constructed in 1981 to provide water in Tay Ninh province as well as neighboring provinces. The lake covers an area of 27,000 hectares, and it contains up to 1.5 billion m³ of water. The reservoir is set in a beautiful landscape of surrounding of mountains with many islets.

listings.name: Lo Go Xa Mat National Park
listings.description: A short ride from Tay Ninh lays the remnant of a primeval forest that used to cover much of land in Tay Ninh province. Covered 18,675 ha and comprised of lowland forests and wetlands, Lo Go Xa Mat National Park was established in 2002 as a nature reserve. The park boasts a rich biodiversity of flora and fauna, some of which are endangered species. The only protected natural reserve in Tay Ninh, the park is nature’s last stand. On the Cambodian side of the park, very little traces of the forest remained, victim of deforestation. On the Vietnam side, agriculture is rapidly encroaching. See…

listings.name: Ba Den Mountain
listings.description: This mountain is considered the roof of southern Vietnam and often called van son or cloud mountain because it is always covered by clouds. The mountain is made up of three smaller mountains called Heo (pig), Phung (phoenix), and Ba Den (black lady). There is a trip cable car from the bottom of the mountain to the top. Or you can walk the trail. The views of the countryside are breathtaking. There are lunar New Year rituals and festivals that attract about a million visitors yearly. Ba Den Mountain Spring Festival is celebrated 15-18 of the 1st lunar month, should you are here at that time.

listings.name: Feed the Monkeys
listings.description: There are monkeys living in trees on the temple grounds. Feeding the monkeys is a favorite activity for the locals and visitors alike. One can see them dashing about near the seating arenas on the two sides of the big square in front of the temple. Peanuts, fruits, and whatever edible are thrown to the monkeys.

listings.name: Walk the Rubber Plantation
listings.description: There are large tracts of rubber plantations all over Tay Ninh, however, you can visit one right inside the Holy See, saving you the need to go anywhere far. Tracts of rubber fields are planted throughout the Holy See complex. You can take a stroll in any of these fields to experience the production of a rubber plantation in Tay Ninh.

listings.name: Conquer Ba Den Peak
listings.description: For the adventurous souls who wish to reach the very summit of Ba Den Mountain, the 360-degree vista of the surrounding countryside is the ultimate reward. Perching 986 m above sea level, the summit offers a good day's hike. Take a taxi or motorbike taxi halfway up the mountain near the temples entrances. From there, it is a good 2 hr hike to the top. At the summit, some climbing skills are needed to reach the very peak. Bring plenty of water and good hiking shoes.

listings.name: Cánh Ký Noodle House
listings.description: Family-owned for more than 20 years. This noodle house is well-known to locals. Famous for their won ton noodle soups.

listings.name: Phở Mai
listings.description: A decent place to find a good bowl of phở (beef noodle soup). Clean place. Fast service.

listings.name: Tùng Ký Noodle
listings.description: Small, but busy noodle house serving delicious won ton noodles.

listings.name: Cafe Bang Lang
listings.description: Large open space and plenty of seating. This place can be crowded with bureaucrats and office workers in the early morning due to its proximity to all the government and business buildings.

listings.name: Cafe Thao Wind
listings.description: This place offers plenty of tropical greens and misty vapours to cool the soul. Overhead swaying baskets of tropical plants form a natural canopy and trickling water fountains cool the air. A nice place to chill and pass the time.

listings.name: Anh Dao Hotel
listings.description: Older hotel with big rooms.

listings.name: Hoa Binh Hotel
listings.description: The town's main hotel. They have massage service. This hotel is quite run down as it has not been renovated for quite some time.

listings.name: Nha Nghi Quyen
listings.price: Small double rooms are 200,000 dong and a large bedroom with 2 double beds is good value for money at 250,000 dong.

listings.name: Song Lam Hotel
listings.description: They also have massage service.

listings.name: Viet Phuong
listings.description: OK rooms.

listings.name: Ho Chi Minh Square
listings.description: Has a statue of Ho Chi Minh and a fountain.

listings.name: Vinh Recreation Centre
listings.description: Indoor pool, cinema, gym, children's playground, arcade and karaoke machine.

listings.name: Mekong Boat Tour
listings.description: The thing to do in Vinh Long. A typical trip includes the floating market at Cai Be and An Binh Islands lasting about 4 hr.

listings.name: Visit An Binh
listings.description: If you are on budget or you already have done enough boat tours, you can go to An Binh on the ferry (1000 dong, one-way) and either walk on the main islands (small bridges connect nearly all the islands), rent bicycle/moto or pay a mototaxi (40-60,000 dong per hour). Bonsai garden is about 20 min from the ferry pier by motorbike. Near the pier there is a Chinese temple and a school, a bit further on, a church.

listings.name: Lạc Long
listings.description: Decent no frills rooms. Apart from the standard features such as TV, fridge, phone, private bath with hot water, it also has Wi-Fi. All the rooms are available fan or air-con.

listings.name: Phựng Hoàng
listings.description: Choice of comforts as the prices indicate. This place is popular with backpackers. Cheapest room is large and includes TV, fridge, private bath with hot walter, Wi-Fi, and air-con.

listings.name: Bạch Dinh
listings.description: Built by the French (1898-1916) as a summer holiday house for French Governor-General Paul Doumer. Also formerly known as Dinh Toàn Quyền (Villa du Gouverneur). Under French rule, the mansion was a holiday getaway for French governors and Bảo Đại, the last Emperor of Vietnam. During the American War, the mansion was used for R&R. Since the end of the American War, the mansion has been for public use. A mix of French colonial and Vietnamese architecture, Bạch Dinh boasts lavish decorations and a collection of antiques, including fine porcelain and African elephants' tusks.

listings.name: Đài Liệt Sĩ
listings.description: A stone obelisk on a hilltop, on the way to the sea, the Soldiers' Memorial Hill is said to incorporate the biggest traffic circle in Indochina. A cool hangout for lovers.

listings.name: Đình Thần Thắng Tam
listings.description: According to legend, it was built in the Minh Mạng dynasty (1820-1840) as a place to worship the 3 men who set up the 3 villages of Thắng in Vũng Tàu, starting a new way of life. The architecture is particularly interesting around the Tam Quan Gate, the sanctum, the public commune, the meeting room, and the stage for military operas that is skillfully engraved. The sanctum is roofed with ying-yang tiles and is in the shape of “a couple of dragons joking upon the moon” and the pillars are engraved with the shapes of dragons. On the right of Thắng Tam commune is the Whale Tomb where there is a…

listings.name: Statue of Christ the King
listings.description: A must-do with panoramic view! The enormous 28-m figure of Jesus gazing to sea with outstretched arms is at the south end of Small Mountain. Built in 1971, this giant Jesus rests on a 10-m-high platform. The interior of the statue is hollow and contains a spiral staircase of 129 steps, ascending from the foot of the statue to its neck. The two shoulders of the figure are balconies, each able to accommodate up to 4 people, which offer a splendid view of the surrounding landscape. This is the largest sculpture in southern Vietnam. A pathway makes the 30-min hike up the mountain pleasant, and…

listings.name: Pagodas
listings.description: Niết Bàn Tịnh Xá and Thích Ca Phật Đài are most popular among the pagodas and temples in Vũng Tàu.

listings.name: Vũng Tàu Lighthouse
listings.description: When it was built in 1907 on the lower peak of Small Mount, it burned kerosene in its lamp. In 1911, it was rebuilt to 3 m in diameter and 18 m in height, and moved to the higher peak where it stands today. The Vũng Tàu Lighthouse projects light as far as 65 km (35 mi) and is equipped with telescopes to follow and direct ships at sea. Next to the platform, 4 old French cannons (weighing several tons) were once used to defend the area from naval attacks. The lighthouse affords a panoramic view of the whole of Vung Tau.

listings.name: Robert Taylor Museum of Worldwide Arms
listings.description: A fascinating collection of arms and uniforms from around the world. Most major wars and battles are covered. The emphasis is in British and Australian regimental uniforms but there are also Samurai, Mongols, Saracens, Turks and Bulgarians as well as most European and North American armies. There is a wide range of guns, swords and other weapons of war. Quite why Bob Taylor chose to open his museum in the relative obscurity of Vung Tau is not clear from the collection but if you have even a passing interest in military history it is well worth a couple of hours of your time if you find…

listings.name: Ho May Park
listings.address: 1A Trần Phú, Phường 1, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa
listings.description: Fun day out if you have kids (quite fun even if you don't!). Dodgems, Go-Karts, various fairground rides, a large water park, a games centre, the 'Alpine Luge' and other attractions are all included in the cost!

listings.name: Lam Son Greyhound Racing Stadium
listings.price: 60,000 dong (slightly more for VIP tickets - worthwhile)
listings.description: A fun evening if you don't have hang ups about dogs racing. You are given a 'form card' and can use that to bet on races. Either 'slum it' with the locals next to the track or go VIP for an air-conditioned experience. Beers are a little more than in local bars but not much more so. A good place to engage with locals and expats alike!

listings.name: Bãi Dâu
listings.description: Small beach on the west side of Big Mount.

listings.name: Bãi Dứa
listings.description: Small beach along Hạ Long St, by Small Mount.

listings.name: Bãi Sau
listings.price: Locker 15,000 dong, beach umbrella 30,000 dong, chaise longue 25,000 dong, deck chair and umbrella 50,000 dong, fresh water showers 8,000 dong
listings.description: Also known as Thùy Vân Beach. The only standard beach for tourism in Vung Tau. It is 3 km long and stretches from the Small Mount to Paradise Park. All beaches here are free. You must pass through some "water parks" to get to the beach in some places, in most places there is a pleasant promenade that leads directly to the beach. The beach is clean, the water is shallow quite a way out, there are very few jet-skis and hardly any beach hawkers. Sea parachuting and canoeing available all day.

listings.name: Bãi Trước
listings.description: Restaurants, kiosks, and hotels are close to the beach. Front Beach is connected through a small park called Front Beach Park. As this lies near the tourist centre of the city, most people come here to visit the park and view the sunset when it becomes hugely popular with local tourists.

listings.name: Long Hải
listings.description: A nearby seaside town. The beach here is smaller, but the town owns a local goddess temple called "Dinh Cô" which holds an annual cultural festival called "Dinh Cô Festival". It is one of the three well-known traditional festivals in southern Vietnam. The town also features Minh Đạm Tunnel, a former hideout of the Viet Minh during the wars.

listings.name: Long Sơn
listings.description: Head here for the wooden Nhà Lớn Long Sơn complex dating from the 19th century.

listings.name: Bánh Khọt 368
listings.description: Inexpensive Bánh Khọt in a simple but friendly restaurant.

listings.name: Bà Hai's Restaurant
listings.description: A small Bánh Khọt restaurant run by a family.

listings.name: Bò Kho
listings.description: Delicious Vietnamese goulash (Bò Kho) served with a Bánh mì and salad.

listings.name: Sủi Cảo
listings.description: They call it Sủi Cảo, but it is similar to, if not the same as Hoành Thánh Mỳ, i.e. Wonton dumplings, served in Hoi An. 4 dumplings prepared in soup or deep-fried.

listings.name: Hùng - Hủ Tiếu Mực
listings.description: Friendly local restaurant serving squid soup (Hủ Tiếu Mực).

listings.name: Quan Su Bin - Bò Lá Lốt
listings.description: Grilled minced beef rolled into wine leaves. You take that and vegetables, roll them into rice paper and dip them into sweet and salt sauce for final consumption. The owner ladies are not particularly friendly, but don't let spoil you meal.

listings.name: Loan Cháo Lòng
listings.description: Intestines porridge, for people how like experimenting and to experience the full range of Vietnamese cuisine.

listings.name: Bistro Nine
listings.description: Bistro style, open early for breakfast until late for dinner. Large wine cellar, bakery, house-made excellent bread and charcuterie. Nice place to chill out for coffee or dinner. Sandwiches, wood oven pizzas, meats, fish, great ribs.

listings.name: David Pizzeria
listings.description: An Italian restaurant with a wide selection of pasta, wood-fired pizza, seafood, wine, and Italian desserts. They also have fresh bread, coffees. Delivery available.

listings.name: Nhà hàng Kozak
listings.description: Ukrainian restaurant, decorated with Ukrainian stuff. Restaurant offers traditional beverages: Ukrainian liquors, borsht, vareniki, kvass.

listings.name: Vườn Bàng
listings.description: Large indoor restaurant, ideal place for parties. Special foods include shashlyk (Russian fried pork) and Russian salad.

listings.name: Matilda's Pub
listings.description: Laidback Aussie pub. The cheapest beers/drinks in town. Very affordable meals, including breakfast. Happy hour every day from 09:00-18:00. Very friendly staff. An excellent place to enjoy a relaxing beer or meal.

listings.name: Mr Splash Cocktail Bar
listings.description: Makes amazing coffee, tea and cocktails at very affordable prices. Very professional, and Phú is a proper bartender.

listings.name: Bistro Nine
listings.description: Espresso, cappuccino, fresh juice and home made French ice cream. Indoor-outdoor.

listings.name: Belly's Restaurant and Watering Hole
listings.description: Belly's is a super friendly Aussie pub that also serves excellent food. Relax with a game of pool, watch the footy or chat with the regulars. Great, friendly and efficient staff.

listings.name: Cafe Rin
listings.description: Serves a decent cup of strong, dark, and rich aromatic coffee. Said to serve only coffees that are grown directly from Vietnam highland provinces. The beans here are kept fresh and are ground only on order. Popular for to go orders among locals and tourists alike.

listings.name: Vungtau Surf Hostel
listings.description: Nice lounge and decent dorms. Offers all the tours and surfing.

listings.name: Tomorrow Hostel
listings.description: Good rating and central location.

listings.name: The Imperial Hotel
listings.description: 5-star hotel. Victorian English-style architecture. Includes a private beach, 300 rooms, four on-site restaurants, meeting rooms, ballrooms, and manicured gardens.

listings.name: Pullman Vung Tau
listings.address: 15 Thi Sach Street, Thang Tam Ward, Vung Tau, Vietnam
listings.description: A hotel and convention building, Pullman offers big hotel rooms with modern designs like no other. It has a swimming pool at the side of the building which is very windy. It is near the Lotte Mall, which is east of one of Vung Tau famous beaches ; Bãi Sau beach.

listings.name: A1 hill, Vietnam Military History Museum and cemetery
D1 hill
listings.address: at Tran Dang Ninh and Duong 7-5/AH13/QL 279
listings.description: A set of giant stairs. This site contains a monument wall, statue and great views of the valley on all sides.

listings.name: The Light House Club
listings.address: Mường Thanh Hotel, Võ Nguyên Giáp Road
listings.description: This nightclub serves cheap beer (35,000 dong) and plays improbably loud electronic music.

listings.name: Ba Na Hill Station
listings.price: You need to get a taxi to Suoi Mo Station (US$25 one-way from Da Nang) then pay 750,000 dong per adult (500,000 dong for children between 1-1.3 m tall, free admission for children under 1 m tall) for the ticket to the cable car and the Fantasy Park
listings.description: Ba Na is 1,487 m above sea level in the Truong Son Mountains. In the 1920s, it was a French resort that boasted 200 villas, restaurants, and clubs. It is known as the second Dalat or Sa Pa in central Vietnam. Its temperate climate, unspoiled forest, and spectacular views over the South China Sea and the Lao mountains made Ba Na a popular retreat for both the French and the wealthy Vietnamese. Today the area still attracts locals and tourists alike thanks to a cable car system that was opened in 2009 and set two Guinness World Records for its height and length. Great view from the top but it's…

listings.name: Golden Bridge
listings.description: A 150m long pedestrian bridge, used as viewpoint. A notable feature is the hands sculpture that support the bridge.

listings.name: Dragon Bridge
listings.description: A 2013 bridge built in the shape of a dragon, breathing fire and water each Saturday and Sunday night at 21:00.

listings.name: Han River Promenade
listings.description: The beauty of the Han River has inspired poets and composers throughout Da Nang's history, and any local will probably be able to sing you a few lines of Sông Hàn Tình Yêu Của Tôi (Han River, My Love) as they stroll the edge of the water. The promenade on the western bank of the river is well built up, stretching from the Dragon Bridge in the south to the city port in the north. The promenade passes underneath the famous Han River Bridge, a swing bridge built in the late-1990s, one of four bridges across the Han you can glimpse from here (the others are the Thuan Phuoc, Dragon, and Tran Thi…

listings.name: Linh Ung Temple
listings.description: Located on Son Tra Mountain and clearly visible from My Khe Beach, this temple has stunning views of the sea, the sky, and a 67-m tall statue of "Quan The Am" (Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy) facing the ocean. The pagoda was built in 2010.

listings.name: Marble Mountains
listings.price: 40,000 dong but may enter for free if arriving before 08:00; tickets for a ride up by elevator are 15,000 dong
listings.description: The group includes Kim Son (Mountain of Metal), Moc Son (Mountain of Wood), Thuy Son (Mountain of Water), Hoa Son (Mountain of Fire), and Tho Son (Mountain of Earth). Several Buddhist temples have been built into the caves and grottoes, and it's a popular pilgrimage site. The real fun, though, is at the Am Phu cave, where you can make the steep climb up toward the light and a view from the top of the mountain, surrounded by approving sacred images; or head in the opposite direction, physically and spiritually, down to the crude Hieronymous Bosch-esque statues of sinners getting their due in…

listings.name: Museum of Cham Sculpture
listings.description: Founded in 1915 by the École Française d'Extrême Orient, it houses a collection of stone sculptures from the Hindu-practicing Cham civilization, which occupied much of central Vietnam in the first millennium CE to about the 14th century. The museum can be toured in about an hour. The sculptures are nearly all made of sandstone, and some have weathered badly over the centuries, but you can still appreciate the delightful artistic quality of the figures, which include shiva, garudas, nagas, lions, monkeys, and elephants. The collection also includes striking examples of the ancient Hindu icons…

listings.name: My Khe Beach
listings.description: Across the Han River from the city centre, My Khe Beach is a wide, sandy beach long known for its beauty. Locals will often gather here as early in the morning as 05:00 to enjoy the surf while the sun rises over the ocean. Tourists often arrive later on, when the locals have already started their day; you'll probably find that by 09:00 or 10:00 the beach is mostly deserted. An even larger local crowd gathers in the late afternoon, with folks wading, picnicking and strolling along the beach well into the night. The beach isn't steep, meaning that you can swim far out and still feel your feet…

listings.name: Motorbike ride up Monkey Mountain
listings.description: If you feel like a ride with an amazing view, rent a motorbike and make your way up the side of Monkey Mountain (aka Son Tra Mountain), where an American army base used to be. Although access to the base is closed off, you can still follow Hoang Sa Rd. for a good distance and enjoy getting lost in the beautiful scenery on this road that hugs the mountainside while offering an expansive view of the Pacific Ocean. You can also stop off at Linh Ung Temple along the way, both to pay your respects to Quan The Am and to enjoy the wonderful view.

listings.name: Ride a motorbike up the Hai Van Pass
listings.description: The Hai Van Pass is a great day trip from Da Nang (or Hoi An). The road was called "a deserted ribbon of perfection—one of the best coast roads in the world" in the BBC show Top Gear. Since the tunnel opened, most heavy traffic has diverted from the pass, making the ride much safer, and you'll only meet a few trucks ferrying live animals or dangerous goods, plus quite a few motorbikers coming to enjoy the views. Make sure you ride down the north side of the pass all the way to Lang Co and enjoy the view of the lagoon set against a background of mountains. Make sure you fill up your tank…

listings.name: Phở 29 - Phở Hà Nội
listings.description: Bun cha, banh xeo and the fried rice are nice. Huge portions and good staff with customer service. Nice ambient sidestreet seating and many drink choices.

listings.name: Edo Sushi
listings.address: 27 Thái Phiên, Phước Ninh, Hải Châu
listings.description: Budget Japanese restaurant. The dishes are diverse. Most of the staff are students.

listings.name: Cơm gà A.Hải
listings.address: 100 Thái Phiên, Phước Ninh, Hải Châu
listings.description: Typical basic Vietnamese restaurant. The chicken rice that the locals also enjoy is nice. Both the roast chicken and thinly steamed chicken rice are tasty. The chicken soup served first is also tasty.

listings.name: Bánh Mì̀ Bà Lan
listings.address: 62 Trưng Nữ Vương, Bình Hiên, Hải Châu
listings.description: One of the most famous sandwich carts in the city. Try their bánh mì que which is a string baguette filled with a pork pâté.

listings.name: Mi Quang 1A
listings.address: 1 Hải Phòng, Hải Châu 1, Q. Hải Châu
listings.description: Mi Quang 1A is one of the best known mì quảng restaurants in the area. While still good it has lost a bit of its luster over the years. Prices are higher than most places at 30,000 to 45,000 dong (Jan 2018). Make sure you are in Mi Quang 1A as there is a "copycat" place next door. Before going in grab a fresh sugarcane juice from the cart in the front.

listings.name: Bún Mắm Vân
listings.address: 23/14 Trần Kế Xương, Hải Châu 2, Hải Châu
listings.description: Bún mắm is an extremely pungent noodle dish made with a fermented fish sauce called mắm nêm. Mắm nêm can best be described as "smells like hell, tastes like heaven." Bún Mắm Vân is in what is called "Bún Mắm Alley" where a few bún mắm shops have congregated. You can smell this alley from a block away. Try the bún mắm thịt quay or bún mắm with roasted pork. If you are put off by the smell of strong fish sauce this is not the place for you. If you like bún mắm this place is heaven.

listings.name: Kenta Vietnamese cuisine & coffee
listings.description: Hot pho. Very good food. They offer a vegetarian version of bun (cold vermicelli noodles) on request. The lemongrass and chilli tofu is nice. Amazingly friendly service. Warm people. Nice cozy environment.

listings.name: H Coffee
listings.description: Recommended is the Bo ne Viet Nam steak. Bahn mi is good. The setting is quite tranquil with open spaces in a natural setting away from the hustle and bustle of the city life. The staff are nice people.

listings.name: Taco NGON
listings.description: Small taco restaurant. The tacos are nice (recommended is the BBQ pork), as are the fresh fries and the tortilla chips. If you're expecting them to open a pack of Doritos and put it on the plate, you're wrong. They fry the tortilla chips to order so they come warm and full of flavour. The owner is enthusiastic and always smiling. It's no stress and has a curbside street food vibe.

listings.name: Pho Viet Kieu
listings.description: Local restaurant. Nice Pho. Still there's rice, so if you don't like pho, you can enjoy it. The menu is diverse. The owners are friendly.

listings.name: Cơm Nhà Linh
listings.description: Delicious food, true to the homemade style, suitable for the North. The set menu is full of meat, fish, soup, vegetables, peanuts and eggs. If you are craving something local, they don't disappoint. Great experience to grill your own meat at the table. The service might be a bit slow though.

listings.name: Thìa Gỗ Restaurant Da Nang
listings.description: Real Vietnamese cuisine. Good food. Nice pho. Many traditional Vietnamese street food dishes done in a more comfortable setting. The location is little bit hidden. Very friendly staff.

listings.name: Chân Gà Nướng Hai Còi - Delicious BBQ Chicken
listings.description: Hai Còi is a local restaurant. There are 3 locations with the same boss. Still, the original house seems to be the best one. The stir-fried noodles are good. The chicken wings are very good, seasoned and grilled over charcoal fire.

listings.name: Kangaroo Bar and Burger
listings.description: Good for brunch. The pancakes are delicious. And the yogurt and fruit menu is very good. A lot of Vietnamese people come here to eat. Excellent service, quality and kindness.

listings.name: Bún mắm Bé Hà
listings.description: Great local place. Casual restaurant. The Bun Mam is good. The rice crackers are recommended. From afar, you can already smell the fish sauce. If you are a foreign tourist this is a good choice.

listings.name: Quán Thảo
listings.address: 135, Dương Trí Trạch, An Hải Bắc, Sơn Trà
listings.description: Traditional street food establishment frequented mostly by locals for breakfast, on a quiet side road. While Ms Thảo serves Mì Quảng or [Province of] Quảng style noodles, she's known for her bún bò or beef noodle soup. Some like to add a baguette for an additional 5,000 dong.

listings.name: Quán Dung Mỳ Quảng
listings.address: 99 Nguyễn Thị Định, An Hải Bắc, Q. Sơn
listings.description: Well known for their mì quảng cá lóc, the best known noodle dish of Đà Nẵng, served with broad rice noodles, fresh greens, a broth seasoned with turmeric, shallots and garlic topped and with peanuts. It is served in a shallow and pungent pool of broth unlike its better known cousin phở, which is milder and fills the bowl. Cá lóc is snakehead fish; when prepared correctly, which this place is known for, has a mild flavour and very light texture. Take some of the fresh greens and stir them into the broth to give them a bit of warmth and flavour making this dish half salad and half soup. Menu…

listings.name: Red Sky Bar and Restaurant
listings.description: An expat-run Western restaurant. The food is nice, always delicious with generous portions. The staff are good. Prices are above average by Vietnamese standards, but not too expensive for the quality of food and service received.

listings.name: Hải sản Mộc quán
listings.description: Seafood. Busy and crowded with locals.

listings.name: Happy Heart Cafe
listings.address: 57 Đ. Ng. Thì Sĩ, Bắc Mỹ An
listings.description: Tasty food, friendly people.

listings.name: Pizza 4P's Hoang Van Thu
listings.description: Great Restaurant. Good location, superb service and very tasteful food.

listings.name: Torino Restaurant & Bakery
listings.description: Italian food. The pizza dough is excellent.

listings.name: Com Nieu Nha Do
listings.description: Cơm niêu is a type of rice that's baked in a clay pot and served with any number of sides — beef, chicken, fish, hot pot — but it's the way it's served that catches your attention. Waiters come out of the kitchen bearing hot clay pots straight out of the oven, pull out hammers, smash them at your table, and fling the crusty, baked rice inside back and forth across the room. Otherwise, the food is what you'd get at a normal restaurant, but it's fun to see the show. There are many of these restaurants on Nguyen Tri Phuong St, but this one is a favourite.

listings.name: Bambino
listings.description: Quiet location, good food wine selection. Australian steak grilled to order. International, French and local foods, run by a French couple. A good place for a quiet meal with friends.

listings.name: Limoncello
listings.description: Great Italian food with homemade limoncello.

listings.name: Memory Lounge
listings.description: Quite possibly the most expensive place to go for coffee in Da Nang. The high-end Memory Lounge overlooks the river — in fact, it was built directly on top, jutting out onto the river and accessible from the promenade. Built by the wife of a former president of South Vietnam, it's quite a fancy affair — with foreign chefs blending Asian and European cuisines and using organic and sustainable ingredients to create an impressive menu.

listings.name: Ngoc Huong
listings.description: A typical but tasty live seafood neon emporium, with the motto "there is no seafood that is not available", as a glance at the nightmare fuel giant isopod tank will confirm. Fear not, they also have everything else from shrimp to imported Alaskan king crab, plus a wide variety of local molluscs, hotpot, and more.

listings.name: Dac San Tra Tien
listings.address: 46 Nhon Hoa 17, Hoa An, Cam Le
listings.description: Whether you're a tea lover or just looking to try something new, Da Nang Pineapple and Jasmine Tea is a must-try beverage that will leave you feeling refreshed and satisfied. So, come to Da Nang and indulge in this delicious and unique tea experience.

listings.name: Bamboo Bar 2
listings.description: Popular haunt for expats. Bamboo 2's owner speaks excellent English, there are always foreigners there.

listings.name: Festival Disco
listings.description: The newest disco and the only one on the My Khe Beach side of the river. It's part of a complex with a restaurant and karaoke rooms. If you buy the staff a drink here (a normal thing to do in this kind of disco-night club) they can be very aggressive about drinking it fast and running up a big bill for you.

listings.name: Golden Pine
listings.description: This is a popular bar opposite Memory Lounge on the river side. Open till 04:00 or last customer, they play music on request from customers. Lots of regulars here and a casual vibe.

listings.name: Green Town Bar
listings.description: One of relatively few bars open past the witching hour and most expats drop in there for either an early evening or late night drink. The view is excellent with an outdoor terrace and 2 big pool tables inside. The prices are very reasonable. Food is available until 22:00.

listings.name: New Phuong Dong Disco
listings.description: New Phuong Dong has a resident Ghanaian DJ and many visiting singers from Saigon and Hanoi.

listings.name: Red Hot Bar
listings.description: A real late night place. ("Late night" is more flexible in Da Nang than in Hanoi. Most of the time discos and places like Red Hot, an approximations of a Thai girlie-bar, close at 01:00 or 01:30, but if the police decide to crack down, they may unexpectedly close at midnight or 00:30).

listings.name: Ngoi Café
listings.description: A inexpensive and comfortable little café.

listings.name: Ca Fe 49
listings.description: Ca Fe 49 is a simple, family-run, outdoor cafe serving excellent coffee at a good price. Enjoy a "cà phê sữa đá Đà Nẵng" while enjoying a quiet view. The husband and wife owners are friendly. Recommend if you are out in Sơn Trà.

listings.name: Long Coffee
listings.description: Crazy popular cà phê cóc-style coffee shop in Da Nang that serves and sells its own brand of coffee—not the best, according to some, but very popular with locals. It's always busy, noisy and smoky, but that's part of the atmosphere. Go there with a local friend to shoot the breeze and enjoy a quintessential Vietnamese experience.

listings.name: Café Vi Lan
listings.description: Comfortable, typical coffee shop that plays soft music and plays HBO movies on mute. Upper floor is air-conditioned.

listings.name: Hai Quynh Café
listings.description: Known as the "Rock Coffee Shop", where you can enjoy coffee and listen to rock music at the same time. You can request songs. Usually, they play ballads and soft rock in the daytime and hard rock and metal in the evening (very loudly).

listings.name: Tuy Anh Chinese Chess Coffee Shop
listings.description: Hangout for coffee-drinking Chinese chess enthusiasts.

listings.name: Trúc Lâm Viên
listings.description: Pleasant garden-style café. Food is a little expensive; worth it mainly for the décor. Tends to be busy.

listings.name: Danang Backpackers Hostel
listings.description: Cheap, clean and spacious hostel. Breakfast included, free playing billiards, free beer every night, fast Wi-Fi. Comfy beds, A/C, hot shower. English speaking staff 24/7.

listings.name: Dang Viet Hotel
listings.description: Air-con, comfortable beds, fast Wi-Fi, hot showers, refrigerator and international cable TV. Staff speak English.

listings.name: Funtastic Hostel
listings.description: Modern hostel with comfy beds, big lockers, good Wi-Fi and friendly English speaking staff. Breakfast on the rooftop, with some nice views, is included and the hostel offers a free daily shuttle to Hoi An and airport dropoff.

listings.name: Funtastic Beach Hostel
listings.address: 5 Hà Bổng, Phước Mỹ, Sơn Trà
listings.description: Sister hostel to the Funtastic [City] Hostel on Hai Phong and very similar except it's a three minute walk to the beach. Excellent staff most of which speak English. Ask them about their local restaurant suggestions and their food tour.

listings.name: Nhà Nghỉ Cát Tường
listings.address: 278 Lê Đại Hành, Hòa Thọ Đông, Cẩm Lệ
listings.description: Cheap, but nice guesthouse with Wi-Fi, hot water, air-con. Possibly closed. Call first.

listings.name: Thien Duc Motel
listings.description: An OK option, although services are far from superior.

listings.name: Danang Carpe Diem Hostel
listings.address: Dinh Thi Hoa Street, An Hai Bac Ward, Son Tra District
listings.description: Complimentary breakfast consisting of specialities, sausage, bacon, ham, fresh fruits, eggs any style, bread and homemade jam every morning. High security standard of key card access, free wifi in all area, big lockers, free luggage storage on check out day and quick laundry service.Front desk is always available,

listings.name: Sea Wonder Hotel
listings.address: 57 Nguyen Cong Sau, Phước Mỹ, Sơn Trà
listings.description: The Sea Wonder is similar to other basic hotels in the area. The great advantage is that it's on a beautiful and quiet street very near the beach, cafes, taxis and street food. The rooms are clean and the staff friendly. A taxi into the city can be found one street over and costs less than US$2.

listings.name: Conical Hats Homestay
listings.address: 1, Nguyễn Công Sáu, Phước Mỹ, Sơn Trà
listings.description: Conical Hats Homestay is a family-run, budget, long-term homestay also available for weekly rentals. Located in a new building it's situated in a quiet neighborhood and only a five minute walk to the beach. While lacking some amenities it offers a pleasant change to staying in a hotel or hostel offering a kitchen on the first floor. Lots of great street food and coffee right out the door. The staff is helpful, friendly and speak some English. Email them for details.

listings.name: Rom Casa Da Nang
listings.address: Lot 26 An Thuong 4, Ngu Hanh Son, Da Nang
listings.price: US$12 for dorm beds, US$30 for private rooms (double beds)
listings.description: Unique hostel offering private rooms and dorms in... shipping containers! Pool as well is made out of a container. Rooftop terrace. Common room with board games and table football. Library. Free WiFi accessible from the whole property. All rooms feature AC, lockers, reading lamps, power sockets. On site bar. Working space. Very clean, modern & eco-friendly hostel. Very friendly staff members who speak excellent English.

listings.name: Dai A Hotel
listings.address: 51, Yen Bai St, Hai Chau District
listings.description: A friendly old hotel. The owner is involved with charity. You can visit "the Northwind Broom Workshop" and "Bo Mung Orphanage".

listings.name: My Khe Beach Hotel 1 and 2
listings.price: From US$18, breakfast included, air-con room with refrigerator and private bath (My Khe 1) or shower (My Khe 2)
listings.description: These old-school low-rise hotels, both under the same management, are comfortable and very reasonably priced especially given that they are just the other side of the beach road from My Khe Beach, but still only a five minute or less moto ride from downtown. My Khe 1 is older, has smaller rooms, but the electricity does not go off in the room when you leave; My Khe 2 has very large rooms, caters more to groups of Saigon tourists (My Khe gets lots of Vietnamese business and government travellers, plus some tourists and some Lao visitors, business or government). Staff at both places are…

listings.name: Night Sky Hotel
listings.description: Opened early 2015. Large Samsung TV with lots of good reception cable TV channels. Free breakfast included. Nice quiet location but a little out of town. Their free bicycles more than makes up for that.

listings.name: Red Beach Resort and Spa
listings.address: Nguyen Tat Thanh St, Hoa Hiep Nam Ward, Lien Chieu District
listings.description: All rooms are equipped with LCD TV with cable channels, balcony/lanai/terrace, Air conditioning, complimentary breakfast, private toilet, and bath. Restaurant, spa, swimming pool, Pearl Island tour and water sports facilities.

listings.name: Sanouva Danang Hotel
listings.description: The Sanouva Danang Hotel is a city hotel at the center of Danang.

listings.name: Sao Minh Business Hotel
listings.description: Spacious and cosy rooms, all equipped with air conditioning, TV with cable channels, and mini-bar. Facilities include business centre, restaurant, and bar.

listings.name: Furama Resort
listings.description: One of the first five-star resorts built in Da Nang, and thus unusually spacious. 198 rooms and suites. The resort has its own dive centre, spa, and health centre. Club Tourane opens daily from 20:00-02:00 with a Filipino Band. Hai Van Lounge serves cocktails and light snacks. Many restaurants.

listings.name: Grand Tourane Hotel
listings.address: 252 Vo Nguyen Giap, Son Tra District
listings.description: The hotel includes 189 rooms with 22 floors. It offers 2 conference rooms, restaurant with Asia and Western food. Its facilities include spa and swimming pool, tennis court, fitness room/gym, bar, and café.

listings.name: Hyatt Regency Da Nang
listings.address: Truong Sa St, Hoa Hai Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District
listings.description: 200 comfortable rooms and 27 ocean-view villas.

listings.name: InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort
listings.description: This might be the finest hotel in the city. It's where US President Trump, Russian President Putin and other world officials stayed during the 2017 APEC conference. Located in a very secluded area and has a private beach.

listings.name: Pullman Danang Beach Resort
listings.address: Truong Sa St, Ngu Hanh Son District

listings.name: Radisson Danang
listings.description: Opened 2022, this skinny high-rise across the road from the beach typifies the latest wave of hotels in Da Nang. The regular rooms are nothing special, but the spacious corner suites with wraparound balconies have amazing views across the bay and are available in both 2 and 4 person configurations. Solid breakfast buffet and more great views from the rooftop pool/bar on the 21st floor.

listings.name: Sala Danang Beach Hotel
listings.address: 36-38 Lam Hoanh Street, Son Tra District

listings.name: TIA Wellness Resort
listings.description: Resort with pool villas, offering complimentary wellness classes.

listings.name: Smiling Buddha
listings.address: Nam Ban, Lam Ha, Lam Dong
listings.description: A happy Buddha statue that is almost 50 feet tall.

listings.name: Me Linh Coffee Garden
listings.address: To 20 thon 4, Ta Nung, Tp. Da Lạt, Lam Dong
listings.description: Surrounded by coffee plantation

listings.name: Dong Hoi Citadel Gates
listings.description: Only two gates and a moat remain of the citadel. You can climb up in the gates, but inside you will find syringes, burnt debris, and feces.

listings.name: Tam Toa Church
listings.description: Tam Toa church is a bombed-out ruin. Only the facade remains, behind some iron gates.

listings.name: Blind Massage Therapy Center
listings.description: Enjoy a massage by the blind while soft, sultry saxophone music echoes in the corridor. Not all the employees are actually blind, as they sometimes check and write text messages on their phones during the massage, but it has been claimed that they are all legally blind. Good energetic massage by properly trained people.

listings.name: Nhat Le Beach
listings.description: Although Nhat Le Beach is nearby, the focus of Dong Hoi is on the river. Accordingly, you will find the beach to be generally empty and abandoned, with just a few hotels, construction work, and piles of dirt. The beach is pleasant, but the current is strong and the waves often too powerful for swimming.

listings.name: Paradise Cave
listings.description: A huge cave with thousands of stalactites and stalagmites of amazing size and shape. Paradise Cave is a rewarding trip, as it is not touristy and the spotlights are white, not coloured. The best way to get there is by motorbike as the scenery is amazing. Motorbikes and cars with drivers can be rented in Dong Hoi at many hotels. Booking a tour in Dong Hoi is possible as well and a very common way to see the caves. Paradise Cave takes around 2 hours to visit.

listings.name: Phong Nha Caves
listings.price: 80,000 dong, boat for 320,000 dong (sharable with 14 people);
listings.description: Visit the largest and most stunning cave in Vietnam. The cave is nearly 55 km long but visitors can only access the first kilometre. Look out for pictures of the caves and learn the Vietnamese names (Phong Nha is the national park, not just the cave). Phong Nha Caves take around 3½ hours to tour.

listings.name: 7th Heaven Restaurant
listings.description: Large menu featuring primarily Western food (steaks, burgers, grilled honey-chicken, etc.) as well as Vietnamese and Thai selections for a hefty price.

listings.name: Cheese
listings.description: An inexpensive and innovative little restaurant serving Korean-style dishes. However, they also have spaghetti and fish-less maki aka sushi rolls. The spaghetti sauce is a little sweet, so it is worth mentioning beforehand that they should omit any sweet-tasting sauce when preparing them.

listings.name: Nhu Y
listings.description: Good Vietnamese food. They have English menu.

listings.name: QB Teen
listings.description: They have Vietnamese and Western food such as pizza, pasta, burgers, and chips. Also very nice fruit shakes, and English menu.

listings.name: Tree Hugger Café
listings.description: Little nice café in central Dong Hoi. The menu is small but features fresh drinks and simple light food options. Good for learning more about Dong Hoi as well as handicraft store on the second floor. Tour bookings also available.

listings.name: Bar Hoang De
listings.description: Discotheque, cocktails, beer, coffee, fruit shakes.

listings.name: Coco's Coffee Bar Classic
listings.description: Free Wi-Fi, coffee, fruit juices, breakfast.

listings.name: Geminai Bistro
listings.description: One of the best coffee shop in Dong Hoi. Pretty chill atmosphere with cool music and not too loud. Good place for cocktail.

listings.name: Mau Hong Hotel
listings.description: Clean and cheap rooms, good location. Rooms with balcony overlook the river. Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Nam Long Hotel
listings.description: They have only 2 kinds of room, 1 double bed with balcony or 1 double bed and 1 single bed with window. All rooms have cable TV, fridge, air-con, and Wi-Fi. Owners speak decent English.

listings.name: Sun Spa Resort
listings.description: This is the only luxury resort in Dong Hoi. Many lodging choices, from rooms to 3 bedroom bungalows.

listings.name: Anh Linh Hotel
listings.description: Very good hotel. Staff friendly, accommodating and English speaking. Recommended as they are more customer-oriented than most hotels in this price range in Vietnam (May 2014).

listings.name: Beachside Backpackers
listings.description: Budget accommodation - dorms and private rooms, beachside bar and restaurant, hammocks, kayaks, surfboards, volleyball. Bicycles and motorbikes available. On the bus route to Phong Nha.

listings.name: Geminai Hotel & Cafe
listings.description: Best location look out Nhat Le river, cave tour booking, laundry service. On-site restaurant and bar. Western, local and vegetarian dishes, beer, shisha.

listings.name: Fairy Bosom
listings.description: Two even hills lying side by side, with a bra made of trees.

listings.name: Lung Ho Fort
listings.description: Ruins of a French military post constructed in 1935.

listings.name: Lung Khuy Caves
listings.description: A large karst cavern located near Quan Ba. The cave was originally used locally for its spring, but was opened for tourist sightseeing several years ago by the national government. A dedicated non-slip footpath has been installed with handrailings. The cave has many stunning features, including stalagmites, stalactites, flowstone, and drapery. The cave is a half-hour hike up from the parking lot and admission is only by cash, but is owned collectively by the local village.

listings.name: Khau Làn waterfall
listings.description: A short and steep trail leads to a secluded 20 m waterfall and swimming hole.

listings.name: Quản Bạ Pass
listings.description: The road to Quan Ba Heaven gate is winding, twisty crossing limestone mountains. At 1945 m, the viewpoints on both sides of the pass is one of the highlights of the park. From the top of the Heaven Gate, you can look down across a large valley of unending terraced fields, displaying a charming beauty like a paradise dimly visible through the clouds.

listings.name: Thâm Luông Waterfall
listings.description: Two large and several smaller cascades, one with a pond for swimming. Somewhat remote, the gravel path can be difficult to find.

listings.name: Dong Van Old Town
listings.description: The quarter was built in the early 20th century and has a few families of the Hmong, Tay still living in it. The oldest house is the house of Luong family, built in 1860. The common architecture here is the two-story house and yin and yang roofs. Hostels and hotels are common, but may fill up quickly in peak season. Saturday nights, the plaza has a community party. On Sunday mornings there is a regional market—arrive before 9am to see locals shopping, and after for tourist wares.

listings.name: Dong Van Fort
listings.description: Above Dong Van, the French built a fort in 1925. The remains, partially restored in 2013, overlook the entire town.

listings.name: Hmong King Palace
listings.address: Sa Phin commune, Dong Van district
listings.description: This historical landmark of the local Hmong ethnic group was built in the early 20th century in the form of the letter 王 (meaning "king" in English). Vuong King (Vuong Chinh Duc) became rich from dealing goods, especially opium, as Sa Phin is in the middle of the Golden Triangle region. The building imitates ancient Chinese architecture from the Man Thanh dynasty, and features carvings in Hoa Nam style. The 1120 m² grounds were chosen for feng shui, and also sight lines, as it was also a military fortress. Duc set up his own army unit of loyal Hmong people and equipped them with weapons, some…

listings.name: Làng Văn Tourist Village
listings.description: This village showcases minority culture. The turnoff to the right is clearly marked by a labeled gate.

listings.name: Lung Cu Flag Tower
listings.address: Lung Cu commune, Dong Van district
listings.description: Built on the top of Dragon Mountain, and modeled on the flag tower of Hanoi. Plug in the 12.9 m flagstaff is a national flag with an area of 54m², representing for 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. At the foot tower, there is a commemorative house, where displays production tools, costumes and cultural products of the ethnic groups in Ha Giang. From distances, Lung Cu is very spectacular with three quarters of the land covered with stone, a national flag pole erected on the top of the mountain, which is surrounded with magnificent and majestic mountain forests at 1,600 m above sea level.

listings.name: Ma Pi Leng Pass
listings.address: Pai Lung commune, Meo Vac district, on National Road 4C connecting Dong Van and Meo Vac districts
listings.description: Ma Pi Leng is a high mountain pass on the famous Sky Path. This is one of the most complex parts of the karst plateau typified by continuous karst pyramids, karst cones, slopes and karst walls. At a length of 7 km and 70-90° steep cliffs, this is the most spectacular landscape on the karst plateau. The canyon below the pass is the deepest of its kind in Vietnam. The pass itself can be reached by motorbike, however, it is a dangerous and narrow concrete path.

listings.name: Nhà Há Súng
listings.description: A traditional extended family house, open to visitors.

listings.name: Pho Bang Village
listings.description: A peaceful and calm town that is home of Hoa and Hmong ethnicities. The houses here embrace the traditional architecture of wooden columns and mud walls.

listings.name: Sà Phìn
listings.description: A Hmong village very close to the border, known for its Chinese-style houses with yellow bricks.

listings.name: Pả Vi
listings.description: A hexagonal, wagon-like Hmong “cultural tourism village” geared towards visitors. Among other things, herbal baths are offered.

listings.name: Tràng Hương
listings.description: Village in the Nho Que valley. There are tour boats in the narrow river with turquoise water (round trip 1 hour) as well as kayak rentals.

listings.name: Dong Van market
listings.address: in the centre of Dong Van Old Quarter
listings.description: On sale are local products made by Hmong, Han, Dao, Giay and Tay ethnic people. To reach the market on time they have to leave their homes very early in the morning or even one day earlier. At the market, people in different ethnic groups mingle with people from outside their small village to find their life-partners.

listings.name: Ha Giang Sky Path
listings.description: A 7-km hiking trail, high above the highway, near Ma Pi Leng Pass. It is accessible by stopping at the side of the road, and looks rather like a sidewalk going up the mountainside. Motorbikes are allowed for most of the road, and locals will ride past you if you are hiking. The end of the Sky Path is a gorgeous ~2km hike along a narrow trail cut into the karst cliff walls with stunning views of the landscape, river, and local farms.
